[tools-layers-ui] Asset browser drag handoff via globals _assetDragFile/_assetDragName set at editor.js:2498 and consumed on canvas drop; stale-state hazard.

[input-history-export] Selection/layer model: selectedLayerId, layers[] z-order (end = top), layer fields (id,name,visible,opacity,x,y,scale,rotation,flipH,flipV,brightness,contrast,saturate,hueRotate,rShift,gShift,bShift) are shared by every slice, snapshots, project save/load (editor.js ~2560-2630) and Add image.

[input-history-export] Region tables SHIRT_REGION_DATA/PANTS_REGION_DATA (editor.js:20-58) with the mutable alias named SHIRT_REGIONS used in both modes; placement helpers and addLayer hard-code torso_front/torso_back and throw in Pants mode (editor.js:502, 855, 1328, 1339-1340, 1387, 1869-2272).
[input-history-export] TW=585 TH=559 constants; maskCanvas rebuilt on mode switch; export and preview share paintRegions, drawLayerWithAdjustments, and the destination-in mask.

[input-history-export] Async Image loading (data URL round trips) in addDrawingLayer, eraser commit, and restoreState produces race windows that a synchronous native implementation removes; decide which Electron timing quirks (selection cleared on undo, double snapshots in presets) to keep.
[input-history-export] Single-slot _rgbCache keyed by layer id (editor.js:177-202) is invalidated only by the eraser; any new bitmap-replacing feature must also invalidate or key by bitmap.
[input-history-export] Keyboard handler (editor.js:1775) gates on focused INPUT/SELECT/TEXTAREA and the Keys toggle; Ctrl+Z/Y share that gate.
[input-history-export] main.js: nodeIntegration true, contextIsolation false; no will-download handler (Save As behavior is Electron default); no custom menu/IPC for export.
[input-history-export] Preview vs export divergences to resolve once: bg 'transparent' guard, mask always on in export, smoothing differences, GPU-vs-CPU AA edges.

[regions-modes-details] Region table dependency: the active region dictionary SHIRT_REGIONS is swapped between SHIRT_REGION_DATA and PANTS_REGION_DATA (identical rectangles, different key prefixes torso/rarm/larm vs waist/rleg/lleg). Presets, Fit, addLayer, drag-drop and all detail generators hardcode torso_/rarm_/larm_ keys and break in Pants mode (editor.js:502, 855, 1328, 1339, 1741, 1869-2068, 2272). Port should use a semantic region map (BodyFront, BodyBack, LimbRFront ...) so both modes work.

[regions-modes-details] Undo model: saveUndo pushes a JSON snapshot of the whole editor state (mode, bg color/opacity/image, regionColors, showMask, showGrid, every layer with data-URL pixels) BEFORE each mutation; lib/history.js caps at 30, clears redo on push, does not dedupe. currentFill, fill controls, tool, detail settings, keyboard-toggle state, zoom and selection are NOT in snapshots. Native should snapshot immutable state by reference.

[regions-modes-details] Double-undo bug: preset handler calls saveUndo then delegates via element.click() to Fit/Allover/Fit F+B/Scatter handlers that call saveUndo again (editor.js:1734 plus 1327/1337/1354/1365): 2 entries per click. Keyboard transforms (arrows, [ ], R, +/-) create no undo entries at all.

[regions-modes-details] Selection-dependent mode: region buttons paint fills only when NO layer is selected, otherwise they fit the selected layer. Deselect happens elsewhere (canvas empty click, editor.js:1114, Clear, removeLayer of last). The port must keep this overloaded click or make it explicit.

[regions-modes-details] Shared render pipeline: region fills (paintRegions, editor.js:274-293) use lib/fills.js and connected-component extents; export and preview must call the same painter. Swatches in the region grid use CSS fillToCSS approximations, not the canvas painter.

[regions-modes-details] Keyboard routing: one document.onkeydown; suppressed when focus is on INPUT/SELECT/TEXTAREA (including range sliders and color inputs, which keep focus after use) and when Keys: OFF (which also disables Ctrl+Z/Y). Ctrl+V/B/L/U/O tool keys swallow native Ctrl shortcuts.

[regions-modes-details] Persistence: regionColors are saved and loaded in the project (editor.js:2559, 2615) and may be legacy color strings; mode is saved as currentMode. Fill controls, detail settings and Keys toggle are session-only.

[regions-modes-details] Stale-UI pattern: several handlers call render() without updateUI() (region fit, arrow keys, switchMode), leaving inspector sliders stale; decide to refresh in native (invisible to files).
[regions-modes-details] Random inputs: Scatter uses Math.random (26 layers per click); needs injectable RNG for tests.
[regions-modes-details] Two HTML shells exist: editor.html (live, cyan/magenta, 4.1.0) and legacy shirt_editor.html plus backup/*.html (purple palette, older). Port from editor.html + editor.js only.

[regions-modes-details] Pixel-diff caveat: detail strokes and fill edges differ by up to 3/255 across Electron GPU vs software canvas; native exports will be deterministic, so tolerance must apply to edge AA only.

[wordart-assets-io] Layer factory: pack click, Add image, drop, drag-from-assets, right-click full, and Word Art all create the same layer record (id, name, img, visible, opacity=1, x, y, scale, rotation=0, flipH/V=false, brightness/contrast/saturate=100, hueRotate=0, rShift/gShift/bShift=0). Word Art and right-click build it inline instead of via addLayer; native should centralize while preserving each path's distinct placement math (85% fit centered in torso_front; cover at 0,0; centered at drop point).

[wordart-assets-io] Undo/history: saveUndo() (lib/history.js, depth 30) is called BEFORE every mutation including Word Art add, asset add, Add image. loadProject neither pushes nor clears history. Snapshots (snapshotState/restoreState editor.js:~1400-1470) duplicate the save-project schema (restoreState re-implements nearly the same fields); keep one serializer in native.

[wordart-assets-io] SHIRT_REGIONS.torso_front is the placement anchor for new layers in both modes; variable name is stale in Pants mode (pants region set). Verify PANTS_REGION_DATA.torso_front exists or else addLayer would throw in Pants mode.
[wordart-assets-io] Template constants TW=585, TH=559 used by right-click full-size layers and export.

[wordart-assets-io] Fill descriptors (lib/fills.js, RBX15Fills.fillToCSS/fillKey) are part of the .r15proj contract through regionColors; must stay schema-identical for cross-version file compat. currentFill (active fill style) is NOT saved.
[wordart-assets-io] Layer rotation units are degrees in the file and layer model; Canvas translates via rotation*PI/180.

[wordart-assets-io] Canvas rasterization differences: Electron GPU canvas vs software differ by up to 3 levels at AA edges; Word Art output (shadow/neon blur, text AA) cannot be bit-exact vs the Electron goldens, so the harness needs an edge-AA tolerance mask as established in the spike.

[wordart-assets-io] Fonts: Word Art depends on 15 Google Fonts loaded from the network (editor.html:9-11) at weight 900 with faux bold on single-weight faces; native must bundle licensed font files (all are OFL) and decide on faux-bold parity. The packs/word_art PNGs were produced by this generator and are good golden fixtures.

[wordart-assets-io] MSIX packaging: packs must be Content payload (current electron-builder extraResources filter **/*.png excludes packs/README.md); same Store identity and appId com.626labs.rbx15maker concerns belong to the packaging slice.

[wordart-assets-io] Global module state shared with other slices: layers, selectedLayerId, nextId, history, zoom, currentMode, bgColor/bgOpacity/bgImage, regionColors, showMask/showGrid, currentTool (setTool('select') after every add), _assetDragFile/_assetDragName (cross-handler hidden coupling between asset-browser dragstart and canvas.ondrop at editor.js:962-985).
[wordart-assets-io] User-visible blocking alert() dialogs used for all errors; no toast system in this slice.

[wordart-assets-io] Docs drift to fix: packs/README.md claims 'back' drip variants (none exist); project version '4.0' vs app 4.1.0; docs/SMOKE_TEST.md:91 references the .r15proj download flow which becomes a Save dialog.

[ui-surface] Layer array order is z-order (last = top). The panel list renders reversed; Up/Down/drag-reorder/dupe-insert semantics all depend on that. Layer objects share Image instances across clones (Allover/Scatter/F+B/Dupe), so eraser replaces only the selected layer's img reference (clones unaffected) and the RGB-shift cache is single-entry keyed by layer id.

[ui-surface] Whole-editor snapshot undo (30 deep): mode, bg, bg image, regionColors, mask/grid flags, layers incl. image data. Many mutations skip saveUndo (drag/wheel/keys/inspector sliders/flip/move/center/adjustments/hide). Port must keep or consciously change the push list (see file-undo-snapshot-scope).

[ui-surface] updateUI() fully rebuilds the layer list and inspector (collapsing the adjustments panel, resetting focus). Native port should data-bind but preserve the observable side effects: adjustments section collapse on rebuild is a quirk, inspector X/Y not live during drags, brightness/contrast/saturation 0 displayed as 100.

[ui-surface] SHIRT_REGIONS global is swapped on mode change and read by: mask, grid, paintRegions, region grid, placement, presets, detail generators, word art, addLayer. Pants-mode key mismatch (bug-pants-mode-region-keys) cuts across this surface and the Placement/Details/Text slices.

[ui-surface] currentFill (type,c1,c2,angle,scale) and fillKey identity drive live-edit grouping and tile previews; lib/fills.js fillToCSS (tile previews) and paintRegionFill (canvas) must be ported together; connectedRegionGroups(tol 4) and union extents decide gradient spans (editor.js:239-293).

[ui-surface] Tool state machine: setTool resets cursor; layer selection/adding/detail/wordart force Select; draw tools produce layers via autocrop(pad 10). Eraser cursor and 50% preview alpha are tool-specific render hooks.

[ui-surface] Fonts: UI fonts (Inter, Space Grotesk, JetBrains Mono) and 15 word-art fonts are runtime-network today; port must bundle all and drop the Google Fonts preconnect/@import (also an offline and privacy improvement; update docs/PRIVACY.md accordingly).

[ui-surface] Rendering determinism: spike shows Skia matches Electron except AA edges (max 3/255 vs software canvas; GPU canvas adds more). Parity checks for canvas/export items should use shared pixel-diff harness with an edge-tolerance mask.

[ui-surface] No persistence layer exists (no localStorage/settings/recent files/window state). Any native persistence (window bounds, recent files, shortcuts toggle) is new scope and should be an explicit decision.

[ui-surface] Electron-specific coupling to remove: nodeIntegration:true + require('fs'/'path') in the renderer (packs loader), HTML file inputs and anchor downloads, alert/confirm blocking dialogs, webkitdirectory. Packs ship as extraResources (packs/drips ~156 images with word_art pack) and must be packaged as MSIX content.

[ui-surface] Version/branding strings: header 'ItsjustEste | v4.1', title 'RBX15 Classic Shirt and Pants Maker', footer 'Developed at 626 Labs LLC', project file 'version' literal '4.0'; keep Store identity and MSIX manifest values in lockstep.

[shell-ship] Store identity is a hard invariant: Name 626LabsLLC.RBX15ClassicShirtandPantsMaker, Publisher CN=177BCE59-0966-4975-9962-10E36652141F, PublisherDisplayName '626Labs LLC' (no space), Application Id RBXMaker, PFN ..._wz1chhb2h2v4a, Store ID 9MV9G4XFJ8S0. Any change breaks the in-place upgrade; the native version must be strictly greater than 4.1.0.0.

[shell-ship] Network surface goes from 2 hosts (fonts.googleapis.com, fonts.gstatic.com) to zero only if all 15 fonts are bundled. That one change must be mirrored in five documents (PRIVACY.md, SECURITY.md, TEST_PLAN section 14, reviewer letter, README/index.html) and in the Partner Center privacy answers and the runFullTrust justification text, which currently describes Electron.

[shell-ship] Single source of truth for the template geometry: SHIRT_REGIONS in editor.js is duplicated in roblox_shirt_maker.py and variation_generator.py (18 regions, 585x559); the native app should expose one table and a unit test should assert it equals the legacy copies and the pants table.

[shell-ship] Version is derived in three places: package.json (build + MSIX via make-msix.ps1, release workflow tag), .626labs/manifest.json, and the header text 'v4.1' in editor.html; TEST_PLAN/index.html still say v4.0. The native build needs one version source feeding csproj, MSIX manifest, About text, manifest.json, and the release tag check.

[shell-ship] Several release-time artifacts are hardcoded to Electron naming: 'RBX15 Classic Shirt and Pants Maker Setup <ver>.exe' (electron-builder default artifact name) in windows-release.yml, 'RBX15-Maker-v<ver>.0.msix' in make-msix.ps1 and the workflow, and Executable='RBX15 Classic Shirt and Pants Maker.exe' in the manifest. Change one without the others and fail_on_unmatched_files or Store validation fails.

[shell-ship] Download/Save semantics are implicit in Chromium (Save As dialog from anchor-download, filename sanitization regex, blob URL revoke). Every file-producing action (Export PNG, Save Work) in the editor slice shares the same sanitizer and dialog contract defined here; implement once as a service.

[shell-ship] Ctrl-key handling interacts with Electron's default menu accelerators (Ctrl+R reload, Ctrl+Shift+I, zoom, F11) that main.js never removes; the editor slice's keyboard map (README Controls table, Ctrl+D/Z/Y/Shift+Z) must be implemented as WPF InputBindings/PreviewKeyDown, and the port must choose which Electron-only accelerators to drop (reload especially).

[shell-ship] No state persists between launches and none should be added without privacy updates; undo history (cap 30) and the dirty/clean notion are in-memory only, and no close-confirmation exists, so any unsaved-changes prompt is a new feature rather than parity.

[shell-ship] Test suite maps cleanly to the port's pure-logic layer: fills (14), erase (5), history (7) are ports; injection (3) and smoke parse (2) are replaced by behavioral and compile-time gates. CI path filter bug (lib/** and tests/** not in windows-ci triggers) must not be reproduced.

[shell-ship] Repo hygiene decisions needed before the native cutover: remove roblox_uploader.py (credential extraction in a public repo, contradicts the certification letter), archive 143 legacy PNGs (about 17 MB incl. possibly third-party art), the v3 monolith and its two identical backups, the stray root PNGs and create_shortcut.ps1 (leaks a local path), and the unused pants_manifest.json.

[gap:claims] Ctrl/Meta key ownership: editor.js:1803-1806 hands every Ctrl combo to the Electron shell's hidden default menu. The native KeyBinding table must decide each of Ctrl+R, Ctrl+Shift+I, Ctrl+=/-/0 and F11 explicitly, or behavior silently changes, including the Ctrl+R data-loss path.

[gap:claims] Claims versus reality has to be settled per release doc: PRIVACY.md, SECURITY.md, the reviewer letter, the store listing (store-listing-console/apps/rbx15/copy/listing-copy.md), docs/index.html, README, TEST_PLAN and SMOKE_TEST all state Electron-era facts (Electron packaged as MSIX, Node/npm build, Google Fonts request, DevTools via Ctrl+Shift+I, region color picker, v4.0 header). Every one needs a rewrite pass tied to the port's ship, not after it.

[gap:claims] The network-zero promise depends on three things together: bundling all 18 fonts (15 Word Art + 3 UI from styles.css:6), restricting .r15proj image fields to data: URIs, and keeping no internetClient capability in the MSIX manifest.

[gap:claims] .r15proj forward/backward compatibility: any optional field added (for example the template title) must be ignorable by 4.1.0 Electron, and the native reader must accept every v3/v4/v4.1 file that only contains data: URIs.
[gap:claims] Two install channels (Store MSIX and GitHub NSIS) share a display name. Port planning must cover migration for both, not only the Store update path (parity-store-update-path).

[gap:code-sweep] Every undo snapshot serializes all layer images as data URLs (JSON.stringify), and restore re-decodes them async. The race, empty steps and lost selection all stem from this. A C# snapshot holding immutable SKImage references fixes several items at once (undo-rapid-restore-race, project-load-error-path-bugs).

[gap:code-sweep] Keyboard gating (editor.js:1777) couples to WPF focus semantics: which controls count as 'text input' decides whether sliders and checkboxes swallow the shortcuts. Decide this once for the whole app.

[gap:code-sweep] updateUI() rebuilds the layer list and property panel wholesale and is called from drag/wheel/key paths. Any parity spec about panel state (expander open, focus) depends on the port choosing binding over rebuild.

[gap:code-sweep] Async image decode via FileReader and Image.onload is everywhere (drop, add, asset click, word art, detail, erase, load, undo). The port should centralize decoding (SKCodec) and define a deterministic add order.

[gap:code-sweep] Several actions call other buttons' .click() (presets → Fit Front/F+B/Allover/Scatter; Ctrl+Z → btnUndo). The port should call commands directly, which also removes the double undo step. Decide whether to keep the step count.
[gap:code-sweep] Decisions needed before spec: Ctrl+O/Ctrl+S mapping, SVG support, close-without-save prompt, zoom pan/scroll, clear history on project open, no-op undo suppression.

rows.name: Ribbon tab switching
rows.behavior: Every .ribbon-tab gets a click handler: reads data-tab, removes 'active' from all tabs and all .ribbon-pane, adds 'active' to the clicked tab and to the .ribbon-pane whose data-tab matches. Missing pane is silently ignored (tab still highlights, no pane shown). Click only: no keyboard/arrow navigation, no ARIA roles, no persistence of last tab; initial active tab comes from editor.html markup.
rows.quirks: Handlers bind once at load; panes added later would not get handlers. Unmatched data-tab leaves no pane visible.
rows.portTarget: WPF TabControl styled as ribbon (or custom RadioButton strip + ContentControl bound to selected tab). Panes as TabItems with Visibility toggled by selection.
rows.parityCheck: Click each tab: exactly one tab and one pane active; initial tab matches editor.html default. Decide whether to add keyboard nav (native TabControl gives it free).

rows.name: Template canvas size 585x559
rows.behavior: TW=585, TH=559 are fixed logical template dimensions (Roblox R15 clothing template). The offscreen composite, mask, bg image draw and export all use these. Visible canvas is TW*zoom by TH*zoom.
rows.quirks: Zoom is applied by resizing the canvas element, not CSS scaling.
rows.portTarget: const int TemplateWidth=585, TemplateHeight=559; SKBitmap/SKSurface at that size for composite.
rows.parityCheck: Export PNG is 585x559; hit-test and region coordinates match reference pixel-for-pixel.

rows.name: Shirt region table (18 regions)
rows.behavior: SHIRT_REGION_DATA: torso_up(231,8,128x64), torso_right(165,74,64x128), torso_front(231,74,128x128), torso_left(361,74,64x128), torso_back(427,74,128x128), torso_down(231,204,128x64), rarm_up(217,289,64x64), rarm_left(19,355,64x128), rarm_back(85,355), rarm_right(151,355), rarm_front(217,355) all 64x128, rarm_down(217,485,64x64), larm_up(308,289,64x64), larm_front(308,355), larm_left(374,355), larm_back(440,355), larm_right(506,355) all 64x128, larm_down(308,485,64x64). Object key order is the iteration order for mask, grid and fills.
rows.quirks: Region name keys are persisted in saved projects (regionColors), so names must be kept verbatim for v4 file compat.
rows.portTarget: static readonly OrderedDictionary / ImmutableArray<(string Name, SKRectI Rect)> in a Template class; preserve key order.
rows.parityCheck: Unit test asserting all 18 names and rects equal the JS table; golden mask PNG diff.

rows.name: Pants region table (18 regions)
rows.behavior: PANTS_REGION_DATA has identical geometry to shirt but names waist_* in place of torso_* and rleg_*/lleg_* in place of rarm_*/larm_*. Same coordinates per slot (waist_up 231,8 etc.).
rows.quirks: Geometry is duplicated in source; the port can derive one from the other but must keep names exact.
rows.portTarget: Second static table keyed by TemplateMode; share geometry array, differ only by name.
rows.parityCheck: Unit test: for each index, rect equals shirt rect at same index; names match.

rows.name: Active region reference and mode variable
rows.behavior: SHIRT_REGIONS is a mutable shallow copy of SHIRT_REGION_DATA, reassigned on mode change (switchMode at line ~1696-1714 swaps to PANTS_REGION_DATA copy, clears regionColors, rebuilds mask). currentMode is 'Shirt' or 'Pants', default 'Shirt'. The variable name SHIRT_REGIONS is misleading in Pants mode.
rows.quirks: Cross-slice: mode switch resets regionColors to {} (line 1711), so fills do not carry over.
rows.portTarget: Template.ActiveRegions property recomputed on mode set; raise event so mask cache invalidates.
rows.parityCheck: Toggle mode: mask, grid, fills use new table; regionColors emptied; mask rebuilt.

rows.name: Initial editor state defaults
rows.behavior: layers=[], selectedLayerId=null, bgColor '#192e44', bgImage null, bgOpacity 1, zoom 1, showMask true, showGrid false, currentTool 'select', drawColor '#17d4fa', drawSize 4, drawFill false, isDrawing false, drag state zeroed, history = RBX15History.createHistory(30) (30-step undo depth), nextId starts at 1 (declared line 499, used by makeLayer).
rows.quirks: Undo cap 30 is a user-visible limit. nextId is declared with let after makeLayer text but initialized before any call; port must init IDs at 1.
rows.portTarget: EditorState view-model (INotifyPropertyChanged) with these defaults; History<T> capped at 30.
rows.parityCheck: Fresh launch screenshot and settings dump match defaults; undo depth is exactly 30.

rows.name: Background color swatch palette
rows.behavior: BG_COLORS lists 12 swatches in order: Navy #192e44, Navy Deep #0f1f31, Black #050c18, Charcoal #2d2d2d, Wine #4a1942, Forest #1b4332, Ocean #0c2461, Storm #2c3e50, White #f5f5f5, Red #b71c1c, Magenta #f22f89, Cyan #17d4fa. Default bgColor is Navy.
rows.quirks: Swatch UI built outside this slice; confirm tooltip uses name.
rows.portTarget: ItemsControl of swatch buttons bound to a static list; names as tooltips.
rows.parityCheck: Swatch order, names and hex values match; clicking sets bgColor.

rows.name: Region mask canvas
rows.behavior: buildMask creates a TWxTH canvas, clears it, fills every active region rect white. Result is used with destination-in to clip the composite to template regions (transparent in gutters and unused areas). Built at load and rebuilt on mode change.
rows.quirks: Rects are integer so no AA. Mask only applies when showMask is true.
rows.portTarget: SKBitmap Alpha8 or SKRegion of the union of rects; draw with SKBlendMode.DstIn. Cache and rebuild on mode change.
rows.parityCheck: Mask PNG pixel-equal to JS; composite with mask gutters fully transparent (alpha 0) and edges hard (integer rects, no AA).

rows.name: makeLayer factory defaults
rows.behavior: makeLayer(img,name,x,y,scale,overrides): id=nextId++, name default 'Layer', img, visible true, opacity 1, x||0, y||0, scale||1 (so scale 0 becomes 1), rotation 0, flipH false, flipV false, brightness 100, contrast 100, saturate 100, hueRotate 0, rShift 0, gShift 0, bShift 0; overrides merged last via Object.assign and can replace any field including id.
rows.quirks: Falsy-coalesce on x,y,scale,name: scale 0 or empty name silently defaulted. IDs are session-monotonic and rebased on project load (line 1465, 2663).
rows.portTarget: Layer class with these default property values and a Create factory; overrides as an object initializer/record with-expression.
rows.parityCheck: Unit test default field values; scale 0 coerces to 1; id increments monotonically.

rows.name: Layer field schema and persistence shape
rows.behavior: Layer fields: id,name,img,visible,opacity(0-1),x,y,scale,rotation(deg),flipH,flipV,brightness(%),contrast(%),saturate(%),hueRotate(deg),rShift,gShift,bShift(-255..255 additive). v4 project files serialize these; v4 reader must tolerate missing newer fields by defaulting.
rows.quirks: Slider ranges live outside this slice (check lines for UI); rShift/gShift/bShift semantic is additive, clamped 0-255.
rows.portTarget: System.Text.Json DTO with defaults matching makeLayer; image as base64 PNG decoded to SKBitmap.
rows.parityCheck: Open a v4 .json from Electron build: all layers load with identical transforms; round-trip save then reopen in Electron.

rows.name: autocrop of drawn canvas
rows.behavior: autocrop(canvas,pad=10): scans every pixel; alpha>0 expands bounding box; if none returns null; expands box by pad (default 10, pad||10 so 0 becomes 10), clamps to canvas bounds, crops via drawImage; returns {canvas,x,y} where x,y are crop origin in source space. Used when committing pen/shape/eraser drawings into a layer (line 533).
rows.quirks: pad 0 cannot be requested. Threshold is alpha>0 so near-invisible antialias pixels count.
rows.portTarget: SKBitmap scan over pixel span (alpha > 0), SKBitmap.ExtractSubset or SKCanvas.DrawBitmap(src,srcRect,dstRect).
rows.parityCheck: Draw a single dot: layer bounds equal dot bbox +10px clamped; fully empty stroke returns null and creates no layer.

rows.name: RGB channel shift (pixel operation)
rows.behavior: applyRGBShift copies layer.img to a temp canvas, reads RGBA, for each pixel with alpha != 0 adds rShift/gShift/bShift to R/G/B and clamps 0-255; fully transparent pixels skipped; alpha untouched; writes back. Result is non-premultiplied per getImageData semantics. Source dims preserved (img.width/height).
rows.quirks: Browser canvas stores premultiplied, so getImageData on low-alpha pixels is lossy; JS result inherits that loss. Port must decide: replicate by premul-then-unpremul round trip, or accept tiny diffs on low-alpha pixels.
rows.portTarget: Convert SKBitmap to unpremul, per-pixel add/clamp over Span<byte>, then draw. Use SKAlphaType.Unpremul to avoid premultiplication rounding drift.
rows.parityCheck: Pixel diff of a layer with semi-transparent pixels and shifts (+50,-30,+255): exact match. Test alpha 1..254 pixels specifically since canvas premultiplied storage quantizes.
rows.divergence: 4.1: RGB shift runs on browser-premultiplied getImageData, losing precision on low-alpha pixels. v5: RGB shift runs on unpremultiplied pixels (approved decision), so low-alpha pixels are more precise.

rows.name: RGB shift single-entry cache
rows.behavior: _rgbCache holds one entry {layerId,r,g,b,canvas}. Cache hit only if layer id and all three shifts equal the cached ones; any miss recomputes and replaces. Cache is single-slot, so two layers with shifts alternate-thrash every frame. Cache is invalidated externally by setting _rgbCache.layerId=null (line 1279) when the layer pixels change.
rows.quirks: Staleness bug risk: cache keys do not include image content; only the explicit invalidation at 1279 protects it. Eraser/draw edits to a shifted layer elsewhere may show stale shifted pixels. Port with per-layer invalidation to fix. Also layer rename/flip/scale don't need invalidation.
rows.portTarget: Per-layer cached SKBitmap keyed by (r,g,b) with invalidation on pixel edit; can improve to per-layer cache (behavior-neutral).
rows.parityCheck: Output identical regardless of cache; verify stale-cache case: edit pixels (eraser, adjustments) then shift renders new pixels, not old.
rows.divergence: 4.1: single-slot cache keyed only on layer id and shifts can show stale shifted pixels after eraser or draw edits and thrashes with two shifted layers. v5: per-layer cache invalidated on any pixel edit (clearly unintended staleness bug).

rows.name: hasAdjustments predicate
rows.behavior: True if brightness!=100 or contrast!=100 or saturate!=100 or hueRotate!=0 or any of rShift,gShift,bShift!=0. Note it is true for RGB-shift-only layers, which then also sets ctx.filter to the identity-valued filter string.
rows.quirks: Identity CSS filter (100%,100%,100%,0deg) may still route through a filter pipeline in Chromium (rounding/GPU path differences possible); native path skips it.
rows.portTarget: Layer.HasAdjustments property; skip SKColorFilter creation when false.
rows.parityCheck: Unit test truth table; identity filter produces identical pixels to no filter.

rows.name: CSS ctx.filter brightness/contrast/saturate/hue-rotate
rows.behavior: When hasAdjustments, ctx.filter='brightness(B%) contrast(C%) saturate(S%) hue-rotate(Hdeg)' applied in that fixed order for the subsequent drawImage; reset to 'none' after draw. Numbers interpolated raw (no clamp here; UI sliders bound them). Filter applies to the transformed draw (rotated/flipped) in local space; filter operates on the source before opacity (globalAlpha) compositing.
rows.quirks: Each filter function clamps to [0,1] after its stage in Chromium; a single multiplied matrix does not. Use per-stage compose. Edge AA of filtered rotated images differs between GPU and software canvas (noted 3/255 diffs).
rows.portTarget: Compose SKColorFilter.CreateColorMatrix in order: brightness (scale RGB by b), contrast (c*x + (1-c)/2 offset 0.5*(1-c)), saturate (Filter Effects saturate matrix, luma 0.2126/0.7152/0.0722), hue-rotate (Filter Effects hue matrix). Multiply matrices in the JS order; apply via SKPaint.ColorFilter on DrawBitmap. Clamp between stages per CSS (each filter function clamps). Alternatively chain SKColorFilter.CreateCompose per stage to preserve inter-stage clamping.
rows.parityCheck: Pixel diff over a gradient test image for sliders at extremes (brightness 0/200, contrast 0/200, saturate 0/300, hue 90/180/359) and combos; tolerate <=1 level. Compare against Electron with GPU canvas off. Confirm inter-stage clamping by testing brightness 200 then contrast 50.

rows.name: RGB shift applied before CSS filter
rows.behavior: If any shift nonzero the drawn source is the cached shifted canvas; otherwise layer.img. The CSS filter (brightness...) is then applied on top of the shifted pixels. So order: RGB shift then brightness, contrast, saturate, hue-rotate.
rows.quirks: Order is fixed and non-commutative; port must keep.
rows.portTarget: Pipeline: shifted bitmap (or original) -> DrawBitmap with ColorFilter chain.
rows.parityCheck: Test layer with both shift and brightness: result equals shift-then-filter, not reverse.

rows.name: Layer draw transform and opacity
rows.behavior: drawLayerWithAdjustments: save; globalAlpha=layer.opacity; center = (x + imgW*scale/2, y + imgH*scale/2) in template space; translate to center; rotate(rotation deg); flipH -> scale(-1,1); flipV -> scale(1,-1); draw image at (-w/2,-h/2,w,h) with w=imgW*scale, h=imgH*scale; restore. Rotation happens before flip so flips are in the rotated frame. x,y is the unrotated top-left, so rotation pivots about the box center.
rows.quirks: Offscreen ctx imageSmoothingEnabled left at default true (only the visible ctx is changed by zoom). Downscale below 0.5 uses Chromium's smoothing path, may differ from Skia bilinear; check heavily downscaled layers.
rows.portTarget: SKCanvas.Save; Translate; RotateDegrees; Scale(±1,±1); DrawBitmap(bmp, SKRect(-w/2,-h/2,w/2,h/2), paint with Alpha=opacity, filter quality = bilinear/low sampling matching Chromium); Restore.
rows.parityCheck: Pixel diff layers at scale 0.5/1/2.37, rotation 0/17/90/-33, flips combos, opacity 0.5; interior exact, edge AA within tolerance. Sampling mode must match Chromium default (bilinear, no mipmap) with SKSamplingOptions(SKFilterMode.Linear).

rows.name: Layer visibility and null image skip
rows.behavior: Layers iterate in array order (index 0 bottom, last on top); skipped if !visible or !img. Layer opacity applied per layer; no per-layer blend modes (always source-over).
rows.quirks: Selected-but-hidden layer still draws selection handles (selection block does not check visible).
rows.portTarget: foreach over ObservableCollection<Layer> in order; skip hidden.
rows.parityCheck: Reorder layers and toggle visibility: composite matches Electron.

rows.name: Fill normalization and legacy string fills
rows.behavior: normalizeFill: falsy -> {type:'solid',c1:'#000000'}; string -> {type:'solid',c1:string}; object returned as is. Legacy v4.0 saved projects store region colors as plain color strings, so they load as solids. TYPES list: solid, linear, radial, stripes, checker, dots, camo.
rows.quirks: Unknown type falls through to solid in paint but fillToCSS also defaults to c1. Object missing type is not normalized (type undefined -> solid via else branch).
rows.portTarget: FillDescriptor record with JsonConverter accepting string or object; enum FillType in that order.
rows.parityCheck: Load project with string regionColors and with object descriptors; both render identical to Electron.

rows.name: Hex color parse and mix helpers
rows.behavior: hexToRgb accepts #rgb (expanded) or #rrggbb, undefined -> #000000; parseInt(h,16) with no validation (bad strings -> NaN -> bitwise 0 -> black; 8-digit hex reads the low 24 bits of the large number via >> so produces shifted channels). rgbToHex rounds, clamps 0-255, lowercase two-digit. mix(a,b,t) linear interpolates per channel in sRGB space with rounding.
rows.quirks: JS Math.round(2.5)=3, Math.round(-0.5)=-0 and .NET banker's rounding differ; use floor(v+0.5). Only #rgb/#rrggbb inputs expected from color pickers.
rows.portTarget: static class ColorUtil with identical rounding (Math.Round away-from-zero vs JS Math.round half-up toward +inf: use Math.Floor(v+0.5)).
rows.parityCheck: Unit tests for mix at t=0.5 on odd channel sums (e.g. 0 and 1) to confirm .5 rounds up; camo tone parity.

rows.name: mulberry32 PRNG and FNV-1a seed
rows.behavior: seeded(seed): mulberry32 with s=(s+0x6D2B79F5)>>>0; t=imul(s^(s>>>15),1|s); t=(t+imul(t^(t>>>7),61|t))^t; return ((t^(t>>>14))>>>0)/4294967296. seedFrom(str): FNV-1a 32-bit with offset 2166136261, prime 16777619, over charCodeAt (UTF-16 units). Camo seed string is c1+c2+scale+'_'+gx+'_'+gy where scale is the number (JS number-to-string, e.g. '16', '2.5') and gx,gy are integers possibly negative ('-1').
rows.quirks: Seed uses raw c1/c2 strings, not normalized hex: case differences change the camo pattern. c2 default '#ffffff' used when missing, but the seed string uses f.c1/f.c2 (not the defaulted c1/c2 locals? it uses c1,c2 locals which are defaulted) so confirm defaults flow in.
rows.portTarget: uint arithmetic in unchecked C#; build seed string with invariant culture and JS-style number formatting for scale (double.ToString("R", Invariant)); c1/c2 strings used verbatim including case (so '#FF0000' vs '#ff0000' seed differently).
rows.parityCheck: Golden test vectors: first 10 outputs for several seeds equal JS; camo render pixel-diff equals (spike already proved).

rows.name: Fill parameter defaults and clamps
rows.behavior: c1 default '#000000', c2 default '#ffffff', scale = max(2, f.scale||16) (so 0/undefined -> 16, 1 -> 2, negative -> 2), angle = (f.angle||0) degrees converted to radians. Each paint: ctx.save, clip to region rect, draw, restore.
rows.quirks: f.scale||16 means explicit scale 0 becomes 16 but scale 1 becomes 2.
rows.portTarget: Same defaults in FillDescriptor accessors; SKCanvas.Save, ClipRect(rect, antialias:false), Restore.
rows.parityCheck: Scale 0, 1, 2, 3, 200 render same as JS; clip edges pixel-exact (integer rects).

rows.name: Solid fill
rows.behavior: fillRect(region) with c1. Also the fallback for unknown types.
rows.quirks: Unknown or missing type renders as solid c1.
rows.portTarget: canvas.DrawRect with SKPaint Color, antialias off.
rows.parityCheck: Exact pixel match.

rows.name: Linear gradient fill
rows.behavior: Center of extent; dx=cos(angle)*ext.w/2, dy=sin(angle)*ext.h/2 (so gradient vector is scaled per-axis by extent w and h, not a true length-preserving CSS angle); createLinearGradient from (cx-dx,cy-dy) to (cx+dx,cy+dy); stops 0=c1, 1=c2; fillRect region. Angle 0 = left-to-right c1 to c2; 90 = top-to-bottom. Colors interpolated in non-linear sRGB (canvas default), premultiplied.
rows.quirks: Non-uniform axis scaling means 45 degrees on a 128x64 extent is not a true 45-degree ramp. Keep for parity.
rows.portTarget: SKShader.CreateLinearGradient(p0,p1,[c1,c2],null,SKShaderTileMode.Clamp) with sRGB non-linear interpolation (default Skia). Use unpremul interpolation flag consistently since opaque colors.
rows.parityCheck: Spike showed exact match; keep as regression: angle 0/45/90/135/270, with grouped extent across torso.

rows.name: Radial gradient fill
rows.behavior: Center of extent, inner radius 0, outer radius max(ext.w, ext.h)/2, stops c1 at center to c2 at edge; angle ignored; areas outside radius extend c2 (canvas pad behavior).
rows.quirks: Angle control has no effect for radial.
rows.portTarget: SKShader.CreateRadialGradient(center, radius, colors, null, Clamp).
rows.parityCheck: Pixel diff on grouped torso and single arm region.

rows.name: Stripes fill (global lattice)
rows.behavior: Fills region with c1; rotates the context by angle about canvas origin (0,0) (not region center); period=scale*2; R=ceil(1000/period)*period; for i from -R while i<R step period: fillRect(i,-R,scale,R*2) in c2. Stripes thus anchor to global origin so adjacent regions line up. Rotation of the clip: clip was set before rotate so region rect stays axis-aligned.
rows.quirks: Stripe coverage limited to +-R (~1000 px) rotated, fine for 585x559. Rotation about origin means visual phase changes strongly with angle. Rotated edge AA differs by GPU vs software canvas.
rows.portTarget: Clip then canvas.RotateRadians(angle); loop DrawRect with antialias ON for rotated edges (Chromium AA on rotated fillRect), antialias semantic for angle 0 integer-aligned stripes is exact.
rows.parityCheck: Pixel diff angle 0 (exact), 45 and 30 (edge AA diffs allowed), scale 2/16/37; verify phase continuity across torso faces.

rows.name: Checker fill
rows.behavior: Fills c1; cells of size scale on the global grid; for gy in [floor(y/scale), ceil((y+h)/scale)), gx likewise: if ((gx+gy)&1)===0 fill c2 square at (gx*scale, gy*scale, scale, scale). Parity from absolute index, so c2 sits on even cells and cell (0,0) is c2. Negative index parity: &1 on negative ints works as two's complement.
rows.quirks: Fractional scale (UI may allow) produces AA seams; scale min 2.
rows.portTarget: Same loops in C#; (gx+gy)&1 identical for ints. Fractional scale: use antialias ON and float rects.
rows.parityCheck: Exact pixel match at integer scales; fractional scale edge tolerance.

rows.name: Dots fill
rows.behavior: Fills c1; radius r=scale*0.3; loops gy from floor(y/scale) through ceil((y+h)/scale) INCLUSIVE and gx likewise (note <= unlike checker); for each draws a full arc at center (gx*scale+scale/2, gy*scale+scale/2) in c2 via beginPath/arc/fill (one path per dot). Dots straddling region seams are clipped by the region clip, continuing across seams.
rows.quirks: Inclusive bounds draw extra off-region dots that are fully clipped; harmless but keeps cost.
rows.portTarget: DrawCircle per dot with antialiased paint; keep <= bounds to cover partially visible dots.
rows.parityCheck: Pixel diff; spike confirmed. Check arcs at region edges.

rows.name: Camo fill (seeded blobs on global cells)
rows.behavior: tones=[c1,c2,mix(c1,c2,0.5),mix(c1,#000000,0.35)]; base fill tones[0]. cell=scale*2; cell range gx0=floor(x/cell)-1 to gx1=ceil((x+w)/cell)+1 exclusive. Per cell: rand=seeded(seedFrom(c1+c2+scale+'_'+gx+'_'+gy)); for b in 0..1: color tones[1+((gx+gy+b)%3)] (JS % on negative gives negative result: gx+gy+b negative yields -1 or -2 -> tones[0] or tones[-1]=undefined); blob center bx=(gx+rand())*cell, by=(gy+rand())*cell, br=scale*(0.6+rand()*1.1); four sub-circles: ox=(rand()-0.5)*br, oy=(rand()-0.5)*br; moveTo(bx+ox+br,by+oy); arc(bx+ox,by+oy,br*(0.6+rand()*0.4),0,2PI); single fill of all four per blob. RNG call order is: bx rand, by rand, br rand, then per k: ox, oy, radius rand.
rows.quirks: Negative gx+gy (cells at index -1) makes (gx+gy+b)%3 negative; tones[1+neg] can be tones[0] (c1) or tones[-1]===undefined: ctx.fillStyle=undefined is ignored in canvas so the PREVIOUS fillStyle (prior blob/base) is retained. Port must replicate: if index out of range keep previous color. Edge-case only in off-template cells (gx=-1,gy>=0 with sum -1 or gy=-1): cells with x<cell near left edge of template (x=19 region rarm_left gx0 = floor(19/32)-1=-1) so IT IS REACHED for left-edge regions with default scale 16. Most blobs there are clipped but those overlapping region matter.
rows.portTarget: SKPath with AddCircle-equivalent arcs (moveTo then arcTo full circle) filled nonzero; reproduce exact RNG consumption order; implement JS % semantics (C# % matches sign-of-dividend like JS for ints) and replicate undefined-tone behavior.
rows.parityCheck: Spike showed no pixel differences except AA edges; keep golden diff for several seeds, scales 8/16/40, and cells with negative indices (gx or gy < 0 only occurs when extent near origin: gx0=-1 for x<cell).

rows.name: fillToCSS swatch approximation
rows.behavior: CSS strings for region button swatches: linear -> linear-gradient(angle deg, c1, c2); radial -> radial-gradient(circle,c1,c2); stripes -> repeating-linear-gradient(angle, c1 0..scale px, c2 scale..2*scale); checker -> repeating-conic-gradient(c1 0% 25%, c2 0% 50%) sized 2*scale; dots -> radial-gradient(c2 30%, transparent 32%) sized scale over c1; camo -> linear-gradient(135deg, mix(c1,c2,.5), c1 60%, c2); solid -> c1. Explicitly an approximation, not source of truth.
rows.quirks: Swatches deliberately differ from canvas (e.g. CSS angle convention differs: CSS 0deg is bottom-to-top, canvas 0 is left-to-right), so the swatch can show a gradient direction inconsistent with the render. Decide to fix by rendering thumbnails from the real painter.
rows.portTarget: Region button swatch: render a small SKBitmap thumbnail via the real paintRegionFill (better and simpler than CSS) or WPF Brush equivalents (LinearGradientBrush, RadialGradientBrush, DrawingBrush tile).
rows.parityCheck: Reworded in M4b to the fixed behavior: the swatch is the canvas painter's pixels for the region at thumbnail size for each of the 7 types (RegionsGroupTests.Swatch_is_the_canvas_painter_cropped_to_the_region), and gradients and stripes follow the canvas angle convention (A_zero_degree_gradient_swatch_runs_left_to_right, A_zero_degree_stripes_swatch_runs_left_to_right, A_ninety_degree_stripes_swatch_runs_top_to_bottom).
rows.divergence: 4.1: swatch gradients use the CSS angle convention (0deg is bottom-to-top) so direction can contradict the canvas render (0 is left-to-right). v5: swatches are drawn with the canvas angle convention so they match the render (clearly unintended inconsistency). Each swatch is the region painted by the canvas painter with the region as its own gradient extent, so a tile shows the full gradient even where the canvas spans a group.

rows.name: fillKey grouping identity
rows.behavior: fillKey = [type, c1||'', c2||'', angle||0, scale||0].join('|'). Two regions share a group only if all five match exactly (string compare, case-sensitive hex). Solid fills with different c1 are separate keys; string legacy fill and equivalent object share key if normalized to same values (type 'solid', c1, '', 0, 0).
rows.quirks: Case differences or irrelevant fields (e.g. angle on solid) split groups; irrelevant for solid but matters for gradients if UI stores differing angle values. Note the key uses f.scale||0 raw while paint uses max(2,scale||16).
rows.portTarget: record struct equality or string key with the same fields; case-sensitive comparer.
rows.parityCheck: Unit: two regions same gradient but '#FF0000' vs '#ff0000' c1 produce separate gradients (not spanning), as in Electron.

rows.name: Module export shape and test dual-loading
rows.behavior: UMD wrapper: exports via module.exports for node tests and window.RBX15Fills for browser; exposes TYPES, normalizeFill, paintRegionFill, fillToCSS, fillKey, mix. Used identically for screen render and PNG export (same call), guaranteeing WYSIWYG.
rows.quirks: The export path lives in another slice but must call the same paintRegions.
rows.portTarget: A single FillPainter class in a shared library used by both the on-screen SkiaElement render and export.
rows.parityCheck: Export and on-screen composite are bit-identical on same machine in native (an improvement over Electron GPU/software variance).
rows.divergence: 4.1: UMD wrapper exposes the fills module to both browser (window.RBX15Fills) and Node tests. v5: not carried, since Fills is a C# engine class and the WYSIWYG guarantee comes from screen and export sharing one render path.

rows.name: unionRect
rows.behavior: Bounding box of a list of rects: min x,y; max x+w, y+h; returns {x,y,w,h}. Empty list would return Infinity values (never called with empty).
rows.quirks: Empty input yields infinities; guard in port.
rows.portTarget: static SKRect Union(IEnumerable<SKRect>).
rows.parityCheck: Unit test with torso group: (165,8)-(555,268).

rows.name: connectedRegionGroups (gradient spans connected faces)
rows.behavior: Connected components over rects where two rects touch if a.x-tol < b.x+b.w && b.x-tol < a.x+a.w && a.y-tol < b.y+b.h && b.y-tol < a.y+a.h with tol default 4 (tol==null check, so 0 allowed). Template gutters ~2px, so torso six faces form one group; rarm 6 faces one group (rarm_left x19..83, back 85.. gap 2); larm another; rarm and larm: rarm_front ends x281 and larm_front starts 308 (gap 27) so separate. Traversal: DFS stack, groups in order of first unseen index; region order within group is DFS pop order.
rows.quirks: Condition effectively inflates on the min side only (a.x - tol < b.right and b.x - tol < a.right), giving a one-sided tolerance of tol per pair test but tested both ways, so overall gap up to <tol bridges (gap 2 bridges, gap 4 does not: strict <). Group order and within-group order only matter for overlap painting and are irrelevant for non-overlapping rects.
rows.portTarget: Same union-find/DFS over rects using the same strict inequalities (note the asymmetric inflate: only a is inflated by tol on left/top, but b is symmetric in the second clause; replicate exactly).
rows.parityCheck: Unit test group membership for shirt and pants tables with a single fill on all regions: expected 3 groups (torso 6, rarm 6, larm 6); with only front/back selected: front(231..359) and back(427) gap 68 -> separate groups.

rows.name: paintRegions: group by fill then by connectivity
rows.behavior: Iterates regionColors entries (insertion order); skips names not in active region table or falsy fills; buckets by fillKey; for each fill bucket, splits rects into connected components; per component extent=unionRect(comp); calls paintRegionFill(target, r, fill, extent) for each r. Different fills never share a gradient extent, even if adjacent. Same fill on distant clusters gets separate extents (arms vs torso). Bucket iteration is by object key insertion order of byFill (string keys, JS orders integer-like keys first, not an issue here).
rows.quirks: regionColors keys not in the active mode (e.g. torso_front after switching to Pants if not cleared) are ignored without error. Fill buckets with non-overlapping rects mean paint order doesn't matter, but overlapping would.
rows.portTarget: RegionPainter.Paint(SKCanvas, regionColors, activeRegions) with same bucketing; use ordered dictionary.
rows.parityCheck: Painted result identical for: all-one-gradient, torso gradient + arm solid, two different gradients adjacent, partial selection of faces. Regions stale from another mode (names absent) are skipped silently.

rows.name: Persistent offscreen composite
rows.behavior: One reusable TWxTH canvas (_offCanvas) cleared (clearRect) every render. Composite order: 1) clearRect, 2) background, 3) region fills, 4) layers bottom-to-top, 5) live drawing preview, 6) mask via destination-in (if showMask). Everything for export-equivalent output lives here.
rows.quirks: Offscreen context is not created with willReadFrequently, so Chromium may use GPU backing; this is the source of the edge differences noted in the spike.
rows.portTarget: Single SKSurface/SKBitmap 585x559 reused; render pipeline function Composite(canvas).
rows.parityCheck: Composite PNG (mask on and off) equals Electron software-canvas output within tolerance.

rows.name: Background image vs color with opacity
rows.behavior: If bgImage: globalAlpha=bgOpacity, drawImage(bgImage,0,0,TW,TH) stretched to template size (aspect ratio NOT preserved), reset alpha to 1. Else: fillStyle=bgColor, globalAlpha=bgOpacity, fillRect(0,0,TW,TH), reset alpha. bgOpacity default 1. With opacity <1 the background is blended over a transparent offscreen (so alpha, not blended with checkerboard until final draw).
rows.quirks: Background image overrides bgColor entirely (color not drawn under image). Image is stretched, not fit or cropped. Clearing the image falls back to color.
rows.portTarget: DrawBitmap(bg, dest rect 0,0,585,559) with SKPaint alpha = bgOpacity and linear sampling; else DrawRect with color alpha.
rows.parityCheck: Load a non-585x559 background image: stretched to fill; bgOpacity 0.3 shows checkerboard through; color and image paths pixel-compared.

rows.name: A new template's background starts transparent
rows.behavior: Startup state sets bgColor '#192e44' and bgOpacity 1, so every new template is navy at 100% and an untouched region exports navy; the Layout tab's opacity slider is the only way to clear it.
rows.portTarget: EditorSession.NewDocument(): 4.1's startup state with BgOpacity 0. The color stays #192e44, so raising the opacity shows 4.1's navy. Opened projects keep their own background, and a project without bgOpacity still loads at 1 (ProjectIO, editor.js:2602).
rows.parityCheck: EditorSessionTests.A_new_session_is_4_1s_startup_state pins the new state (4.1's document with opacity 0, color #192e44); ProjectIO's missing-bgOpacity default stays 1 (Engine tests unchanged); Engine goldens keep 4.1's Document defaults.
rows.divergence: 4.1: a new template starts on a navy background at 100% opacity, so untouched regions export navy. v5: a new template starts with the background at 0% opacity, so untouched regions export transparent (Este, 2026-10-18).

rows.name: Region guide on the canvas (view only)
rows.behavior: 4.1 has no region guide: the regions show only as the navy background inside the mask (or the yellow grid when Grid is on), so a transparent template's regions look like the checkerboard around them.
rows.portTarget: ViewOptions.ShowRegionGuide (Engine, default off so the view goldens keep 4.1's frame); TemplateCanvasHost turns it on. Under the composite: each region tinted white at 7% and outlined in brand cyan at 45%, one device pixel inside its edge. Never in the export or the 3D preview.
rows.parityCheck: RegionGuideTests: a transparent region differs from the unguided frame while gaps and the outside do not, opaque art covers the guide, every region of both modes is outlined, the export is unchanged. TemplateCanvasHostTests compare the host frame with the engine view with the guide on.

rows.name: Region fills painted over background, under layers
rows.behavior: paintRegions(oc) occurs after background and before any layer, so region fills cover the background within region rects (fills are opaque unless colors carry alpha; hex has no alpha) but gutters still show background (until mask).
rows.quirks: Fills ignore bgOpacity: region areas are always opaque.
rows.portTarget: Call RegionPainter.Paint after bg draw.
rows.parityCheck: Fill + semi-transparent bg opacity: region interiors are fully opaque fill, gutters partially transparent bg.

rows.name: Live drawing preview composite
rows.behavior: If drawCanvas exists: globalAlpha = 0.5 when currentTool==='eraser' else 1; drawImage(drawCanvas,0,0) at 1:1 over all layers; alpha reset. Drawn before the mask so preview is also masked when showMask on.
rows.quirks: Eraser preview is a magenta/colored stroke marking removal at 50% alpha, not the actual erased result. drawCanvas must be template-size.
rows.portTarget: DrawBitmap(drawBitmap, 0,0, paint alpha 0.5/1) after layers, before DstIn mask.
rows.parityCheck: GoldenViewSelectTests vs-preview-* scenes hold the shape and eraser previews to 4.1 with Mask on; RendererOverlayTests pins that a preview pixel outside every region is masked when Mask is on and shown when it is off, and that the eraser preview draws at half alpha. Narrowed in M3b: pen previews are not frozen (approved divergence draw-pen-incremental-stroke), so the gutter clause is checked on a shape preview.

rows.name: Mask application (destination-in)
rows.behavior: If showMask: globalCompositeOperation='destination-in'; drawImage(maskCanvas,0,0); back to source-over. Everything outside region rects becomes alpha 0 (including bg, layers, preview). If showMask false, content in gutters and outside regions is visible (useful for placing art across seams); export behavior with mask is in another slice.
rows.quirks: Mask toggle (showMask) is a view/export setting; confirm the export slice honors it.
rows.portTarget: Paint with SKBlendMode.DstIn drawing the mask bitmap.
rows.parityCheck: Toggle mask: exact gutter pixels transparent vs filled; mask edge exact.

rows.name: Zoom resize and smoothing rule
rows.behavior: Every render sets canvas.width = TW*zoom and canvas.height = TH*zoom (resetting the canvas and its state each frame, fractional sizes truncated by the browser to integers), imageSmoothingEnabled = zoom < 1 (zoom >=1 uses nearest-neighbor for crisp pixels, zoom <1 smooth), clearRect, then draw checkerboard, then the offscreen scaled to the visible size.
rows.quirks: Canvas dims truncated: TW*zoom non-integer loses fractional pixel, while region coords * zoom still use float, causing 0.5px offset at the right/bottom edge for fractional zoom. The visible canvas is also stretched to the truncated size. Zoom value sets from a slider elsewhere; list allowed values (see zoom UI slice).
rows.portTarget: SkiaSharp SKElement/SKGLElement sized TW*zoom; draw offscreen with SKSamplingOptions Nearest when zoom>=1, Linear when <1 (and mipmap off).
rows.parityCheck: GoldenViewTests (M3a) at zoom 0.25, 0.5, 1, 1.5 and 3 and GoldenViewSelectTests at 0.5, 1, 1.5 and 2: crisp magnification and smooth downsampling; 1.5 gives 877x838 (RendererViewTests). The 200% scroll host compared side by side in the M3b look sign-off (state 05), signed off by Este on 2026-10-16 (.superpowers/m3b-look/SIGNOFF.txt). Narrowed in M3b: zoom 4 is outside v5's 25-300% range.
rows.divergence: 4.1: the canvas is reallocated and cleared on every render and clipped when it outgrows the area. v5: the frame keeps 4.1's truncated size (TW*zoom, editor.js:340-341), renders through one persistent offscreen surface and checker tile into a reused bitmap, at most once per display frame while dragging, and sits in a scroll host with scrollbars to pan; zoom stays 25-300% in 0.25 steps.

rows.name: Transparency checkerboard
rows.behavior: A 16x16 tile pattern: base #0f1f31, with #050c18 squares in top-left 8x8 and bottom-right 8x8; used as createPattern repeat and fills the whole visible canvas BEFORE drawing the composite. The tile is in screen pixels and does NOT scale with zoom, anchored at canvas origin (0,0). Dark navy tones, not the classic gray/white.
rows.quirks: Checkerboard is baked into the visible canvas, so screenshots of the canvas include it, but exports come from the offscreen (no checker). Created at module load via IIFE; declared after render() text but initialized before first call (const TDZ ok because render is called later).
rows.portTarget: SKShader.CreateBitmap(tile, Repeat, Repeat) on a paint, or a tiled DrawingBrush behind the SKElement; keep tile in device pixels (not scaled by zoom or DPI).
rows.parityCheck: View goldens: the corner pixels (0,0), (8,0), (8,8) and (0,8) match 4.1 at every captured zoom, and the tile stays 16 px at zoom 3. Narrowed in M3a: zoom 4 is outside v5's 25-300% range.

rows.name: Region grid overlay
rows.behavior: If showGrid (default false): strokeStyle rgba(255,255,0,0.3), lineWidth 1; strokeRect for every active region at (x*zoom, y*zoom, w*zoom, h*zoom). Drawn after composite, before selection UI, on the visible canvas only (not in export).
rows.quirks: Lines blurry because coordinates are integer. Port may keep (parity) or snap to half pixels (fix). Alpha 0.3 -> 76.5 rounds.
rows.portTarget: SKPaint Stroke width 1, color #FFFF00 alpha 0.3 (76/255), antialias on, DrawRect with the same unadjusted coordinates (no +0.5 offset) to reproduce the blur.
rows.parityCheck: Zoom 1 screenshot: grid lines are 2px wide faint (AA across two pixels); matches pixel diff within tolerance.

rows.name: Selection bounding box
rows.behavior: Only when currentTool==='select' and selectedLayerId!==null and the layer exists with img: size w=imgW*scale*zoom, h likewise; center at (x*zoom+w/2, y*zoom+h/2); save; translate center; rotate(rotation deg); strokeRect(-w/2,-h/2,w,h) in #17d4fa, lineWidth 2, dash [5,5]; then dash reset to []. flipH/flipV are NOT applied to the box (symmetric anyway). Opacity or visibility not considered.
rows.quirks: Dash starts at the top-left corner of the rect path. Box drawn for hidden layers too. Box sits above grid. Handles scale with zoom only in position; sizes (8px squares, 30px stem, 8px knob) are constant in screen pixels.
rows.portTarget: SKPaint Stroke 2px, SKPathEffect.CreateDash([5,5],0), color #17D4FA, within canvas.Save/Translate/RotateDegrees.
rows.parityCheck: GoldenViewSelectTests vs-select-z100 and vs-select-rot30-z100: the dashed box, its dash phase from (-w/2, -h/2) clockwise and the handles match 4.1's view under the golden rule; the rotation label's box is blanked in both images (interfaces R4). RendererOverlayTests: a hidden selected layer draws nothing. Narrowed in M3b: the label is pinned by unit tests, not pixels.
rows.divergence: 4.1: selection box and handles are drawn for a selected layer even when it is hidden. v5: hidden layers show no handles (approved decision).

rows.name: Corner resize handles
rows.behavior: Four 8x8 filled squares (#17d4fa) centered at the four box corners in the rotated local frame: order TL, TR, BR, BL, each fillRect(hx-4, hy-4, 8, 8). No edge-midpoint handles. Hit-testing for these lives in the mouse-handling slice and must use identical geometry (8px, plus any tolerance).
rows.quirks: Handles are axis-aligned to the rotated frame; fractional centers give AA edges.
rows.portTarget: DrawRect(SKRect) with fill paint, inside rotated transform.
rows.parityCheck: GoldenViewSelectTests vs-select-z100 and vs-select-z200: the 8 px corner handles stay 8 px at zoom 1 and 2. Narrowed in M3b: zoom 4 is outside v5's 25-300% range.

rows.name: Rotation handle (stem, knob, glyph)
rows.behavior: Stem: line from (0,-h/2) to (0,-h/2-30) magenta #f22f89 width 2 (solid; dash reset). Knob: circle at (0,-h/2-30) radius 8 filled #f22f89, stroked white lineWidth 1.5. Glyph: arc radius 4 from -0.7PI to 0.4PI (clockwise in canvas) stroked white 1.5; arrowhead: ax=cos(0.4PI)*4, ay=(-h/2-30)+sin(0.4PI)*4, path moveTo(ax-3,ay-2) lineTo(ax,ay) lineTo(ax+2,ay-3) stroked white 1.5. Note ax omits the knob center x (0) which is right, as center x=0.
rows.quirks: Handle is always above the box top edge in the layer's rotated frame, even when the layer is flipped or when near the canvas top (can be clipped off-canvas). Knob position independent of zoom (fixed 30 px).
rows.portTarget: SKPath arcs: Skia ArcTo with start/sweep degrees (-126 to 72: start -126, sweep 198) in SKPaint stroke 1.5, white; line caps Butt, join Miter to match canvas defaults.
rows.parityCheck: GoldenViewSelectTests at rotation 0, 30 and -135 (zoom 1 and 1.5): stem, knob and glyph match 4.1's view under the golden rule. Narrowed in M3b: rotations 90 and 180 are covered by RendererOverlayTests' geometry pins, not frozen pixels.

rows.name: Rotation angle label
rows.behavior: If layer.rotation !== 0: font '11px "JetBrains Mono", ui-monospace, monospace', fill #f22f89, textAlign center, text rotation.toFixed(1)+'°' (U+00B0) at (0, -h/2-30-16) in the rotated local frame (label rotates with the layer; upside-down at ~180). textBaseline default alphabetic.
rows.quirks: Font is not loaded via local asset in this slice; relies on JetBrains Mono being available (likely Google Fonts or system), otherwise falls back to ui-monospace. Label rotates with layer (can read upside-down). Negative zero rotation is '-0.0'? rotation!==0 guard avoids 0 but -0.04 shows '-0.0°'.
rows.portTarget: SKCanvas.DrawText with SKFont(JetBrains Mono bundled, 11px), SKTextAlign.Center, baseline alphabetic; format with rotation.ToString("F1", Invariant) + "°" (toFixed vs F1 rounding on halves: verify).
rows.parityCheck: SelectionGeometryTests: 17.25 gives '17.3°', -17.25 gives '-17.3°', -0.04 gives '-0.0°', 0 gives no label (JS toFixed(1)). RendererOverlayTests: the face is the vendored JetBrains Mono 400 at 11 px, #f22f89, centered at (0, -h/2 - 46) in the rotated frame, with no label pixel outside SelectionGeometry.LabelBounds. Compared side by side in the M3b look sign-off (state 03). Narrowed in M3b: the label is excluded from the golden comparison (interfaces R4).
rows.divergence: 4.1: label font JetBrains Mono is not bundled and falls back to ui-monospace when absent. v5: bundled JetBrains Mono, with rotation normalized to -180..180.

rows.name: Render tail: restore then updateCursor
rows.behavior: ctx.restore after the selection block, then updateCursor() called at the end of EVERY render (so cursor recomputed per frame/zoom/size change).
rows.quirks: Cursor URI regenerated (SVG string + btoa) on every render while eraser active, e.g. every mouse-move-driven render; expensive but fine.
rows.portTarget: Cursor updated via property-changed handlers for tool, brush size and zoom (not per frame).
rows.parityCheck: Through the bridge (H5): with the Eraser active, a brush size change (UI Automation RangeValue) and a zoom change (the zoom buttons) each change the ring the canvas sets before any pointer move; TemplateCanvasHostTests and CanvasCursorsTests. Reworded in M4a: the bridge reads the cursor the canvas sets (TemplateCanvasHost.CanvasCursor and its WPF cursor) after routed hover and drag input; the OS cursor image is not observable to automation, and CanvasCursorsTests pin the WPF cursors and the ring bitmap (H5).

rows.name: Default tool cursor
rows.behavior: Any tool other than eraser sets canvas cursor to crosshair (including select tool; there is no move/resize cursor change in this slice).
rows.quirks: Select tool shows crosshair even over handles (no hover feedback); resize/rotate hover cursors may be in the mouse slice but not here.
rows.portTarget: Cursor = Cursors.Cross on the SKElement.
rows.parityCheck: Through the bridge (H2, H5): idle hover gives the crosshair (Cross) on empty canvas with Select and everywhere with Draw, Line, Rect and Ellipse, the ring with the Eraser, and Grab (Hand) on the knob, ResizeNwse (SizeNWSE) on each corner and Move (SizeAll) on the body. Reworded in M4a: the bridge reads the cursor the canvas sets (TemplateCanvasHost.CanvasCursor and its WPF cursor) after routed hover and drag input; the OS cursor image is not observable to automation, and CanvasCursorsTests pin the WPF cursors and the ring bitmap (H2, H5).
rows.divergence: 4.1: every non-eraser tool shows a crosshair, with no hover feedback over handles. v5: hover cursors for move, resize and rotate (approved decision).

rows.name: Eraser brush ring cursor
rows.behavior: r=max(4, min(120, drawSize*zoom/2)); svg diameter d=ceil(r)*2+4, center c=d/2; draws black 3px stroke circle opacity 0.5 under a magenta (#f22f89) 1.5px dashed (4 3) circle, plus a 1.5px magenta center dot; encoded as base64 data URI SVG; hotspot at (c,c); fallback crosshair. Ring diameter equals brush size*zoom (min 8px, max 240px diameter) so it stays a valid CSS cursor (browser limit 128px-ish for some, up to 256 in Chromium).
rows.quirks: Brush size is NOT clamped to the ring cap: at large size*zoom the ring under-represents the actual eraser footprint (cap 120 radius). r can be fractional while d uses ceil, so ring is slightly off-center by <1px. Decide to keep cap or draw an overlay uncapped (fix).
rows.portTarget: WPF: create a custom Cursor from a rendered bitmap (CreateIconIndirect with hotspot) at the computed size, regenerate when drawSize/zoom/DPI change; or hide system cursor and draw the ring as an overlay in the SkiaSharp surface (better, no size cap, but then 'cap at 120' is a decision).
rows.parityCheck: Through the bridge (H5): ring radius max(4, size x zoom / 2) DIPs (diameter size x zoom) at sizes 4 and 50 and zoom 25-300%, hotspot centered (CanvasCursorsTests), capped by the Win32 cursor size (128 - ceil(2 x display scale) device px). Reworded in M3b: 4.1's 240 px clamp is the fixed behavior; size 100 and zoom 4 are outside v5's ranges. Reworded in M4a: the bridge reads the cursor the canvas sets (TemplateCanvasHost.CanvasCursor and its WPF cursor) after routed hover and drag input; the OS cursor image is not observable to automation, and CanvasCursorsTests pin the WPF cursors and the ring bitmap (H5).
rows.divergence: 4.1: eraser ring radius is capped at 120 so it under-represents the real footprint at large size and zoom, and is off-center by under 1px. v5: ring drawn at the true brush footprint, radius max(4, size x zoom / 2) DIPs, centered, at device pixels (clearly unintended mismatch). A Win32 cursor bitmap is at most 256x256 device px, so the radius is capped at 128 - ceil(2 x display scale) device px (126 at 100%, 124 at 200%), which binds only above a 124 DIP ring diameter at 200%.

rows.name: Full render order (contract)
rows.behavior: Offscreen: clear -> bg (image stretched or color, with bgOpacity) -> region fills (grouped, per fill) -> layers bottom-to-top (visible, with save/alpha/translate/rotate/flip/filter/RGB shift) -> live draw preview (0.5 alpha if eraser) -> mask destination-in (if showMask). Visible canvas: resize to zoom -> clear -> checkerboard -> composite scaled (nearest if zoom>=1) -> grid (if showGrid) -> selection box, handles, rotation handle, label (select tool only) -> updateCursor.
rows.quirks: render() is called from many places and rebuilds everything each frame (no dirty tracking); port can cache but must preserve output.
rows.portTarget: Skia paint pipeline in the same order; single Render(SKCanvas) used for view and, minus overlays/checkerboard, for export.
rows.parityCheck: Automated pixel-diff harness (reuse spike) against Electron software canvas across a scenario matrix: bg color/image/opacity, each fill type, layers with each adjustment, mask on/off, zoom set, grid, selection states. Edge AA tolerance <=3/255.

rows.name: Premultiplied alpha behaviors across adjustments
rows.behavior: Canvas stores premultiplied; getImageData/putImageData convert. RGB shift routes through these, so semi-transparent pixels get quantization before and after shift. CSS filters operate on the premultiplied/unpremultiplied per Filter Effects spec (color matrices applied on unpremultiplied color).
rows.quirks: Low-alpha pixel channel loss in JS is an artifact; the port may legitimately be more precise (document as accepted diff).
rows.portTarget: Use SKColorType.Rgba8888 with SKAlphaType.Unpremul bitmaps for the shift path; Skia color matrix filters unpremul inputs by default, matching the spec.
rows.parityCheck: Test image with alpha ramp 0-255 and shift/filter combos; max diff <=1-2 levels on alpha 1-254 pixels.
rows.divergence: 4.1: RGB shift round-trips through premultiplied canvas data and loses low-alpha channel precision. v5: shift runs on unpremultiplied pixels, more precise at low alpha.

rows.name: State captured by undo snapshots
rows.behavior: history = createHistory(30); snapshotState/restoreState (outside slice) own what is captured; regionColors are restored via spread copy (line 1444) and layers' nextId rebased (1465). Fills are snapshot-compatible because normalizeFill accepts strings and objects.
rows.quirks: Whether bgColor/bgOpacity/zoom are in the snapshot is in the other slice; verify.
rows.portTarget: Immutable snapshot records (layers list clone, regionColors dictionary, bg settings); structural sharing for images.
rows.parityCheck: Undo/redo across fill changes and layer adjustments restore identical composites.

rows.name: setTool: active tool, button highlight, cursor refresh
rows.behavior: Six tools: select, pen, line, rect, circle, eraser bound to #btnSelect,#btnDrawPen,#btnDrawLine,#btnDrawRect,#btnDrawCircle,#btnEraser. setTool sets currentTool, removes btn-active from all, adds it to the matching button, then updateCursor(). App starts in 'select' (setTool('select') at load). Only one tool active at once.
rows.quirks: None.
rows.portTarget: ToolMode enum on EditorViewModel; toolbar ToggleButtons (RadioButton-style group) bound to CurrentTool with IsChecked converter; SetTool command also refreshes canvas Cursor.
rows.parityCheck: ToolsViewModelTests and LedgerScenarioTests: each tool button makes its tool current and only that button active; Select is active at launch. The active look is compared side by side in the M3b look sign-off (state 04). Narrowed in M3b: view-model evidence, not UI automation (M6).

rows.name: Re-click or re-press active tool returns to Select
rows.behavior: toggleTool(tool): if tool is already current and is not 'select', switch to 'select'; otherwise switch to tool. Select never toggles off (pressing V while on Select stays Select). Button onclick and keyboard shortcuts (v,b,l,u,o,e at editor.js:1782-1787, e ignored with Ctrl) both use toggleTool.
rows.quirks: Shortcuts live outside this slice but share toggleTool; keep one code path.
rows.portTarget: ToggleToolCommand(ToolMode) in view model; KeyBindings V/B/L/U/O/E map to same command. Ensure Ctrl+E does not toggle eraser.
rows.parityCheck: Press B twice: pen then select. Press V twice: stays select. Ctrl+E does nothing to tool.

rows.name: Tool auto-reverts to Select on layer add and layer select
rows.behavior: addLayer() and selectLayer() both call setTool('select'). addDrawingLayer does NOT call setTool, so after finishing a pen/line stroke the drawing tool stays active. duplicateLayer, removeLayer do not change tool.
rows.quirks: Clicking a layer row while drawing tool is active silently switches tool; keep.
rows.portTarget: Same rules inside AddLayer/SelectLayer view-model methods; AddDrawingLayer leaves tool unchanged.
rows.parityCheck: LedgerScenarioTests.Tool_buttons_toggle_off_to_select_and_an_import_or_a_list_pick_returns_to_select: with Pen active an import returns to Select, a pen stroke keeps Pen, a pick in the layer list returns to Select, and undo leaves the tool alone (ImportService.LayersAdded and LayersViewModel.LayerPicked through Composition). Narrowed in M3b: the import is a file drop through LayersViewModel, not a drag from Explorer.

rows.name: Canvas cursor per tool, eraser ring cursor
rows.behavior: updateCursor: eraser tool gets generated SVG cursor (dashed magenta #f22f89 ring over black 50% opacity ring, center dot r=1.5), radius = clamp(drawSize*zoom/2, 4, 120), size d=ceil(r)*2+4, hotspot at center, fallback crosshair. All other tools: crosshair. Called on setTool and on brush size slider input. Not refreshed on zoom change inside this slice. During select drags cursor becomes grabbing/nwse-resize/move; on idle select mouse hover shows grab over rotate handle else crosshair.
rows.quirks: Zoom changes may not refresh eraser cursor unless another call occurs (check zoom handler outside slice); consider fixing by refreshing on zoom. Resize cursor is always nwse regardless of corner. After a drag ends, cursor reset occurs in mouseup (outside slice).
rows.portTarget: Render ring to a WPF Cursor via CursorInteropHelper from a bitmap (or draw ring as overlay in Skia on pointer move, preferred for arbitrary size). Standard cursors: Cross, Hand (grab), SizeAll (move), SizeNWSE (resize), closed-hand custom for grabbing.
rows.parityCheck: Through the bridge (H5): with the Eraser the canvas cursor is the ring with radius max(4, size x zoom / 2) DIPs at sizes 4 and 50 and zoom 25%, 100%, 200% and 300%, rebuilt as soon as size or zoom changes; Draw, Line, Rect and Ellipse hover with the crosshair. CanvasCursorsTests: the ring bitmap at device scale and the 256-px Win32 cap. Reworded in M4a: the bridge reads the cursor the canvas sets (TemplateCanvasHost.CanvasCursor and its WPF cursor) after routed hover and drag input; the OS cursor image is not observable to automation, and CanvasCursorsTests pin the WPF cursors and the ring bitmap (H5).
rows.divergence: 4.1: eraser ring cursor is not refreshed when zoom changes, so it drifts from the real brush size. v5: cursor refreshes on zoom as well as tool and brush size changes.

rows.name: Draw color, size, fill controls
rows.behavior: #drawColor input updates drawColor on each input event (default #17d4fa). #drawSize range updates drawSize (default 4) and refreshes cursor. #drawFill checkbox sets drawFill on change (default false). Min/max for slider are defined in HTML, not here.
rows.quirks: Color input does not snapshot undo. Slider range lives in index.html (other slice); port must copy it.
rows.portTarget: ColorPicker control (WPF has none built in; use a custom or Extended.Wpf.Toolkit/ModernWpf-style picker) bound to DrawColor; Slider for DrawSize; CheckBox for DrawFill. Verify slider range in index.html.
rows.parityCheck: BrushViewModelTests and LedgerScenarioTests: color #17d4fa, size 4 and Fill off at launch; a size change rebuilds the eraser ring (TemplateCanvasHostTests). Narrowed in M3b: view-model evidence, not UI automation (M6).

rows.name: Layer data model and defaults
rows.behavior: Layer fields: id (auto-increment from nextId=1), name, img, visible=true, opacity=1, x,y, scale, rotation=0 (degrees), flipH=false, flipV=false, brightness=100, contrast=100, saturate=100, hueRotate=0, rShift=0,gShift=0,bShift=0. makeLayer defaults: name 'Layer', x/y 0, scale 1 (falsy values coerced: scale 0 -> 1, x 0 stays 0).
rows.quirks: Adjustment display uses `sel.brightness || 100`, so a value of 0 (valid slider min) displays and reloads as 100 in the controls (and sat/contrast likewise). Real stored 0 is used by renderer but the slider shows 100 after any updateUI. Port must decide: fix (recommended, show 0) and verify pixel parity of render stays driven by true values. hueRotate/rShift use `|| 0` which is harmless.
rows.portTarget: Layer record/class with SKBitmap Source; INotifyPropertyChanged. Keep field names for v4 project-file read compatibility.
rows.parityCheck: ProjectIOTests (M2b) load a v4 project and compare every layer field and round-trip it; LayerPropertiesViewModelTests: a stored adjustment of 0 displays as 0. Narrowed in M3b: the display half is the view-model.
rows.divergence: 4.1: a stored adjustment of 0 is treated as falsy and shown as 100 in the controls. v5: 0 displays and reloads as 0.

rows.name: Add image layer: auto-fit and placement
rows.behavior: addLayer(img,name,dropX,dropY): saveUndo first. scale = min(front.w/img.width, front.h/img.height)*0.85 where front=SHIRT_REGIONS.torso_front (active mode's region, so Pants mode uses whatever torso_front maps to there). Without drop point: centered in torso_front. With drop point (both defined): image centered on drop coordinates. Pushed to top of stack, selected, tool -> select, UI and render refreshed.
rows.quirks: Default name uses `'Image ' + nextId` evaluated AFTER nextId++ in the same object literal, so first unnamed layer is named 'Image 2' while its id is 1 (off-by-one). Keep or fix; users rarely see it since file drops pass names. In Pants mode torso_front may not exist: verify SHIRT_REGIONS keys for Pants (switchMode, other slice) or front is undefined and addLayer throws. Image with width 0 gives Infinity scale.
rows.portTarget: AddLayer(SKBitmap, name, SKPoint? dropAt). Read torso_front rect from current region set.
rows.parityCheck: Add 512x512 and 100x400 images in Shirt mode: assert x,y,scale numbers match JS to 1e-9. Drop at (300,200): center equals drop point.
rows.divergence: 4.1: default name 'Image N' uses the incremented id, so the first unnamed layer is 'Image 2' with id 1. v5: default layer names match the id.

rows.name: Add drawing layer from stroke canvas
rows.behavior: addDrawingLayer(canvas,name): autocrop (pad default 10) the full TW x TH draw canvas; if nothing drawn (no alpha>0 pixel) return silently with no layer. Otherwise loads cropped dataURL into an Image asynchronously, then makeLayer(img, name||'Drawing '+(nextId+1), crop.x, crop.y, 1), push, select, updateUI, render. No saveUndo here (caller does it on mousedown). Does not switch tool.
rows.quirks: Default name uses nextId+1 before makeLayer increments, so name number equals id (differs from addLayer's off-by-one) ; 'Drawing 1' for first. Async decode means render order race if two strokes finish rapidly; port sync removes this. Edge pad clipping lives in autocrop (outside slice lines 160+).
rows.portTarget: Crop SKBitmap by alpha bbox + pad 10 (synchronously; no encode round-trip needed) then new Layer at crop origin scale 1.
rows.parityCheck: Draw a single dot: layer bounds = dot bbox +/-10 clipped to canvas; empty stroke (eraser-only) adds nothing.

rows.name: Duplicate layer
rows.behavior: duplicateLayer(id): no-op if missing. saveUndo; shallow clone with new id, name = original + ' copy' (stacks: 'A copy copy'), x+10,y+10, shares same img object. Inserted directly above original in z-order, selected, UI+render. Triggered by row 'Dupe' button and properties 'Duplicate' button.
rows.quirks: Clone copies all adjustment values and flips. Tool not changed.
rows.portTarget: DuplicateLayerCommand; bitmap reference shared (immutable) safe.
rows.parityCheck: Dup layer index+1, offsets exactly +10,+10, name suffix, selection moves to clone, undo restores.

rows.name: Delete layer and reselection
rows.behavior: removeLayer(id): saveUndo (even if id not found), filter out. If the removed layer was selected, select the new topmost layer (last in array) or none if empty; if a different layer removed, selection unchanged. No confirmation dialog. Row 'Del' button. Clear All (btnClear, outside slice) empties all.
rows.quirks: Selecting topmost (not neighbor) after delete; Delete key shortcut is elsewhere (1700s).
rows.portTarget: DeleteLayerCommand; no confirm to match.
rows.parityCheck: Delete selected middle layer: top layer becomes selected. Delete non-selected: selection kept.
rows.divergence: 4.1: removeLayer pushes an undo snapshot even when the id is not found, creating an empty step. v5: every mutation is exactly one undo step, with no empty steps.

rows.name: Toggle layer visibility
rows.behavior: toggleLayerVisibility flips visible with NO saveUndo (not undoable). Row button label 'Hide'/'Show' with title 'Hide layer'/'Show layer'; button text color #c4cdda when visible, #5e6b7f hidden. Hidden layers are skipped by hit-testing.
rows.quirks: Visibility toggle is not undoable though snapshot contains visible; undoing a different change later restores earlier visible state unexpectedly.
