Also nameSpan opacity 0.4 for hidden is assigned then overwritten by `style.cssText +=` (cssText getter includes the opacity so it actually persists; still dim). Treat as: hidden name text at 40% opacity.
rows.portTarget: ToggleVisibilityCommand; do not push history to match, or deliberately add undo (decide).
rows.parityCheck: Toggle, then Undo: the visibility comes back in one step (LayerOpsTests, LayersViewModelTests, LedgerScenarioTests). Reworded in M3a to the fixed behavior; 4.1's toggle was not undoable.
rows.divergence: 4.1: visibility toggle is not undoable. v5: visibility toggle is exactly one undo step.

rows.name: Select layer
rows.behavior: selectLayer(id): set selectedLayerId, tool -> select, rebuild UI, render. Clicking a row (not on an action button, checked via e.target.dataset.action) selects. Canvas hit-test select calls it too.
rows.quirks: Rebuilding the whole list on each selection (innerHTML clear) would cancel an in-progress HTML drag; WPF virtualized list won't have this issue.
rows.portTarget: SelectedLayer property on VM; ListBox/ItemsControl row click.
rows.parityCheck: LayersViewModelTests and LedgerScenarioTests: a pick in the list selects the layer, highlights its row and fills the properties panel. Narrowed in M3b: view-model evidence, not UI automation (M6).

rows.name: Layer list rows (top = highest z)
rows.behavior: List built from last array element to first. Each row: draggable div.layer-item (+ .selected for selected), data-layer-id, 48x48 thumbnail (object-fit contain, black bg, radius 4, pointer-events none) from img.src, right column with bold 12px name (ellipsis, nowrap) and three equal buttons: Dupe (cyan #17d4fa tint), Hide/Show (neutral), Del (red #ff5472). Row styles in styles.css:289-313 (hover border, selected style, drag indicators). List fully rebuilt on every updateUI.
rows.quirks: Thumbnail ignores adjustments, rotation, opacity (raw source). Thumbnails for drawing layers are the cropped data URL. Row has no keyboard focus/accessibility; native should add. Button titles are tooltips.
rows.portTarget: ListBox with reversed ObservableCollection view (CollectionViewSource sort desc by index or reversed projection); DataTemplate with Image (Stretch=Uniform on black, CornerRadius 4), TextBlock TextTrimming=CharacterEllipsis, three small buttons colored per brand tokens (626labs-design).
rows.parityCheck: A selected row (state 03) compared side by side in the M3b look sign-off, and a hidden row, a long name truncated and 20 layers scrolling checked by hand in the M3b manual checklist (H8); signed off by Este on 2026-10-16 (.superpowers/m3b-look/SIGNOFF.txt). Narrowed in M3b: Este's review stands in for a screenshot diff.
rows.divergence: 4.1: layer rows have no keyboard focus or accessibility. v5: layers panel is keyboard operable with automation names and a cyan focus ring.

rows.name: Drag-to-reorder layers in panel
rows.behavior: HTML5 drag on rows: dragstart records layerDragId, effectAllowed move, then (next tick) adds .dragging-layer (opacity 0.4). dragover on another row computes top/bottom by pointer vs row mid-Y, shows 2px cyan border on that edge, stores target id+pos; dragging over itself ignored. drop: saveUndo, remove moved layer, then 'top' inserts AFTER target in array (above in z), 'bottom' inserts BEFORE target (below in z). Drop on self, no target, or missing ids just cleans up (no undo entry is pushed in the self/none case since check is before saveUndo). dragend cleans classes. Selection unchanged by reorder.
rows.quirks: Stale layerDragOverId: if you drag over a row, then leave to empty list area and drop, the drop uses the last hovered target (list container has no drop handler except rows). Drag from outside (a file) over rows triggers dragover with layerDragId null, harmless but shows indicator. Dropping at 'top' of the topmost row etc works. Drop does not stopPropagation of dragover so document-level preventDefault applies.
rows.portTarget: WPF DragDrop.DoDragDrop from PreviewMouseMove after SystemParameters.MinimumHorizontal/VerticalDragDistance; DragOver sets insert-adorner line top/bottom; Drop applies same index math on underlying list. Use custom data format, not Text.
rows.parityCheck: LayerOpsEditTests and LayersReorderTests check the reorder index math with 4 layers over every (from, to, position) against editor.js:621-655. Through the bridge (H7, H7b): the bottom of four rows dropped on the top row's top half becomes the top, and with 20 layers the top row dropped on the last row's lower half becomes the bottom, each one undo step. Narrowed in M4a: the gesture is real WPF routed input injected in-process by the test-only input bridge (brg smoke; interfaces R7, R8) and read back through its inspect command and UI Automation; the bridge cannot show the OS cursor image or drive a physical device (H7, H7b).
rows.divergence: 4.1: dropping outside a row reuses the last hovered target (stale drag target). v5: stale drag target is cleared so only a live target reorders.

rows.name: Up/Down buttons
rows.behavior: Up swaps selected with next array element (raises z) if not last; Down swaps with previous if not first. updateUI+render. NO saveUndo for either. No-op at the ends; no disabled state.
rows.quirks: Not undoable (inconsistent with drag-reorder, which is undoable). Recommend fix: push history.
rows.portTarget: MoveUp/MoveDown commands with CanExecute false at ends (visually enabled in original; either).
rows.parityCheck: Up and Down swap with the neighbor and do nothing at the ends; Undo reverts a move in one step (LayerOpsTests, LayersViewModelTests). Reworded in M3a to the fixed behavior; 4.1's Up and Down were not undoable.
rows.divergence: 4.1: Up/Down reorder is not undoable, unlike drag-reorder. v5: reorder is exactly one undo step.

rows.name: Empty selection panel
rows.behavior:
When no layer selected, #layerControls shows

Select a layer to edit.

and updateUI returns early. Layer list still rendered (empty list shows nothing, no placeholder inside this function).
rows.quirks: None.
rows.portTarget: Properties panel visibility template: TextBlock 'Select a layer to edit.' styled as info text when SelectedLayer null.
rows.parityCheck: LayerPropertiesViewModelTests and LedgerScenarioTests: with no selection the panel shows 'Select a layer to edit.'; a press on empty canvas returns to it. Narrowed in M3b: view-model evidence, not UI automation (M6).

rows.name: Name and X/Y fields
rows.behavior: Name text input: onchange (commit on blur/Enter) sets name and rebuilds UI (list updates). X and Y number inputs show toFixed(0) integers, commit on change (not each keystroke), set sel.x=+value, render only (X/Y header labels 'X: n  Y: n' not refreshed by typing but refresh on next updateUI). Labels show toFixed(0). Values are canvas px of top-left of unrotated image. No undo snapshots for any of these edits. Empty/non-numeric X gives 0 (+'' = 0) or NaN for text (number input blocks text).
rows.quirks: Displayed X rounds, stored X stays fractional: typing then re-rendering UI may silently show a rounded value but not write it back. During drag the header span xVal/yVal and inputs are not live-updated for move (updateUI only for rotate/resize), so X/Y fields go stale while moving until mouseup/next update. Name is not undoable. Name can be empty string.
rows.portTarget: TextBox with LostFocus/Enter commit binding (UpdateSourceTrigger=LostFocus), NumericUpDown-style TextBox with integer display format F0.
rows.parityCheck: LayerPropertiesViewModelTests and LedgerScenarioTests: X '12.7' stores 12.7 and shows '13'; an unparsable entry reverts; a name change shows in the list; X and Y follow a move drag live; each committed edit is one undo step. Narrowed in M3b: view-model evidence, not UI automation (M6).
rows.divergence: 4.1: X/Y fields and header stay stale during a move drag and edits are not undoable. v5: fields track the layer live and each edit is one undo step. Text that is not a finite number below 1e21 is refused and the field reverts (4.1's +value stored Infinity for 1e400).

rows.name: Scale slider
rows.behavior: Range 1..500 (percent), step default 1, value sel.scale*100 (fractional scales truncated by range display rounding to integer step). oninput: scale = value/100, label updates 'N%', render. Label initial (scale*100).toFixed(0)%. Scaling anchors top-left (x,y unchanged), not center. No undo.
rows.quirks: Corner-handle resize scales about center and can produce scale >5 or <0.01*; slider clamps display (range input clamps value to 1..500 when set programmatically, so a 700% layer shows 500% handle but label 700%). Resize min is 0.01 so slider min 1% = 0.01 consistent.
rows.portTarget: Slider Minimum=1 Maximum=500 IsSnapToTickEnabled TickFrequency=1; label binding StringFormat {0:0}%.
rows.parityCheck: LayerPropertiesViewModelTests and LedgerScenarioTests: the slider keeps the top-left corner, clamps to 1-500% and each change is one undo step (a drag is one); scale 1 renders at natural size (GoldenRenderTests, M1). Narrowed in M3b: view-model evidence, not UI automation (M6).
rows.divergence: 4.1: slider range 1-500 disagrees with handle/key/wheel limits and the label can exceed the slider. v5: one scale clamp of 1%-500% for slider, keys, wheel and handles, and the change is undoable.

rows.name: Rotation slider
rows.behavior: Range -180..180 degrees, integer. oninput sets rotation, label 'N°'. Rotation about layer center. Drag-rotate can produce non-integers; slider rounds on display only.
rows.quirks: Label can show fractional degrees after handle rotation (e.g. 12.345678°) because rotVal uses raw value interpolation `${sel.rotation}` with no rounding. Decide format.
rows.portTarget: Slider -180..180; rotate transform in SkiaSharp about center via canvas.RotateDegrees.
rows.parityCheck: LayerPropertiesViewModelTests: the slider stores the rotation normalized to -180..180, the label is whole degrees, and a drag is one undo step. Rotated pixels are held to 4.1 by GoldenRenderTests at 30, -135, 90 and 15 degrees (M1) and GoldenViewSelectTests vs-select-rot30-z100. Narrowed in M3b: 30 degrees stands in for 45.
rows.divergence: 4.1: rotation label shows raw fractional degrees after handle rotation. v5: rotation label is rounded and rotation is normalized to -180..180.

rows.name: Layer opacity slider
rows.behavior: Range 0..100 percent; oninput sets opacity=value/100, label 'N%', render. Default 100.
rows.quirks: Not undoable.
rows.portTarget: Slider 0..100 -> SKPaint alpha (globalAlpha equivalent).
rows.parityCheck: LayerPropertiesViewModelTests and LedgerScenarioTests: 50% stores 0.5 and is one undo step; GoldenRenderTests gap-opacity-with-adjust (M1) holds a 0.5-opacity layer to 4.1's export.
rows.divergence: 4.1: opacity change is not undoable. v5: opacity change is exactly one undo step.

rows.name: Flip H / Flip V
rows.behavior: Buttons toggle flipH / flipV and render. No undo. Buttons have tooltips 'Flip horizontally.' and 'Flip vertically.'.
rows.quirks: Not undoable. Interaction of flip with rotation direction determined by renderer (other slice); hit-testing ignores flip (pointInRotatedRect symmetric, fine).
rows.portTarget: Commands toggling bool; Skia Scale(-1,1) about center in render.
rows.parityCheck: LayerOpsEditTests: Flip H and Flip V toggle and are one undo step each; the flipped pixels are held to 4.1 by GoldenRenderTests layer-rotate-scale-fliph-opacity and layer-rotate-neg-flipv-upscale (M1) and GoldenViewSelectTests vs-select-fliph-z50.
rows.divergence: 4.1: Flip H/V is not undoable. v5: each flip is exactly one undo step.

rows.name: Center on front torso
rows.behavior: Button sets x,y so the scaled, unrotated image is centered in SHIRT_REGIONS.torso_front; scale and rotation unchanged. render only. No undo. Full-width button.
rows.quirks: Uses unrotated w/h so rotated layer is centered by box, same as center anchor (fine). Label says 'front torso' even in Pants mode where region mapping may differ.
rows.portTarget: Command using current region set torso_front.
rows.parityCheck: Numeric x,y check for several scales.
rows.divergence: 4.1: Center on front torso is not undoable and the Placement group is always shown. v5: it is one undo step and the Placement group is hidden until a layer is selected.

rows.name: Image adjustments collapsible panel
rows.behavior: Header 'Image adjustments' (uppercase mono 11px cyan) with arrow ▶ collapsed / ▼ expanded; click toggles #adjPanel display. Collapsed on every updateUI rebuild (state not preserved): selecting another layer, rename, reset, rotate/resize drag all rebuild and collapse it.
rows.quirks: Expansion state lost on any updateUI, including when rotate/resize handle drag triggers updateUI; moving a slider inside the panel does not rebuild so it stays open while adjusting.
rows.portTarget: Expander control with IsExpanded stored in VM; decide whether to persist expansion across rebuilds (improvement).
rows.parityCheck: LayerPropertiesViewModelTests and LedgerScenarioTests: Image adjustments stays open across a selection change, every edit and Reset (the documented fix). Narrowed in M3b: view-model evidence, not UI automation (M6).
rows.divergence: 4.1: adjustments panel collapses on every UI rebuild (select, rename, reset, rotate/resize drag). v5: adjustments panel stays open.

rows.name: Brightness/Contrast/Saturation/Hue/RGB shift sliders
rows.behavior: Brightness 0-200 (default 100), Contrast 0-200 (100), Saturation 0-200 (100), Hue rotate 0-360 deg (0), R/G/B shift -100..100 (0). Each oninput stores numeric value, updates its label (%, °, plain number), renders. R/G/B labels colored #ff5472, #4f4, #66f and slider accent-color same. Values pass into render filters (ctx.filter and RGB shift in renderer, other slice).
rows.quirks: `|| 100` falsy bug: stored 0 for brightness/contrast/saturate displays as 100 and the slider reinstates 100 on next rebuild (but the layer still renders at 0 until the user touches). CSS filter hue-rotate and saturate use specific matrices (not HSL); must match exactly. No undo.
rows.portTarget: Slider x7; Skia SKColorFilter (SKColorFilter.CreateColorMatrix composing brightness/contrast/saturate/hue matrices per CSS filter spec) and per-channel add matrix. Build a matrix that reproduces CSS filter order and clamping.
rows.parityCheck: Narrowed in M4b: the frozen 4.1 goldens adjust-brightness-150, adjust-contrast-40, adjust-saturate-0, adjust-hue-90, adjust-extremes, adjust-combo, gap-opacity-with-adjust, rgb-shift and rgb-shift-with-adjust-rotated under the golden rule (GoldenRenderTests.Engine_export_matches_the_frozen_4_1_golden), AdjustTests (the brightness, contrast, saturate and hue-rotate tables and matrices; Rgb_shift_is_exact_clamped_and_skips_transparent_pixels), LayerPropertiesPanelTests.The_ten_sliders_have_4_1s_ranges and LayerPropertiesViewModelTests (Each_adjustment_is_one_clamped_step_that_keeps_the_others, Zero_adjustments_show_as_zero_after_reselect), in place of a 4.1 render at every slider extreme.
rows.divergence: 4.1: the '|| 100' falsy bug shows a stored 0 as 100 for brightness, contrast and saturation. v5: 0 adjustments display as 0.

rows.name: Reset adjustments
rows.behavior: Button 'Reset adjustments' (pink border #f22f89 text #ff5aa3) sets all seven adjustment values to defaults (100,100,100,0,0,0,0), then updateUI (rebuilds and collapses panel) and render. No undo.
rows.quirks: Collapses panel after reset (via updateUI).
rows.portTarget: ResetAdjustmentsCommand.
rows.parityCheck: LayerPropertiesViewModelTests and LedgerScenarioTests: Reset restores LayerAdjustments.Default as one undo step and none when already at the defaults, the panel stays open, and the render equals the unadjusted layer (LayerOpsEditTests).
rows.divergence: 4.1: Reset adjustments is not undoable and collapses the panel. v5: reset is one undo step and the panel stays open.

rows.name: Layer name never interpolated into markup
rows.behavior: Properties markup is a template with values assigned via DOM properties afterward; layer names are user-controlled filenames. Invariant covered by tests/injection.test.js (PR #27 bug).
rows.quirks: Row names use textContent (safe); this class of bug disappears natively.
rows.portTarget: Not applicable in WPF (data binding); add a test that names with <, quotes, & render as literal text.
rows.parityCheck: Name '' shows literally everywhere.
rows.divergence: 4.1: layer names needed DOM-property assignment to avoid markup injection (tests/injection.test.js). v5: not carried, since WPF bindings cannot interpolate names into markup.

rows.name: Property panel refresh behavior while dragging
rows.behavior: Move drag updates only render (panel X/Y stale). Rotate and resize drags call updateUI each mousemove (full list+controls rebuild), keeping sliders/labels in sync but collapsing the adjustments panel and discarding focus.
rows.quirks: Expensive per-move DOM rebuild; native binding removes. Move drag leaving stale X/Y is likely unintentional.
rows.portTarget: Two-way binding keeps all live; decide to refresh X/Y live while moving (improvement).
rows.parityCheck: During a knob drag the Rotation slider equals the layer's rotation after every move, and during a corner drag the Scale slider equals its scale (bridge H2, read through UI Automation RangeValue); LayerPropertiesViewModelTests and LedgerScenarioTests pin the live X and Y and the panel after a fit. Narrowed in M4a: the gesture is real WPF routed input injected in-process by the test-only input bridge (brg smoke; interfaces R7, R8) and read back through its inspect command and UI Automation; the bridge cannot show the OS cursor image or drive a physical device (H2).
rows.divergence: 4.1: move drag leaves panel X/Y stale while rotate/resize rebuild the whole panel and drop focus. v5: bound properties update live without rebuilds or lost focus.

rows.name: Background color swatches
rows.behavior: 12 swatches generated from BG_COLORS: Navy #192e44, Navy Deep #0f1f31, Black #050c18, Charcoal #2d2d2d, Wine #4a1942, Forest #1b4332, Ocean #0c2461, Storm #2c3e50, White #f5f5f5, Red #b71c1c, Magenta #f22f89, Cyan #17d4fa; title tooltip = name. Click: saveUndo, set bgColor, CLEAR bgImage, sync #bgColor input value, render. Styling in styles.css .swatch (hover, focus-visible, .active at 425-433).
rows.quirks: .swatch.active CSS exists but editor.js never sets it, so no active indicator. Swatches are div not button (keyboard focus via tabindex? check index/html).
rows.portTarget: ItemsControl with Border swatches (focusable, tooltip names) bound to command SetBackgroundColor; selected state not tracked here (.active class never applied in this slice).
rows.parityCheck: Click each: canvas bg = hex, bg image removed, undo restores.

rows.name: Background color picker and opacity slider
rows.behavior: #bgColor (default #192e44): pointerdown saves one undo snapshot, input event sets bgColor and CLEARS bgImage, renders continuously. #bgOpacity: pointerdown saves undo, input sets bgOpacity=value/100 (default 1), render. One drag gesture = one undo step. Range 0-100 (HTML).
rows.quirks: Keyboard/arrow or touch-less changes to color/opacity skip undo. Setting bg color also drops the background image (destructive but undoable). Opacity applies to both color and image presumably in renderer.
rows.portTarget: Color picker open/close transaction: snapshot on picker open or first change; slider Thumb.DragStarted -> push undo.
rows.parityCheck: BackgroundGroupTests.A_thirty_tick_color_drag_is_one_undo_step and A_thirty_tick_opacity_drag_is_one_undo_step (one undo returns to the value before the drag), A_slider_press_and_release_around_thirty_ticks_is_one_step. Reworded in M4b: the keyboard arrow on the slider records one step, the fix (BackgroundGroupTests.The_keyboard_arrow_on_the_slider_records_a_step).
rows.divergence: 4.1: a background color or opacity change made without a pointer press (a keyboard arrow on the slider) records no undo step. v5: it records one, and a drag or a picker session stays one step (M4b, plan item 6).

rows.name: Background image picker
rows.behavior: #bgImageBtn clicks hidden #bgFileInput. On change with a file: saveUndo, read as data URL, decode, set bgImage, render. Cancel does nothing. No type validation beyond input accept (HTML). Failure to decode is silent. bgImage is NOT cleared by any later image; only by swatch or color change. Snapshot stores bgImage.src dataURL.
rows.quirks: saveUndo happens before load success, so a corrupt file leaves a no-op undo entry. The same file chosen twice does not retrigger onchange (input value not reset). Check accept attribute in index.html. Large images embed as data URL in every undo snapshot (memory up to 30 snapshots).
rows.portTarget: OpenFileDialog (png/jpg/jpeg/gif/webp/bmp/svg filter), decode via SKBitmap/SKCodec; Svg via Svg.Skia if kept.
rows.parityCheck: BackgroundGroupTests.Each_accepted_format_decodes_through_the_background_route, A_corrupt_image_gives_no_step_and_a_status_line, Picking_the_same_file_twice_acts_twice, A_cancelled_image_dialog_changes_nothing; the bg-image-opacity and bg-image-stretched goldens; through the bridge (M4b smoke G1) a picked PNG paints the background as one undo step and Undo restores the prior background. Narrowed in M4b: the dialog is the bridge's file-dialog queue; the native single-select dialog (Win32FileDialogs.OpenImage) is not opened by any test. MAN-9 (Este, 2026-10-25): the native dialog lists the import formats and allows one file; a picked PNG becomes the background in one undo step; Cancel changes nothing and records no step.
rows.divergence: 4.1: undo is saved before the image loads, so a corrupt file leaves a no-op undo entry and failures are silent. v5: undo step only on successful load, with a status message on failure.

rows.name: Drop zone panel: click-to-browse and drag-over highlight
rows.behavior: #dropZone click opens #fileInput; dragover preventDefault+stopPropagation and adds .dragover class (styles.css:277 style); dragleave removes; drop removes class and calls handleFiles(files) with no coordinates (centered placement). #fileInput onchange calls handleFiles too. File input is probably multiple (check HTML) and not reset after use.
rows.quirks: Same file selected twice in the picker in a row does not re-fire change. dragleave fires when moving over child elements causing highlight flicker.
rows.portTarget: Border AllowDrop=True with DragEnter/Leave/Drop handling DataFormats.FileDrop; Click opens OpenFileDialog Multiselect.
rows.parityCheck: Drop 3 PNGs through the drop zone's DropFiles path: 3 layers, each placed by LayerOps.Place at the default 0.85 fit centered on torso_front, stacked identically, as one undo step (LayersViewModelTests.A_zone_drop_uses_the_default_placement, ImportServiceTests, LayerOpsTests); a canvas drop centers each on the drop point (ImportServiceTests.A_canvas_drop_centers_every_layer_on_the_drop_point). Narrowed in M3a: the drop zone's own UI (drag-over highlight, Tab and Enter) is the held panel-drop-zone row, checked by hand in the smoke checklist.

rows.name: Drop on canvas places layer at drop point
rows.behavior: canvas dragover and drop preventDefault+stopPropagation. Drop point = (clientX - rect.left)/zoom, (clientY - rect.top)/zoom, i.e. canvas pixel coords; image centered on that point. Multiple files all land on the same point. If _assetDragFile is set (drag from the asset browser panel), that file is consumed (cleared) and loaded with the stored name at drop point, ignoring dataTransfer files.
rows.quirks: If an asset drag is abandoned (dragend outside canvas never clears _assetDragFile unless handled at editor.js:2498+), a later OS file drop is hijacked by the stale asset file. Port should clear on drag end. rect.left uses bounding rect so CSS scroll/zoom consistent.
rows.portTarget: Drop handler on Skia host: convert WPF position through inverse zoom/scroll transform to canvas px. Asset browser drag: use in-process drag payload (DataObject custom format) instead of a global.
rows.parityCheck: LedgerScenarioTests: a file dropped at four template positions at zoom 0.5, 1 and 2 lands with its center on the drop point; TemplateCanvasHostTests map the host point by zoom. The stale asset drag is gone: asset-drag-stale-reference (bridge A1, MAN-1).
rows.divergence: 4.1: an abandoned asset drag leaves a stale _assetDragFile that hijacks the next OS file drop. v5: stale asset-drag state is cleared on drag end.

rows.name: Block browser default open-file on drop
rows.behavior: Document-level dragover/drop preventDefault so dropping files anywhere never navigates the window. Labeled CRITICAL.
rows.quirks: Drops outside canvas/zone do nothing (not add).
rows.portTarget: Not needed in WPF; just ensure unhandled drops do nothing (AllowDrop false elsewhere).
rows.parityCheck: Drop an image on the toolbar: no crash, no new layer.
rows.divergence: 4.1: document-level preventDefault stops the browser navigating to dropped files. v5: not carried, since a WPF window has no navigate-on-drop behavior.

rows.name: Image file acceptance and naming
rows.behavior: isImageFile: true if MIME starts with image/, else extension (lowercased, text after last dot) in png,jpg,jpeg,gif,webp,bmp,svg. Non-images skipped with console.log only (no user message). Layer name = filename with last extension stripped. Each file read independently and asynchronously: layer order depends on decode completion, not drop order. Decode failure only console.error; no UI error.
rows.quirks: Race: multi-file drop order nondeterministic. Each addLayer call pushes its own undo snapshot (N files = N undo steps). SVG without width/height yields img.width 0 or 150x150 default in Chromium; scale = Infinity possible. File named 'a.b.png' becomes 'a.b'. Silent failures hide errors: add toast in native.
rows.portTarget: Decoder via SKBitmap.Decode; SVG needs Svg.Skia or rasterize at intrinsic size; animated GIF uses first frame (check Chromium behavior: first frame). Process files sequentially to make order deterministic (deviation).
rows.parityCheck: Drop png, jpg, gif, webp, bmp, svg, txt and an extensionless text file: the five raster files become layers named by file name minus the last extension; svg, txt and the extensionless file become no layer and each shows a status message (ImageImporterTests, ImportServiceTests). Reworded in M3a: v5 refuses SVG.
rows.divergence: 4.1: SVG accepted, multi-file drops load in nondeterministic order with one undo step per file, and non-images are skipped silently. v5: SVG import dropped with a message, multi-file import in pick order as one undo step, and status messages for rejected files.

rows.name: Topmost layer hit-testing and deselect
rows.behavior: On select-tool mousedown (after handle checks), iterate layers top to bottom; skip invisible; point-in-rotated-rectangle on the layer's scaled bounding box (inverse-rotated about center, bounds inclusive). First hit: selectLayer, start move drag. Transparent pixels inside the box still hit. Miss: selectedLayerId=null, dragMode=null, rebuild UI, render. Mouse coords = (client - canvasRect)/zoom.
rows.quirks: Hit area is the whole box, not alpha-aware, ignoring flips (symmetric). Clicking the selected layer's handles takes priority even if a higher layer is over them. Deselect on empty click also sets dragMode null but a prior dragging state is not reset here. selectLayer inside switches tool (already select). No saveUndo for selection or move start (move undo snapshot, if any, is elsewhere, verify in mouseup).
rows.portTarget: Pointer-down on SKElement: invert zoom transform; same math in editor core (shared pure function).
rows.parityCheck: Unit tests: points on edges, rotated 30/90 degrees, hidden layer skipped, overlap picks topmost.

rows.name: Move drag
rows.behavior: On hit: dragMode='move', dragging=layer, store pointer start and layer start position, cursor 'move'. mousemove sets x,y = start + delta (in canvas px, so independent of zoom). Re-renders only. No snapping, no clamping to canvas.
rows.quirks: Browser canvas mouse events stop when pointer leaves the canvas unless handlers on window/document exist (mouseup likely document-level, see 1242, 1298); native should capture. Move-end undo snapshot is outside this slice: verify where saveUndo is pushed for move/rotate/resize (not in mousedown), otherwise select drags are not undoable.
rows.portTarget: CaptureMouse on canvas host so drags continue outside control; delta in canvas space.
rows.parityCheck: A 50x30 px drag at zoom 2 moves the layer 25x15 template px, as one undo step, and the layer keeps following past the canvas edge under mouse capture (bridge H1; LedgerScenarioTests, TemplateCanvasHostTests). Narrowed in M4a: the gesture is real WPF routed input injected in-process by the test-only input bridge (brg smoke; interfaces R7, R8) and read back through its inspect command and UI Automation; the bridge cannot show the OS cursor image or drive a physical device (H1).
rows.divergence: 4.1: move drag stops tracking when the pointer leaves the canvas and the move has no undo step. v5: mouse capture across the edge and each move is exactly one undo step.

rows.name: Rotation handle
rows.behavior: Handle position: center + rotated vector straight 'up' from center by (scaledHeight/2 + 30/zoom) canvas px (constant 30 screen px beyond top edge at any zoom). Hit radius 14/zoom canvas px (14 screen px). Checked only for the currently selected visible-or-hidden layer with an img, before corners. Press: dragMode='rotate', rotStartAngle = angle(deg, 0 = up, clockwise) of pointer from center minus current rotation; cursor 'grabbing'. Hover (no drag) over handle shows 'grab'. Handle drawing (visual) happens in the renderer outside this slice.
rows.quirks: Handle works even if selected layer is hidden (visible not checked). Handle position ignores flip. Hover grab cursor only updates on mousemove when not dragging.
rows.portTarget: Same math in core; overlay drawn in Skia pass (render slice). Cursor via Cursors.Hand / custom.
rows.parityCheck: SelectionGeometryTests and RendererOverlayTests: the knob sits where the overlay draws it at rotation 0 (zoom 0.5, 1, 2) and 30, 90, 180 (zoom 1); hit boundary 13.9 vs 14.1 screen px; no handle on a hidden selected layer. Narrowed in M3b: zoom 4 is outside v5's 25-300% range, and 30 and 90 stand in for 45.
rows.divergence: 4.1: rotation handle is shown and active for a hidden selected layer. v5: hidden layers show no handles.

rows.name: Rotate drag with 45-degree snapping
rows.behavior: mousemove: angle = atan2(dx, -dy) in degrees about layer center (0=up, positive clockwise); newRot = angle - rotStartAngle; snap to the first of [-180,-135,-90,-45,0,45,90,135,180] within 3 degrees (strict <3), else unsnapped fractional degrees. Rotation is NOT normalized/wrapped, so it can pass beyond +/-180 (e.g. 200 or -250) while slider range is -180..180; after UI rebuild the slider clamps. Calls render then updateUI each move.
rows.quirks: Unbounded rotation values and a jump discontinuity: the atan2 angle jumps from 180 to -180 across the bottom, so newRot can leap by 360 when passing straight down from the start position (e.g. start rotation 0, drag past 180). Snap candidates +/-180 only match near those exact values, so with value 355 no snap appears. Likely user-visible; keep or normalize to (-180,180].
rows.portTarget: Same formula in double precision (Math.Atan2). Keep snap table and 3-degree threshold; decide normalization.
rows.parityCheck: Unit-test: pointer positions producing 44.2, 47.9, 48.1 degrees snap or not; sequence crossing +180.
rows.divergence: 4.1: rotation is never normalized and can jump by 360 across the atan2 discontinuity. v5: rotation normalized to -180..180 with the 45-degree snap kept.

rows.name: Corner resize handles (uniform scale)
rows.behavior: Four corners TL,TR,BR,BL computed from center with rotation applied; hit radius 10/zoom (10 screen px). Checked after rotate handle, only for the selected layer. Press records corner index, start scale, start distance from pointer to layer center; cursor 'nwse-resize'. mousemove: scale = max(0.01, startScale * (currentDist/startDist)); then x,y recomputed so layer center stays fixed. All four corners behave identically (distance-ratio, uniform, aspect preserved, scale about center). render + updateUI each move.
rows.quirks: If pointer pressed exactly on center-distance 0 (corner hit radius ensures nonzero; for tiny layers a corner hit within 10px could have resizeStartDist near 0 giving Infinity/NaN ratio). No max scale (slider caps at 500 only visually). Cursor is nwse for all four corners though NE/SW corners should be nesw. No modifier (shift/alt) behaviors. Dragging past the center keeps growing (distance based, no flip).
rows.portTarget: Same math in core; corner handles drawn by overlay renderer.
rows.parityCheck: Unit-test: pointer doubling distance doubles scale; scale floor 0.01; center invariant to 1e-9.
rows.divergence: 4.1: resize has no upper limit and can divide by a near-zero start distance. v5: single 1%-500% scale clamp shared with slider, keys and wheel.

rows.name: Idle hover cursor
rows.behavior: With select tool and no active drag, mousemove sets 'grab' cursor when over selected layer's rotation handle, else 'crosshair' (even over layers or corner handles; no move/resize hover cursors).
rows.quirks: Cursor only becomes move/resize/grabbing after press; restored at mouseup (outside slice).
rows.portTarget: PointerMoved handler setting Cursor; consider adding resize/move cursors (improvement, not parity).
rows.parityCheck: Through the bridge (H2): idle hover over the knob, each corner and the body gives Grab, ResizeNwse and Move, else the crosshair. Reworded in M4a: the bridge reads the cursor the canvas sets (TemplateCanvasHost.CanvasCursor and its WPF cursor) after routed hover and drag input; the OS cursor image is not observable to automation, and CanvasCursorsTests pin the WPF cursors and the ring bitmap (H2).
rows.divergence: 4.1: idle hover shows only grab or crosshair, with no move or resize cursors. v5: hover cursors for rotate, resize and move.

rows.name: Drawing tools mousedown setup (pen, line, rect, circle, eraser)
rows.behavior: saveUndo, isDrawing=true, record start and points, create a TW x TH offscreen canvas. For pen and eraser: stroke style = drawColor (eraser: opaque #f22f89 mask), lineWidth=drawSize, round caps and joins, beginPath, moveTo. Then render (live preview). Eraser mask consumed at mouseup (applyEraseStroke, outside slice).
rows.quirks: undo is saved at mousedown even if no stroke results (empty click on draw tool). Pen paints in a single moveTo/lineTo path stroked incrementally per move (re-stroking accumulates alpha overlap on semi-transparent colors at joints; opaque unaffected). Included here only for slice-boundary coverage (lines 1058-1147 straddle the slice end at 1055).
rows.portTarget: Slice boundary item: drawing pipeline belongs to adjacent slice; port as SKBitmap/SKCanvas stroke buffer with SKPaint round cap/join, antialias on (match canvas AA for diff).
rows.parityCheck: Reworded in M3b to the approved divergence: a Line, Rect and Ellipse stroke with identical points renders as 4.1 renders it (GoldenAppTests shape-* scenes, M2a); a pen stroke is the whole path stroked once and a pen press is a brush-size dot (ToolsTests, LedgerScenarioTests); no press records an undo step (CanvasInteractionTests, LedgerScenarioTests).
rows.divergence: 4.1: undo saved at mousedown even with no stroke, and pen is re-stroked incrementally per move. v5: pen stroke drawn once at mouseup, a press with no movement draws a brush-size dot, and no empty undo steps.

rows.name: Shared mutable editor state
rows.behavior: Globals referenced across this slice: layers[], selectedLayerId, nextId, currentTool, drawColor/drawSize/drawFill, bgColor/bgImage/bgOpacity, zoom, dragging/dragMode/dragStart/layerStart, rot/resize start values, layerDrag*, _assetDragFile/_assetDragName, SHIRT_REGIONS (swapped by switchMode). updateUI is the single refresh point and is called from many places.
rows.quirks: nextId is never reset on restore/new project (check restoreState), so ids keep growing; names use ids.
rows.portTarget: EditorDocument (layers, bg) + EditorSession (tool, selection, drag state) with change notifications; avoid global mutable state.
rows.parityCheck: Snapshot JSON round trip for state used by history (snapshotState at 1404).
rows.divergence: 4.1: editor state lives in shared mutable globals in editor.js. v5: replaced by the Document/History model, so the globals are not carried.

rows.name: Mouse to template-space coordinate mapping
rows.behavior: All mouse handlers compute mx=(clientX-rect.left)/zoom, my=(clientY-rect.top)/zoom. Canvas is TW*zoom x TH*zoom px (585x559 at 100%), display:block, no CSS scaling. Coordinates are unclamped floats. Single handler per event (onmousedown/move/up/leave/wheel); no pointer or touch events.
rows.quirks: No button filter: right and middle button also draw/drag. Decide keep or restrict to left button (recommend fix) and whether to add mouse capture (see canvas-draw-release-outside).
rows.portTarget: One WPF input surface (SKElement) with MouseDown/Move/Up/Leave/Wheel. Mouse.GetPosition(surface)/zoom. Size the surface to 585*zoom x 559*zoom DIPs and account for Windows DPI scaling so 1 template px = zoom DIPs.
rows.parityCheck: CanvasCoordinatesTests (M3a): template = position in the frame / zoom at zoom 0.25, 1 and 3 and device scale 1, 1.25 and 1.5, to 1e-9, matching editor.js:1059-1061's formula. TemplateCanvasHostTests: only the left button presses, and the press captures the mouse. Narrowed in M3b: compared with the ported formula, not a logged Electron run.
rows.divergence: 4.1: any mouse button draws or drags, with no capture. v5: left button only, with mouse capture across the canvas edge.

rows.name: Cursor shapes per tool and drag state
rows.behavior: Default crosshair. Select tool hover on selected layer's rotation handle (within 14/zoom) shows grab, elsewhere crosshair. Dragging: rotate=grabbing, resize=nwse-resize (all 4 corners), move=move. Mouseup and mouseleave in select tool reset to crosshair. Eraser tool uses generated SVG ring cursor (see eraser-cursor). render() ends by calling updateCursor(), which overwrites to crosshair/eraser ring, so the grabbing/move/nwse-resize cursors set at mousedown are overwritten on the very next render (each mousemove during drag).
rows.quirks: Because render() resets the cursor to crosshair on every move, the move/rotate/resize drag cursors effectively flash only until the first mousemove. Port decision: keep (crosshair during drags) or fix (hold drag cursor). Hover 'grab' also gets overwritten by the render path only when render runs, but hover branch returns without render so grab sticks.
rows.portTarget: FrameworkElement.Cursor: Cursors.Cross, Cursors.Hand/ScrollAll, Cursors.SizeNWSE. Set only if you keep the intent.
rows.parityCheck: Through the bridge (H2): hovering the knob gives Grab (Hand), and the knob drag holds Grabbing (Hand) and the corner drag ResizeNwse (SizeNWSE) after every move until the release. Reworded in M4a: the bridge reads the cursor the canvas sets (TemplateCanvasHost.CanvasCursor and its WPF cursor) after routed hover and drag input; the OS cursor image is not observable to automation, and CanvasCursorsTests pin the WPF cursors and the ring bitmap (H2).
rows.divergence: 4.1: render() resets the cursor to crosshair on every move, so drag cursors flash only until the first move. v5: drag cursor is held for the whole drag. Grab and grabbing show the Windows Hand cursor (WPF has no stock grab cursor); provisional, M3b look sign-off.

rows.name: Rotation handle hit test and drag start
rows.behavior: On mousedown with Select tool, selected layer (exists and has img; visibility not checked) is tested first. Handle position = layer center minus (sin r, cos r)*(h/2+30/zoom) where h=img.height*scale and r=rotation in radians. Hit if distance < 14/zoom template px. Starts dragMode='rotate', dragging=sel, rotStartAngle=atan2(mx-cx, -(my-cy))*180/pi - sel.rotation. Returns without selecting anything else. Cursor grabbing.
rows.quirks: Hit radius 14 screen px vs drawn handle radius 8. Rotation handle remains hittable for a hidden (visible=false) selected layer. Handle is hittable while it overlaps another layer (handle priority).
rows.portTarget: Port getRotHandlePos and atan2 convention verbatim (0 deg = up, clockwise positive). Keep 14/zoom and 30/zoom so on-screen size is constant in pixels.
rows.parityCheck: SelectionGeometryTests: the knob is at the center plus R(rotation) x (0, -(h/2 + 30/zoom)), where the overlay draws it, to 1e-9 at rotation 0 for zoom 0.5, 1 and 2 and at 30, 90 and 180 for zoom 1 (4.1's getRotHandlePos agrees at 0 and 180 only); a press 13.9 screen px from it hits and 14.1 misses; a hidden selected layer has no handle hit (SelectionGeometryTests, RendererOverlayTests.The_rotate_handle_is_hit_where_the_overlay_draws_it, LedgerScenarioTests). Reworded in M3b: the mirrored 4.1 hit point is the fixed behavior this row's divergence states.
rows.divergence: 4.1: the rotation handle stays hittable for a hidden selected layer, and is hit-tested at the knob's mirror image across the layer's vertical axis (getRotHandlePos uses c.x - sin r x d, editor.js:1036), so a rotated layer's visible knob does not rotate it. v5: hidden layers have no handles, and the handle is hit where it is drawn.

rows.name: Corner resize handle hit and start
rows.behavior: If rotate handle missed, the four corners of the selected layer (unrotated half extents +-w/2,+-h/2 rotated by layer rotation about its center) are tested in order TL,TR,BR,BL, hit if distance < 10/zoom. On hit: dragMode='resize', resizeCorner=i (unused later), resizeStartScale=sel.scale, resizeStartDist=distance(mouse, center). Cursor nwse-resize.
rows.quirks: All corners behave identically (uniform scale from center, not anchored at opposite corner). If mousedown starts exactly at center (dist 0) later ratio would divide by zero; cannot occur because start is on a corner unless layer scale ~0.
rows.portTarget: Same math in C#. Store resizeStartScale and resizeStartDist; corner index can be dropped.
rows.parityCheck: Unit test hit/miss at 9.9 and 10.1 px from each rotated corner.

rows.name: Resize drag math
rows.behavior: On mousemove: d=distance(mouse, center); ratio=d/resizeStartDist; scale=max(0.01, resizeStartScale*ratio); then x,y are recomputed so the center stays fixed: x=cx-w/2, y=cy-h/2 with new w,h. Uniform scale only, no shift/alt modifiers, no maximum. render() then updateUI() (sidebar sliders refresh).
rows.quirks: No saveUndo before resize (see undo-coverage-gaps). No upper limit on drag, while key '+' caps at 5 and wheel has no cap.
rows.portTarget: Port formula exactly; raise PropertyChanged for scale/x/y.
rows.parityCheck: Scripted drag from corner at distance 100 to 150 from center doubles... yields scale*1.5; min clamp at 0.01 verified; center unchanged.
rows.divergence: 4.1: resize has no maximum and no undo step, while '+' caps at 5 and wheel is uncapped. v5: one 1%-500% clamp for all paths and the drag is exactly one undo step.

rows.name: Rotate drag with 45-degree snap
rows.behavior: angle=atan2(mx-cx, -(my-cy)) in degrees; newRot=angle-rotStartAngle. If within 3 degrees (strict <) of any of -180,-135,-90,-45,0,45,90,135,180 it snaps to that value (first match in list order). Assigned directly to layer.rotation. render() then updateUI(). Render shows magenta degree readout (toFixed(1)) when rotation != 0.
rows.quirks: Rotation is never normalized during drag: newRot = angle - startAngle can reach about +-360 (e.g. start rotation 170, drag across the 180 discontinuity gives -190ish values). Snap list only has +-180, so values like 350 or -270 do not snap to 0/-90. Keyboard bracket keys DO normalize to [-180,180). Decide whether to normalize.
rows.portTarget: Same math; rotation property in degrees.
rows.parityCheck: SelectionGeometryTests.Driving_the_mouse_around_the_center_in_1_degree_steps_records_4_1s_sequence_with_every_snap_plateau drives the pointer around the layer center in 1-degree steps through a full turn (-179 to 180); the recorded rotation sequence equals, exactly, a transcription of editor.js:1172-1180 (atan2 minus the start angle, then the first multiple of 45 strictly within 3 degrees), including the snap plateaus and the crossing of +-180. Narrowed in M3b: the sequence equals a transcription of editor.js:1172-1180, not a recorded 4.1 run.
rows.divergence: 4.1: dragged rotation is unbounded (about +-360) so values like 350 or -270 never snap. v5: rotation normalized to -180..180 so snapping works at every angle.

rows.name: Layer pick (topmost) and move drag
rows.behavior: If no handle hit, layers are scanned from top (end of array) to bottom; first layer with visible=true and img whose rotated bounding rectangle contains the point is selected via selectLayer(id) (also forces tool to select, updateUI, render), then dragMode='move', dragStart=mouse, layerStart={x,y}, cursor move. Moving sets x=layerStart.x+(mx-dragStart.x), y likewise (no snapping, no clamping to template). Hit test is the layer rect only (img.width*scale by img.height*scale rotated), not pixel alpha, and ignores flips (symmetric).
rows.quirks: Clicking transparent areas of a layer picks it (rect-based). Layers can be dragged fully off-canvas and become unrecoverable by mouse (still in list panel). A move-drag that begins on an already selected layer still calls selectLayer, which re-renders the sidebar (updateUI) every mousedown.
rows.portTarget: Hit test with inverse rotation about center, as in pointInRotatedRect (note sign convention: rotates point by -rotation). Move via delta in template space.
rows.parityCheck: Overlapping layers: a press on a fully transparent pixel inside the top layer's box selects the top layer, and with that layer hidden the same press selects the layer under it (bridge H1; LayerOpsTests, SelectionGeometryTests, LedgerScenarioTests). A (30,-20) px drag at zoom 2 moves the layer (15,-10) template px, and every drag is one undo step (bridge H1). Narrowed in M4a: the gesture is real WPF routed input injected in-process by the test-only input bridge (brg smoke; interfaces R7, R8) and read back through its inspect command and UI Automation; the bridge cannot show the OS cursor image or drive a physical device (H1).
rows.divergence: 4.1: move drag has no undo step and no capture, so a drag can strand a layer off-canvas by mouse. v5: rect-based hit-test kept, drag is exactly one undo step with capture and selection survives undo.

rows.name: Click on empty space deselects
rows.behavior: If no handle and no layer hit: selectedLayerId=null, dragMode=null, updateUI(), render(). Handles disappear. Note this does not clear 'dragging' (already null).
rows.quirks: Clicks in transparent area of a layer still select it (see select-move-hit-and-drag).
rows.portTarget: SelectedLayer = null, invalidate.
rows.parityCheck: A press on empty canvas clears the selection, the properties panel shows its empty state and the view draws no overlay, with no undo step (LedgerScenarioTests, RendererOverlayTests). Narrowed in M3b: view-model and render evidence, not UI automation (M6).

rows.name: Select tool mousemove idle, mouseup and mouseleave
rows.behavior: Mousemove with no drag only updates cursor (grab on rotate handle, else crosshair), no render. Mouseup in select tool clears dragging and dragMode and resets cursor. Mouseleave in select tool also ends any drag (so dragging off the canvas drops the layer where it was). Mousemove with dragging set but dragMode null cannot happen.
rows.quirks: Leaving the canvas edge cancels the drag but keeps the changed position (no revert).
rows.portTarget: Handle MouseLeave to end drag, or use CaptureMouse and keep dragging (behavior change; decide).
rows.parityCheck: Reworded in M3b to the fixed behavior: a move drag follows the pointer past the canvas edge (template x 700 and 760) and back, and a release outside the window ends it where released, as one undo step (bridge H1); a lost capture ends it as a release at the last point (CanvasInteractionTests, TemplateCanvasHostTests). Narrowed in M4a: the gesture is real WPF routed input injected in-process by the test-only input bridge (brg smoke; interfaces R7, R8) and read back through its inspect command and UI Automation; the bridge cannot show the OS cursor image or drive a physical device (H1).
rows.divergence: 4.1: Leaving the canvas edge cancels a drag and hover cursors are limited to grab/crosshair. v5: Left-button mouse capture keeps the drag alive across the edge and hover cursors reflect handles.

rows.name: Selection box and handle rendering (editor overlay)
rows.behavior: Only when tool is select and a layer is selected with img: dashed (5,5) 2px cyan #17d4fa bounding rect, 8x8 cyan corner squares centered at corners, magenta #f22f89 2px stem 30px (screen px, unscaled by zoom) above top edge, 8px radius magenta circle with white 1.5 stroke, inner white arc from -0.7pi to 0.4pi radius 4 plus a small arrowhead, and a '11px JetBrains Mono, ui-monospace' magenta centered rotation readout 'N.N°' 16px above the handle when rotation != 0. All drawn after the layer composite and not in export. Drawn in rotated space around the layer center at zoom scale, line widths in screen px.
rows.quirks: Hit radii (14, 10) are larger than drawn shapes (8, 4). Arrowhead drawn from a hand-tuned offset formula; copy coordinates verbatim.
rows.portTarget: SkiaSharp overlay pass drawn in screen space after composite: SKPaint dashed PathEffect, SKCanvas.Translate/RotateDegrees. Bundle JetBrains Mono or choose fallback.
rows.parityCheck: GoldenViewSelectTests at zoom 1, 1.5 and 2, rotation 0, 30 and -135, flipped and over the Pants grid: boxes and handles in identical positions under the golden rule, the label blanked (interfaces R4). Narrowed in M3b: rotation 30 and -135 stand in for 37.5.

rows.name: Drawing tools mousedown: snapshot, offscreen canvas, stroke style
rows.behavior: For pen, line, rect, circle, eraser: saveUndo() immediately (before knowing if anything will be drawn), isDrawing=true, drawStartX/Y=mouse, drawPoints=[start], new offscreen drawCanvas of TW x TH (585x559, transparent). Pen and eraser immediately set stroke style (drawColor, or '#f22f89' for eraser), lineWidth=drawSize, lineCap round, lineJoin round, beginPath, moveTo(start). Then render(). Tools line/rect/circle set style on every move instead.
rows.quirks: saveUndo runs on every mousedown even if nothing is drawn (single click, off-template click, eraser with no layer selected), creating no-op undo entries that waste the 30-entry stack and require an extra Ctrl+Z. Decide: keep or push snapshot lazily on commit (recommended fix).
rows.portTarget: SKBitmap/SKSurface 585x585... TWxTH BGRA premul in drawing session; SKPaint stroke style, StrokeCap.Round, StrokeJoin.Round for pen/eraser.
rows.parityCheck: A press records no undo step and a click with Line, Rect or Ellipse adds nothing (CanvasInteractionTests, LedgerScenarioTests). Shape pixels: GoldenAppTests shape-* scenes (M2a). Reworded in M3b: 4.1's consumed history entry is the fixed behavior, and the pen pixels follow the approved draw-pen-incremental-stroke divergence.
rows.divergence: 4.1: Every draw mousedown pushes an undo snapshot even if nothing is drawn. v5: Each mutation is exactly one undo step, with no empty steps.

rows.name: Pen and eraser incremental stroking
rows.behavior: On each mousemove while drawing: push point to drawPoints (never used again), dc.lineTo(mx,my), dc.stroke() on the single accumulating open path. On mouseup pen calls dc.stroke() once more (eraser does not). Color is opaque drawColor, width drawSize (1-50), round caps/joins. Live preview is the drawCanvas composited every render.
rows.quirks: The whole path is re-stroked on every mouse event, so antialiased edge pixels get composited onto themselves repeatedly and darken toward opaque; result depends on mouse event frequency (O(n^2) work too). Final edge alpha is therefore not a single-stroke AA. To be pixel-compatible replicate incremental re-stroking; to be deterministic, stroke once at mouseup (a deliberate fix, changes edges).
rows.portTarget: Keep a single SKPath; on each move call path.LineTo then DrawPath(stroke paint) onto the persistent stroke bitmap. This replays the whole path each move exactly like Canvas2D, reproducing the same AA accumulation.
rows.parityCheck: Narrowed in M4b: stroke-once is proven, not pixel-diffed against 4.1's re-stroked edges, which the fix changes on purpose; the pen has no frozen golden. ToolsTests.Pen_strokes_the_whole_path_once; CanvasInteractionTests.A_pen_drag_previews_the_whole_path_and_commits_one_selected_layer_named_Pen_drawing (the committed layer equals Tools.CommitDrawing of the whole path, so the event rate does not change it); LivePreviewTests pin the preview stroke; the eraser's two-point scenes match 4.1's goldens stroked once (GoldenAppTests.Production_stroke_once_matches_the_golden_on_two_point_erase_scenes, EraserTests.A_two_point_drag_strokes_identically_once_and_replayed). The bridge's pen strokes pass end to end (M4b smoke, M4a H4).
rows.divergence: 4.1: Pen and eraser re-stroke the whole path on every mouse event, so edges depend on event frequency. v5: Strokes are drawn once at mouseup for deterministic edges.

rows.name: Single click / zero-length stroke handling
rows.behavior: Pen: mousedown does moveTo only; with no mousemove, stroke() of a path containing only moveTo paints nothing, so hasContent=false and no layer is created (no visible dot). If the mouse moves to the same pixel (lineTo same point) round-cap zero-length segment may paint a dot in Chromium. Line tool: click with no move shows nothing; move to a distinct point draws. Rect: zero width and zero height strokeRect/fillRect paints nothing. Circle: zero radii ellipse paints nothing (stroke) .
rows.quirks: A plain click with the pen produces no dot, which users may expect. Keep or fix (draw a dot of diameter drawSize).
rows.portTarget: Explicitly special-case: only commit when the drawing bitmap has any alpha>0. Verify degenerate behavior empirically in Skia (Skia draws dots for zero-length round-cap lines; Canvas2D may not).
rows.parityCheck: Line, Rect and Ellipse: a click without movement adds no layer and no undo step. Pen: a click adds one layer, a brush-size dot. Eraser: a click erases nothing (eraser-click-without-move). LedgerScenarioTests, CanvasInteractionTests. Reworded in M3b to the approved divergence (a pen click draws a dot).
rows.divergence: 4.1: A press with no movement draws nothing and creates no layer. v5: A press with no movement draws a brush-size dot.

rows.name: Line tool geometry
rows.behavior: On each move the drawCanvas is fully cleared and redrawn: strokeStyle and fillStyle = drawColor, lineWidth=drawSize, lineCap='round' (lineJoin left default miter), beginPath, moveTo(start), lineTo(mouse), stroke. The 'Fill' checkbox is ignored. No shift-constrain for angle, no snapping.
rows.quirks: Round caps extend beyond endpoints by drawSize/2; beyond canvas bounds clipped at 0..585/0..559.
rows.portTarget: Clear bitmap, SKPaint stroke with StrokeCap.Round, DrawLine.
rows.parityCheck: Scripted drag from (50,60) to (300,200) at width 4 and 30; pixel diff within AA tolerance.

rows.name: Rectangle tool geometry
rows.behavior: Normalized rect: x=min(start,mouse), y=min, w=abs diff, h=abs diff (drag any direction). If Fill checkbox (drawFill) on: fillRect with drawColor, no outline; else strokeRect with lineWidth=drawSize, miter joins (lineJoin default). Stroke is centered on the rectangle edge (extends drawSize/2 outward and inward). Drawn into cleared drawCanvas on each move.
rows.quirks: Filled rect has no stroke, so filled size = drag rect, unfilled outer size = drag rect + drawSize. Miter limit default of 10 matters for thick strokes only at sharp angles (rect corners are 90 so unaffected).
rows.portTarget: DrawRect with SKPaintStyle.Fill or Stroke, StrokeJoin.Miter, miter limit 10 (Canvas2D default).
rows.parityCheck: Drag four directions, filled and unfilled, widths 1/10/50; compare bounding boxes exactly and pixels within AA tolerance.

rows.name: Ellipse tool geometry
rows.behavior: Bounding box from start to mouse: center=midpoint, rx=|dx|/2, ry=|dy|/2, ctx.ellipse(cx,cy,rx,ry,0,0,2pi). Fill checkbox: fill() else stroke() with lineWidth=drawSize. Always axis-aligned. No shift-for-circle.
rows.quirks: ellipse() with one radius 0 and the other >0: Canvas2D draws a degenerate path (a line when stroked); verify Skia DrawOval behaves the same or special-case.
rows.portTarget: SKCanvas.DrawOval(SKRect) fill or stroke.
rows.parityCheck: Drag in all four directions; compare pixel diff within AA tolerance; rx or ry = 0 draws nothing/line as in fixture.

rows.name: Live preview compositing
rows.behavior: While drawCanvas exists, render() composites it on top of all layers at globalAlpha 1 (0.5 for eraser) before the region mask is applied, so preview respects the Mask checkbox (clipped to the garment regions when Mask on). Preview is not in the layer list, not in export.
rows.quirks: Preview and final committed layer differ for strokes extending outside masked regions (committed layer keeps all pixels, only the view/export mask hides them).
rows.portTarget: Draw stroke bitmap with SKPaint alpha 0.5 (eraser) or 1 in the compositing pass before the DstIn mask.
rows.parityCheck: GoldenViewSelectTests: the live preview of a rect, a filled ellipse, a line and a two-point eraser stroke mid-gesture, at zoom 0.5, 1 and 2, with Mask on, match 4.1's view under the golden rule; the eraser preview is magenta at half alpha (RendererOverlayTests, LivePreviewTests).

rows.name: Mouseup commit of a drawing as a new layer
rows.behavior: On mouseup with isDrawing and drawCanvas: pen calls stroke(); the full TW*TH alpha channel is scanned for any alpha>0. If content: non-eraser tools call addDrawingLayer(drawCanvas, 'Pen'|'Line'|'Rect'|'Circle' + ' drawing'), name uses the tool id capitalized (so 'Pen drawing', not 'Draw drawing'). addDrawingLayer autocrops to the alpha bounding box padded by 10 px (clamped to canvas), makes a PNG data URL, and on image load creates a layer at (crop.x,crop.y), scale 1, rotation 0, opacity 1, defaults for adjustments, pushes it on TOP of the stack, selects it, updateUI, render. Tool stays the same (does not switch to Select). Afterwards drawCanvas=null, isDrawing=false, drawPoints=[], render().
rows.quirks: Layer creation is async (img.onload), so nextId is assigned later and an undo between mouseup and load could race. makeLayer is called with name fallback 'Drawing '+(nextId+1) which is unused since a name is always passed. Layer id consumed in onload. Newly drawn layer is selected but handles are not shown until user switches to Select.
rows.portTarget: Autocrop on SKBitmap pixels (alpha>0 scan, pad 10, clamp), SKBitmap.Extract; layer model owns SKBitmap directly (no data URL round trip). Add layer synchronously.
rows.parityCheck: After a stroke the layer count is +1, the new layer is selected and topmost, it is named per 4.1 (Tools.DrawingName) and the tool is unchanged (LedgerScenarioTests, CanvasInteractionTests); its origin, size and pixels are Tools.CommitDrawing's, held to 4.1 by GoldenAppTests shape-* scenes (M2a).

rows.name: Nothing drawn means no layer
rows.behavior: If the alpha scan finds no non-zero alpha (click with no movement, pure transparent), no layer is added/erased and drawCanvas is discarded; the earlier saveUndo snapshot remains.
rows.quirks: See draw-tool-start (wasted undo entry).
rows.portTarget: Same alpha scan.
rows.parityCheck: A click without movement with Line, Rect, Ellipse or the Eraser leaves the layer count and the undo count unchanged (CanvasInteractionTests.A_shape_click_draws_nothing_and_records_nothing, Eraser_click_without_move_changes_nothing_and_records_no_step; LedgerScenarioTests S4, S5); a stroke that leaves no pixels adds no layer (Tools.CommitDrawing returns null). Reworded in M3b: a Pen click draws a brush-size dot (approved divergence draw-pen-single-click).

rows.name: Mouse released or left outside canvas while drawing
rows.behavior: Only the select tool is handled by onmouseleave. For draw tools, leaving the canvas does nothing; mouseup outside the canvas element is not delivered, so isDrawing stays true. Re-entering the canvas continues the stroke from the old path (lineTo to the new point draws a straight connecting segment) even with the button up, and the next mouseup commits it. Pressing mousedown again while stuck would start a new saveUndo and replace drawCanvas, discarding the stuck stroke.
rows.quirks: Known bug class: 'phantom stroke' after dragging out of the window. Not likely relied on by users.
rows.portTarget: Use Mouse.Capture on MouseDown and release on MouseUp so the stroke commits reliably. This differs from Electron: choose and document (recommended fix).
rows.parityCheck: Reworded to the fixed behavior: a Line drag released outside the window is committed as one layer, and moving back over the canvas with the button up draws nothing (bridge H4; CanvasInteractionTests, TemplateCanvasHostTests). Narrowed in M4a: the gesture is real WPF routed input injected in-process by the test-only input bridge (brg smoke; interfaces R7, R8) and read back through its inspect command and UI Automation; the bridge cannot show the OS cursor image or drive a physical device (H4).
rows.divergence: 4.1: Releasing outside the canvas leaves a phantom stroke that resumes on re-entry. v5: Mouse capture on left button commits the stroke at release even outside the canvas.

rows.name: Tool switch during a stroke
rows.behavior: Tool keys/buttons are not blocked while isDrawing (keyboard shortcuts work while mouse held). currentTool changing mid-stroke changes which branch mouseup/mousemove take (e.g. switching pen to select leaves drawCanvas orphaned: select branch of mouseup returns early so isDrawing/drawCanvas stay set and the live preview keeps showing in render until next draw tool mouseup).
rows.quirks: Orphaned preview bug.
rows.portTarget: Cancel the in-progress stroke when the tool changes (fix) or replicate.
rows.parityCheck: Hold mouse, press V: Electron leaves preview lingering; native must match chosen behavior.
rows.divergence: 4.1: Switching tools mid-stroke orphans the live preview. v5: The in-progress stroke is cancelled cleanly when the tool changes.

rows.name: Brush color, size, fill controls and defaults
rows.behavior: Defaults: drawColor '#17d4fa' (color input), drawSize 4 (range 1..50, width 60px), drawFill false (checkbox 'Fill'). Color and size apply to the NEXT stroke (pen reads at mousedown, shapes read live each move). Size slider also updates the eraser ring cursor. Fill only affects rect and ellipse. Not part of undo snapshot and not saved in project files (verify in project save).
rows.quirks: Color input is opaque only (no alpha). Shapes read drawColor live during the drag, so changing color mid-drag affects the shape but not an in-progress pen path whose strokeStyle was fixed at mousedown.
rows.portTarget: WPF: color picker (e.g. ColorPicker control or button + dialog), Slider Min=1 Max=50 Value=4, CheckBox 'Fill'. Bind to a BrushSettings view model.
rows.parityCheck: BrushViewModelTests: the defaults (#17d4fa, 4, off) and the size clamp 1..50; compared side by side in the M3b look sign-off (state 04).

rows.name: Wheel in Select tool scales selected layer
rows.behavior: preventDefault always (canvas never scrolls the page). If tool is select and a layer is selected: delta = deltaY>0 ? 0.95 : 1.05 (any deltaY<=0 including 0 grows); scale=max(0.01, scale*delta); updateUI(); render(). Scales about the layer's top-left (x,y unchanged), not the center. No modifiers, no undo snapshot, no upper bound. One event = one 5% step regardless of delta magnitude (trackpads fire many).
rows.quirks: Asymmetric steps (0.95 vs 1.05) so up-down does not return to the original scale. Scaling anchors at top-left, so the layer drifts visually (center moves), unlike corner-drag resize which keeps the center. High-resolution wheels/trackpads on WPF raise many small Delta events; Electron deltaY for those also fires many events; match per-event not per-notch. deltaY===0 (horizontal scroll) grows 5%.
rows.portTarget: MouseWheel e.Delta: Delta<0 (wheel down) means shrink 0.95, else grow 1.05; handle e.Handled = true. Per-event step, not per-120-unit, to match.
rows.parityCheck: Reworded to the fixed behavior: one notch up scales x1.05 about the center and one down returns; ten notches down then ten up return to the start scale with the center unchanged (4.1 ends near 0.9794 s); 200 fast notches stop at 500% (bridge H3; SelectionGeometryTests, LedgerScenarioTests). Narrowed in M4a: the gesture is real WPF routed input injected in-process by the test-only input bridge (brg smoke; interfaces R7, R8) and read back through its inspect command and UI Automation; the bridge cannot show the OS cursor image or drive a physical device (H3).
rows.divergence: 4.1: Wheel scales about the top-left with asymmetric 0.95/1.05 steps and no upper bound. v5: Wheel scaling is centered with symmetric steps under the single 1%-500% scale clamp.

rows.name: Wheel with draw tools changes brush size
rows.behavior: For any tool other than select (pen, line, rect, circle, eraser): drawSize=max(1,min(50, drawSize + (deltaY>0 ? -1 : 1))); slider value synced; updateCursor() redraws the eraser ring. Wheel up = bigger, down = smaller, 1 px per event, no modifier needed. No render call.
rows.quirks: During an active stroke the new size does not affect the pen path already started (lineWidth set at mousedown) but does affect shapes on next move. deltaY===0 counts as up (+1).
rows.portTarget: Same, update Slider.Value and eraser cursor.
rows.parityCheck: From 4, 20 wheel-up steps give 24 and 60 more give 50 (clamped); wheel-down clamps at 1 (ToolsTests.StepBrushSize, BrushViewModelTests, LedgerScenarioTests).

rows.name: Eraser ring cursor
rows.behavior: Cursor image = SVG with a ring radius r=max(4,min(120, drawSize*zoom/2)), svg size d=ceil(r)*2+4, hotspot at center; layers: black 3px stroke at 0.5 opacity, magenta #f22f89 1.5px dashed (4 3) ring, 1.5px magenta center dot. Fallback 'crosshair'. Updates on tool change, brush size change, wheel, and every render.
rows.quirks: Cap of r=120 means brush ring understates size beyond 240 px on screen (size 50 at zoom 3 = 150 px diameter so never reached with current ranges). Min r=4 overstates size 1-8 brushes at low zoom.
rows.portTarget: Generate an SKBitmap/WPF Cursor (via CreateIconIndirect/ CUR stream) per size, or hide system cursor and draw the ring as an overlay on the canvas at the mouse position.
rows.parityCheck: Through the bridge (H5): the ring diameter equals size x zoom DIPs at zoom 0.25 and 3, with no 240 cap (amended to fix in M3b); CanvasCursorsTests. Reworded in M4a: the bridge reads the cursor the canvas sets (TemplateCanvasHost.CanvasCursor and its WPF cursor) after routed hover and drag input; the OS cursor image is not observable to automation, and CanvasCursorsTests pin the WPF cursors and the ring bitmap (H5).
rows.divergence: 4.1: the ring radius is max(4, min(120, drawSize x zoom / 2)) CSS px, an SVG cursor that is not redrawn on zoom (editor.js:443-454). v5: the ring is the true brush footprint, max(4, size x zoom / 2) DIPs, drawn at device pixels and redrawn on zoom, tool and size changes; the Win32 cursor-size cap is stated on cursor-eraser.

rows.name: Eraser commit: erase from selected layer through inverse transform
rows.behavior: On mouseup with eraser and non-empty mask: requires getSelected() with img, else alert('Select a layer to erase from, then try again.'). Otherwise erased = applyEraseStroke(sel.img, sel, drawCanvas, createCanvas) returns a new imgW x imgH canvas; a new Image is made from erased.toDataURL() and on load replaces sel.img, invalidates the RGB shift cache (_rgbCache.layerId=null), updateUI, render. Erase applies to the selected layer even if hidden or the layer is under other layers; erased pixels are permanent in that layer's own bitmap (image dimensions unchanged). Layers sharing the same Image object (clones from Allover/F+B etc.) are unaffected because only sel.img is swapped.
rows.quirks: Alert is a blocking OS dialog (port: MessageBox). The erase mask is drawn via drawImage with default bilinear smoothing under scale/rotate, so stroke edges are resampled (soft). Erasing in a stroke that does not touch the layer still rewrites the bitmap and costs an undo step. Erase result is async (image load) so undo immediately after could race. Eraser ignores layer opacity/adjustments (works on source bitmap).
rows.portTarget: SKCanvas: create imgW x imgH mask bitmap; apply matrix inverse of render transform; DrawBitmap(stroke); then new layer bitmap = copy of source with SKBlendMode.DstOut mask drawn at identity. Replace layer.Bitmap (clone before mutation so shared bitmaps are not erased in other layers).
rows.parityCheck: GoldenAppTests erase-* scenes (M2a) on scaled, rotated and flipped layers against 4.1's frozen exports; EraserTests for the single-stroke production path; LedgerScenarioTests: the eraser acts on the selected layer only, hidden or not, as one undo step. Narrowed in M3b: the production path's fringe divergence is the one this row states (M2a Task 6 measurement).
rows.divergence: 4.1: the eraser re-strokes its whole path on every mousemove, so the antialiased fringe of a drag of three or more points is erased more the more mouse events the drag produced. v5: the eraser path is stroked once (the eraser half of draw-pen-incremental-stroke); fully covered pixels and two-point drags erase identically, and only that fringe keeps slightly more alpha (measured in M2a Task 6; GoldenAppTests replays 4.1's stroking against the frozen goldens).

rows.name: lib/erase.js inverse-transform and destination-out details
rows.behavior: w=imgW*scale, cx=x+w/2, cy=y+h/2, rad=rotation deg to rad (|| 0). Mask canvas (imgW x imgH) CTM built in order: translate(imgW/2,imgH/2) scale(1/s,1/s) scale(flipH?-1:1, flipV?-1:1) rotate(-rad) translate(-cx,-cy), then drawImage(strokeCanvas,0,0). Stroke pixels use plain source-over into the mask (stroke alpha preserved). Then out = copy of source; globalCompositeOperation destination-out; drawImage(mask,0,0) at identity; back to source-over. Erase amount is proportional to mask alpha: dest alpha *= (1 - maskA). Doc notes @napi-rs/canvas 1.0.2 mishandles transformed destination-out so two-step form is required. Render transform is translate(c) rotate flip scale draw; flips applied after rotate.
rows.quirks: The stroke canvas is TW x TH opaque magenta; only its alpha matters. Scale = 0 would divide by zero but scale is clamped at >=0.01 (project load could still deliver 0 - guard).
rows.portTarget: Port as SKMatrix concat in the same order; use two-step compositing with SKBlendMode.DstOut at identity. Reuse tests/erase.test.js fixtures as golden vectors if present.
rows.parityCheck: Golden pixel fixtures from the existing node:test suite for erase (tests dir); also check premultiplied alpha rounding: DstOut on premul bitmap vs Canvas2D should match within 1 level.

rows.name: Eraser operates on selection, not on topmost under cursor
rows.behavior: Photoshop-style: eraser affects only the currently selected layer, chosen beforehand. Selecting via the Select tool then switching tool (key E or button) retains selection. After erasing, the layer stays selected. With no selection: strokes are drawn as magenta preview and then rejected with the alert after release (stroke lost).
rows.quirks: The user draws a whole stroke before learning nothing is selected (and a no-op undo entry exists).
rows.portTarget: Same rules. Consider disabling the tool when no selection, but alert behavior must match for parity.
rows.parityCheck: Eraser with no selection: the press shows the status message 'Select a layer to erase from, then try again.' (editor.js:1270), starts no stroke and changes nothing (LedgerScenarioTests, CanvasInteractionTests). Reworded in M3b to the fixed behavior: a status message at the press replaces 4.1's alert after the stroke.
rows.divergence: 4.1: Eraser with no selection lets the user draw a whole stroke, then alerts and loses it. v5: Eraser refuses on mousedown with a status message when no layer is selected.

rows.name: Zoom buttons and label
rows.behavior: State zoom default 1. zoomIn: min(3, zoom+0.25); zoomOut: max(0.25, zoom-0.25); steps of 0.25 between 0.25 and 3.0 (12 levels). Label text '(zoom*100)+"%"' e.g. '100%', '125%', '25%'. Each click calls render() which resizes the canvas to TW*zoom x TH*zoom (assigning canvas.width resets state). No wheel zoom, no Ctrl+wheel, no keyboard zoom, no fit-to-window. Zoom is not in undo, not saved in project, resets to 100% on launch. imageSmoothingEnabled=(zoom<1): below 100% the composite is downscaled smoothly, at or above 100% scaled with nearest neighbor (crisp pixels). Checkerboard (16px, #0f1f31 with #050c18 8px squares) fills at zoom scale... pattern is created on the zoomed canvas so squares do not scale with zoom.
rows.quirks: Zoom buttons have no disabled state at limits. The canvas is resized on every render (flicker risk in WPF if done naively). Checkerboard cell size is constant on screen, not tied to template. Hit radii and handles are in screen px so UI feels the same at all zooms.
rows.portTarget: ScaleTransform or explicit surface size; draw offscreen composite to view with SKSamplingOptions: Nearest when zoom>=1, linear/mipmap when <1. Checkerboard via SKShader.CreateBitmap with Repeat tiling in screen space (not scaled).
rows.parityCheck: Zoom label text for all 12 levels (CanvasViewModelTests); the engine view goldens at zoom 0.25, 1 and 3 (GoldenViewTests) pixel-match 4.1 within tolerance. Narrowed in M3a: no window screenshot is diffed; the smoothing filter below 100% is the engine's, pinned by those goldens.

rows.name: Mask checkbox (default on)
rows.behavior: showMask default true (checkbox checked). When on, render() applies destination-in with maskCanvas (white rects for each active-mode region) to the composited art, so everything outside the 18 region rectangles is transparent (shows checkerboard). When off, art outside regions is visible in the preview. Export ALWAYS applies the mask regardless of this checkbox. Toggling re-renders, no undo entry (but IS captured in undo snapshots and project files). Mask is rebuilt on mode switch (buildMask).
rows.quirks: Preview with Mask off does not match the export (WYSIWYG break; keep or add a warning).
rows.portTarget: SKBlendMode.DstIn with a mask SKBitmap built from region rects (or clip to union path; rects are pixel-aligned so a clip is equivalent). CheckBox bound to ShowMask.
rows.parityCheck: A layer placed outside every region: hidden in the view with Mask on, shown with it off, and the exported PNG hides it either way; each toggle is one undo step (LedgerScenarioTests, SettingsGroupTests, view goldens with Mask on and off). Narrowed in M3a: the layer is placed, not dragged; dragging lands with M3b's select tool.
rows.divergence: 4.1: toggling Mask re-renders without an undo step, though showMask is in every undo snapshot and project file, so a later Undo of an unrelated edit flips it back (editor.js:1494, :1404-1415, :1432-1436). v5: each Mask toggle is exactly one undo step.

rows.name: Grid checkbox (default off) region outlines
rows.behavior: showGrid default false. When on, after compositing, strokes every active region rect with rgba(255,255,0,0.3), lineWidth 1 (screen px), at (x*zoom,y*zoom,w*zoom,h*zoom) on the zoomed view canvas, above art but below selection handles. Pure overlay, not exported. Toggle re-renders; captured by undo and project files. Strokes at integer coordinates produce blurry 2px lines at zoom 1 (half-pixel AA) as in Canvas2D.
rows.quirks: Grid draws region rects of the current mode (variable named SHIRT_REGIONS even in pants mode).
rows.portTarget: SKPaint stroke 1px, color 0x4DFFFF00 (alpha 0.3 -> 76/255), DrawRect on integer coords reproduces the same AA half coverage; keep coords unshifted.
rows.parityCheck: View goldens: the grid lines in Shirt and in Pants at zoom 1 match 4.1 under the golden rule; the export with Grid on equals the export with Grid off; each toggle is one undo step (LedgerScenarioTests, SettingsGroupTests). Narrowed in M3a: zoom 2 not captured.
rows.divergence: 4.1: toggling Grid re-renders without an undo step, though showGrid is in every undo snapshot and project file, so a later Undo of an unrelated edit flips it back (editor.js:1495, :1404-1415, :1432-1436). v5: each Grid toggle is exactly one undo step.

rows.name: Undo/redo snapshot model and stack discipline
rows.behavior: lib/history.js createHistory(limit default 30; editor passes 30). undoStack holds PRIOR states (snapshot before mutation). push(snapshot): append, drop oldest (shift) if length>limit, clear redoStack. undo(current): if empty return null; push current onto redo, pop and return top undo. redo(current): mirror. canUndo/canRedo/sizes. The editor calls saveUndo() BEFORE each mutation, and history stores opaque JSON strings. Max 30 undoable steps; redo discarded by any new snapshot push.
rows.quirks: A snapshot pushed by saveUndo() that precedes a no-op still consumes one of 30 steps (see draw-tool-start). Because redo parking happens at undo time using a fresh snapshotState(), changes made via non-undoable mutations (drags) are folded into the states silently.
rows.portTarget: Port createHistory as a generic History<T> class; copy the node:test cases (tests for history) as xUnit tests for exact stack parity.
rows.parityCheck: Port the history unit tests; sequence push x35 -> only 30 undo steps; push after undo clears redo; undo on empty returns null/no-op.

rows.name: What a snapshot captures (and what it does not)
rows.behavior: snapshotState serializes JSON: mode (Shirt/Pants), bgColor, bgOpacity, bgImageSrc (data/URL of background image or null), regionColors (shallow copy; fill descriptors or legacy colors), showMask, showGrid, and every layer's properties (all fields via spread: id, name, visible, opacity, x, y, scale, rotation, flipH, flipV, brightness, contrast, saturate, hueRotate, rShift, gShift, bShift, plus any extra) with img replaced by imgSrc = img.src. NOT captured: selectedLayerId, currentTool, brush color/size/fill, currentFill editor config, zoom, export title, assetType beyond mode, Word Art / UI panel state, keyboard-toggle state, nextId.
rows.quirks: Every snapshot embeds each layer's full PNG data URL: 30 snapshots x N layers can be hundreds of MB (memory blow-up risk in Electron; native design with shared bitmaps removes it). Images loaded from object URLs/blob URLs (if any) would not survive restore; check how Add image creates src (data URL vs blob).
rows.portTarget: Immutable snapshot record: list of layer records referencing shared immutable bitmap objects (copy-on-write, no re-encoding), plus bg fields and region fills. Do not serialize pixels per snapshot.
