Controls and defaults: waText textarea rows=2, prefilled 'RIZZ', placeholder 'Type text...', vertically resizable, min-height 36px, width 150px, Enter inserts newline (multiline supported); waFont select width 150px default first option Anton; waColor (Fill) #17d4fa; waStroke (Stroke) #000000; waColor2 (Grad) #f22f89; waSize number default 64 min 8 max 300 (min/max are only HTML hints, typed values outside range are NOT clamped); waStrokeW range 0-20 default 3; waAngle range 0-360 default 0. Style buttons (3-col grid): Solid (active at start), Gradient, Neon, Shadow, Outline, Retro. Ribbon group labels: 'Text', 'Colors & Size', 'Style', 'Preview'. Module state waStyle='solid'. Preview canvas #waPreview attr 200x60 inside black (#000) box with 1px #333 border, radius 4, min-height 44, content centered, overflow hidden. 'Add to canvas' primary button full width under preview.
rows.quirks: Size min/max not enforced on typing: 0 or empty falls back to 64 via `+value || 64`; 5000 is accepted and can create a giant canvas. Decide: clamp to 8-300 in native (deliberate fix) and document.
rows.portTarget: WPF Ribbon/TabItem 'Text' with TextBox (AcceptsReturn, MinLines=2, VerticalScrollBar, resizable via GridSplitter or Thumb), ComboBox of 15 fonts, three color pickers (use a shared ColorPicker control matching the existing fill-style pickers), IntegerUpDown/NumericUpDown for size, two Sliders (0-20, 0-360), six RadioButton/ToggleButton styled group bound to enum WordArtStyle. ViewModel record WordArtSettings with the defaults above.
rows.parityCheck: Launch fresh: assert every control's initial value equals the table above; Solid is the only active style; preview shows 'RIZZ' in Anton cyan with 3px black stroke.
rows.divergence: 4.1: Word Art size is not clamped, so 0 falls back to 64 and 5000 makes a giant canvas. v5: size clamped to 8-300 (unintended, named divergence).

rows.name: Word Art font list (15 fonts) and display labels
rows.behavior: Option value -> label: Anton -> 'Anton (Block)'; Bebas Neue -> 'Bebas Neue (Tall)'; Dancing Script -> 'Dancing Script'; Great Vibes -> 'Great Vibes'; Pacifico -> 'Pacifico (Retro)'; Creepster -> 'Creepster'; Poppins -> 'Poppins (Bold)'; Lato -> 'Lato (Modern)'; Bangers -> 'Bangers (Comic)'; Permanent Marker -> 'Permanent Marker'; Bungee Shade -> 'Bungee Shade (3D)'; Rubik Mono One -> 'Rubik Mono'; Press Start 2P -> 'Press Start 2P'; Righteous -> 'Righteous'; Orbitron -> 'Orbitron (Cyber)'. Font is applied as CSS `900 <size>px "<family>", sans-serif`. The dropdown items are not rendered in their own typeface.
rows.quirks: Weight is always 900. Single-weight fonts (Anton, Bebas Neue, Pacifico, Creepster, Bangers, Permanent Marker, Bungee Shade, Rubik Mono One, Press Start 2P, Righteous, Great Vibes) get Chromium synthetic (faux) bold; Dancing Script maps 900 -> its 700 file; Poppins/Lato/Orbitron use true 900. To match the existing look natively you must emulate faux bold (SKFont.Embolden = true) for the 400-only fonts, else text is thinner than today. Decide keep (match) vs fix. Offline Electron users silently get sans-serif; native fixes this deliberately.
rows.portTarget: Bundle all 15 TTF/OTF files (OFL licensed) as Content in the MSIX; load via SKTypeface.FromStream / SKFontManager.CreateTypeface at startup into a Dictionary<string,SKTypeface>. Poppins 700+900, Lato 900, Orbitron 700+900, Dancing Script 700 are variable/weights; the rest are single-weight 400 files. Fallback typeface = system sans (Segoe UI).
rows.parityCheck: For each of the 15 fonts render 'RIZZ' solid and compare against the Electron reference output (online, fonts loaded) with the pixel-diff harness; tolerate edge-AA only. Verify offline launch renders the real fonts (unlike Electron).

rows.name: Font load timing and initial preview
rows.behavior: On script load, if document.fonts.ready exists the preview is rendered once after it resolves; otherwise a 1000ms setTimeout. Until then the preview canvas is the blank 200x60 element. Preview also re-renders on every input/change of the 8 controls and on style-button click.
rows.quirks: In Electron, document.fonts.ready only waits for fonts already requested; fonts used only by canvas are not requested until first draw, so first render with a not-yet-downloaded font draws fallback sans-serif and is NOT re-rendered when the font arrives (stale preview and potentially a fallback-font layer if Add is clicked immediately). Native bundling removes this; do not replicate.
rows.portTarget: Fonts are local, so render preview synchronously in the ViewModel constructor after settings load; no readiness gate needed. Use a debounced invalidate (or immediate, rendering is cheap) on property change.
rows.parityCheck: App start shows RIZZ preview on first frame; no blank preview state.
rows.divergence: 4.1: first preview or Add can render in a fallback font because canvas-only fonts are fetched lazily and never re-rendered. v5: bundled fonts render synchronously with no readiness gate.

rows.name: renderWordArt layout: measure, line height, padding, canvas size
rows.behavior: text = waText || 'TEXT' (empty string -> 'TEXT'); lines = text.split('\n'); fontSize = +waSize || 64; lineHeight = fontSize*1.15; totalW = max measureText(line).width over lines using the 900 font; totalH = lines*lineHeight. pad = max(strokeW*2, neon?30:10, shadow?15:0, retro?12:0) (so base pad 10 for every style incl. solid/gradient/outline; neon 30; shadow 15; retro 12; stroke width 6+ can exceed these). cw = ceil(totalW+2*pad); ch = ceil(totalH+2*pad). Target canvas set to min(cw,maxW) x min(ch,maxH) when max given (preview 200x80), else full cw x ch. Uniform scale sc = min(width/cw, height/ch). clearRect, scale(sc), textAlign center, textBaseline 'middle'. Center x = cw/2; first line y = pad + lineHeight/2; each subsequent +lineHeight. Returns {cw,ch}.
rows.quirks: Preview: when only one dimension is clamped (e.g., cw<200 but ch>80) canvas width stays cw while content is scaled by height only, so the content is left-aligned inside a wider canvas (it only looks centered because the flex wrapper centers the canvas). Whitespace-only text is truthy and renders blank. Widths from measureText ignore stroke/shadow/glow; pad covers them only approximately (heavy neon blur can clip at 40px blur on pad 30). Trailing newline produces an empty last line that still adds lineHeight.
rows.portTarget: Port as a pure function WordArtRenderer.Render(settings, maxW?, maxH?) -> SKBitmap + (cw,ch). Use SKFont.MeasureText for widths. 'middle' baseline in Chromium = em-box middle ((ascent-descent)/2 offset using font metrics); replicate with y_baseline = ty + (font.Metrics.Ascent... ) so glyphs sit at the same vertical position (compute from font metrics: baseline = ty - (ascent+descent)/2 where ascent negative in Skia convention, verify empirically against Electron reference).
rows.parityCheck: WordArtTests.Canvas_size_is_4_1s_cw_by_ch, Lines_are_shaped_to_chromiums_measureText_width, Middle_baseline_is_the_normalized_typo_metrics_in_layout_units, The_preview_clamps_the_canvas_and_scales_the_content; the frozen Word Art goldens, 6 styles in Anton, Poppins and Dancing Script, multi-line in Orbitron (wordart-multiline-orbitron), under GoldenRule.AssertWordArtMatches (WordArtSwapTests, WordArtRatchetTests). Narrowed in M4b, as M2b's Word Art rows: multi-line is captured in one font and style only.

rows.name: Style: Solid (fill then optional stroke then refill)
rows.behavior: fillStyle=waColor; fillText at (cx, ty). If strokeW>0: strokeStyle=waStroke, lineWidth=strokeW, lineJoin='round', strokeText, then fillText again on top (so stroke shows only outside the glyph, effectively half its width). strokeW==0 -> fill only. Stroke color default black, width default 3.
rows.quirks: Stroke is drawn centered on the outline then fill is repainted over the inner half. Note stroke width slider shares the same value for Solid/Gradient/Shadow/Retro and Outline.
rows.portTarget: SKPaint fill pass, then SKPaint Stroke style (StrokeJoin=Round, StrokeWidth=strokeW) via canvas.DrawText or path from SKFont.GetTextPath for exact outline, then fill pass again. Default stroke cap = Butt (Canvas default) and miter limit 10 for non-round joins is irrelevant since join is round.
rows.parityCheck: Goldens: 'RIZZ' cyan fill, stroke 3 black in Anton, Poppins and Dancing Script, 'NO/CAP' Orbitron at stroke 3, and Anton at stroke 12 white; stroke 0 by WordArtTests.Solid_with_stroke_width_0_draws_no_stroke. Narrowed in M2b: stroke 20 not captured.

rows.name: Style: Gradient (per-line linear gradient fill + angle slider)
rows.behavior: For each line: gx = cos(angle)*cw/2, gy = sin(angle)*ch/2 (angle = waAngle degrees -> radians); linear gradient from (cx-gx, ty-gy) to (cx+gx, ty+gy), stop 0 = waColor (Fill), stop 1 = waColor2 (Grad). Used as fill in the Solid path (including stroke redraw with same gradient). Angle 0 = left-to-right across the whole canvas width; 90 = top-to-bottom spanning half the canvas height each side of the line's center.
rows.quirks: Gradient vector uses ellipse semantics (cw/2 and ch/2 independently), so 45 degrees is NOT a true 45-degree gradient on non-square canvases. Gradient is recomputed per line centered on that line, so multi-line text repeats the gradient per line. Keep for parity; angle slider only affects Gradient style (ignored by others). Colors2 also used by Retro.
rows.portTarget: SKShader.CreateLinearGradient(p0, p1, [c1,c2], null, SKShaderTileMode.Clamp) in local (pre-scale) coordinates, applied to the fill paint; the preview scale transform applies on top via canvas.Scale(sc).
rows.parityCheck: Goldens wordart-gradient-{anton,poppins,dancing} at angle 0 and wordart-gradient-135-poppins; WordArtTests.Gradient_endpoints_scale_each_axis_by_its_own_half_extent pins the endpoint math at 0, 45, 90, 180, 270 on a 300x100 canvas. Narrowed in M2b: no pixel golden at 45, 90, 180 or 270.

rows.name: Style: Neon glow
rows.behavior: For each line: save; shadowColor=waColor; shadowBlur=20; fillStyle=waColor; fillText; shadowBlur=40; fillText again; shadowBlur=0; restore. Then fillStyle '#fff', globalAlpha 0.8, fillText (white inner core) and globalAlpha reset to 1. The stroke width and stroke color are ignored in Neon. pad=30.
rows.quirks: Canvas shadowBlur scales with the canvas transform? (No: shadowBlur is NOT affected by the current transform in Canvas2D) so in the 200x80 preview, where scale(sc) is applied, the glow stays 20/40px in device pixels and looks relatively larger than in the full-size output. Preview is therefore not WYSIWYG for Neon/Shadow offset behavior; Shadow offset (4,4) is a normal path coordinate and does scale. Decide: keep (matches today's preview) or compute shadow sigma in scaled space for true WYSIWYG.
rows.portTarget: SKPaint with ImageFilter = SKImageFilter.CreateDropShadowOnly(0,0,sigma,sigma,color) or MaskFilter blur. Canvas shadowBlur B maps to Gaussian sigma = B/2, so sigma 10 and 20; draw shadow-and-content (CreateDropShadow with dx=dy=0), twice. Then white pass with alpha 204 (0.8*255).
rows.parityCheck: Pixel-diff neon render against Electron (note GPU vs software canvas differs slightly, tolerate <=3 levels); verify glow extent not clipped differently.

rows.name: Style: Shadow
rows.behavior: Before the Solid fill/stroke path, draws the line in rgba(0,0,0,0.6) offset (+4,+4) with fillText (no blur). Then normal fill and optional stroke on top. pad=15.
rows.quirks: Shadow is a fill only (no stroke shadow), so with a thick stroke the shadow appears smaller than the stroked glyph.
rows.portTarget: SKPaint Color=(0,0,0,153); DrawText at (cx+4, ty+4) before the main passes.
rows.parityCheck: Golden diff for Shadow style; offset exactly 4 px in unscaled space.

rows.name: Style: Outline (hollow, stroked in the Fill color)
rows.behavior: strokeStyle = waColor (Fill, not Stroke color), lineWidth = strokeW || 3 (strokeW 0 falls back to 3), lineJoin round, strokeText only; no fill so the interior is transparent. Stroke color picker and gradient are ignored. pad=max(strokeW*2,10).
rows.quirks: Zero stroke width silently becomes 3. Add-to-canvas result has transparent interior so the template shows through.
rows.portTarget: SKPaint Style=Stroke, StrokeWidth=(strokeW==0?3:strokeW), StrokeJoin=Round, color waColor; draw text path.
rows.parityCheck: Goldens wordart-outline-{anton,poppins,dancing} at strokeW 3 and wordart-outline-stroke-0-dancing (0 renders as 3px); WordArtTests.Outline_with_stroke_width_0_draws_at_3 pins the 0 to 3 mapping. Narrowed in M2b: strokeW 12 not captured.

rows.name: Style: Retro stacked 3D
rows.behavior: For i = 8 down to 1: fillStyle = (i even) ? waStroke : waColor2 ; fillText at (cx+i, ty+i). Result: 8 diagonal stacked copies alternating Stroke-color (i=8,6,4,2) and Grad-color (i=7,5,3,1), with the deepest at +8,+8. Then the normal Solid fill (waColor) and optional stroke at the base position. pad=12.
rows.quirks: Retro silently uses the Grad and Stroke color pickers as extrusion colors; the stroke picker therefore doubles as extrusion color even when strokeW=0.
rows.portTarget: Loop of SKCanvas.DrawText with solid paints at integer offsets then main passes.
rows.parityCheck: Diff Retro render; confirm color alternation order (i=8 stroke color is the bottom-most).

rows.name: Word Art glyph rasterization (antialiased glyph edges)
rows.behavior: renderWordArt draws its text with fillText and strokeText (editor.js:2166-2236) in the font '900 <size>px "<family>", sans-serif' (editor.js:2131-2132). Chromium on Windows rasterizes those glyphs through DirectWrite with ClearType-style coverage: 87 to 184 distinct coverage levels in a fill-only render, and horizontal spreading at stems.
rows.quirks: Measured 2026-10-14 on the 22 frozen Word Art goldens: under the unchanged golden rule every scene fails on glyph edges only (largest edge delta 79). Interior differences are 0 on 21 scenes, and 7 pixels of one level on wordart-outline-anton (x=314, y=147..153). Swapping 4.1's own Word Art bitmap into the engine document matches all 22 goldens exactly.
rows.portTarget: WordArt draws HarfBuzz-shaped text blobs with the SkFont Chromium's canvas uses (Fonts.CreateFont). SkiaSharp 4.153.1 exposes no font-manager choice, text gamma or contrast, so its glyph coverage differs from DirectWrite's. Exact parity would need DirectWrite glyph-run analysis through COM interop, which M2b does not take.
rows.parityCheck: GoldenAppTests holds the 22 Word Art scenes to GoldenRule.AssertWordArtMatches: same size, every interior pixel within 1 level per channel, edge pixels unbounded. WordArtSwapTests swaps 4.1's own Word Art bitmap (tests/goldens/app/wordart-ref) into the engine document and requires an exact match under the unchanged GoldenRule.
rows.divergence: 4.1: Chromium rasterizes Word Art glyphs through DirectWrite with ClearType-style coverage. v5: SkiaSharp's rasterizer smooths glyph edges differently; interiors match within 1 level, layout and placement match exactly (pinned by the 4.1-bitmap swap test). The engine bitmap is also held to per-scene ceilings by WordArtRatchetTests against tests/goldens/app/wordart-ref, and ceilings move only by a logged update.

rows.name: Live preview wiring
rows.behavior: updateWordArtPreview() calls renderWordArt(#waPreview, 200, 80). Triggered by input AND change events on waText, waFont, waColor, waStroke, waSize, waStrokeW, waColor2, waAngle (every keystroke / slider tick), by style button click, and once after fonts ready. Preview canvas background transparent over black panel.
rows.quirks: Preview is rendered at device pixel resolution into a 200x80 canvas (no devicePixelRatio handling) so it is soft on HiDPI; native can render at DPI but then does not byte-match; parity tolerance applies to the full-resolution output only.
rows.portTarget: Bind SKElement (SKXamlCanvas / SkiaSharp.Views.WPF SKElement) invalidated by property-changed on WordArtSettings; render at 200x80 max, same uniform-scale logic, black background.
rows.parityCheck: Change each control; preview updates immediately (<100ms) and matches full render downscaled.
rows.divergence: 4.1: the preview renders into a 200x80 canvas with no devicePixelRatio handling, so it is soft above 100% display scale. v5: it renders at device pixels and shows at the same size in DIPs, sharp at 125% and above; parity applies to the full-resolution output only (M4b, T2, run 2 D5).

rows.name: Add to canvas: full-resolution render and new layer
rows.behavior: Click #btnAddWordArt: saveUndo(); render at full size (no maxW/maxH -> canvas = cw x ch) to PNG data URL; load as Image; then create a layer (not via addLayer): id=nextId++, name = '✨ ' + text.substring(0,20) + ' [' + fontName + ']' (text = waText || 'TEXT'), visible true, opacity 1, scale = min(torso_front.w/img.w, torso_front.h/img.h)*0.85 where torso_front is current mode's region (Shirt 128x128 at 231,74 / Pants region per mode), x/y centered in torso_front, rotation 0, flips false, brightness/contrast/saturate 100, hueRotate 0, r/g/bShift 0. Pushes onto top of layers, selects it, setTool('select'), updateUI(), render().
rows.quirks: Name embeds raw newlines for multi-line text (up to 20 chars including newline) and the font family, not its display label. Layer is added asynchronously after image decode (undo snapshot is taken first). In 'Pants' mode the placement uses pants SHIRT_REGIONS.torso_front (the variable name is stale; check PANTS_REGION_DATA.torso_front exists). The code first sets canvas to 1024x512 and renders twice (first call result unused except dimensions); native needs only one pass. Very large size x long text can exceed canvas limits and fail silently (empty/failed toDataURL); native should cap bitmap size.
rows.portTarget: Command AddWordArtCommand: push undo snapshot, render SKBitmap, wrap as the layer's image (keep as SKBitmap/SKImage; no need to PNG round trip but must PNG-encode when saving project), LayerFactory with identical defaults, select, switch tool to Select, refresh layer list, invalidate canvas.
rows.parityCheck: Script: default settings, click Add; assert layer count +1, name '✨ RIZZ [Anton]', scale/x/y numeric equality with Electron within 1e-6, selection and tool state, undo removes it in one step.

rows.name: Word Art edge cases and invalid input
rows.behavior: Empty text -> 'TEXT'. Size non-numeric/0 -> 64. Style buttons are mutually exclusive (single active class, set on click only). Font select always has a valid value. Color inputs always valid hex. strokeW=0 disables stroke for Solid/Gradient/Shadow/Retro; Outline forces 3. Angle only used by Gradient. No persistence: word art settings are NOT saved in .r15proj nor remembered between sessions; only the rendered raster layer persists.
rows.quirks: No way to re-edit word art after adding (it is a raster layer). Keep.
rows.portTarget: Unit tests on WordArtRenderer for empty text, size 0, strokeW 0 per style; ViewModel validation clamps.
rows.parityCheck: Table-driven tests of the above input matrix producing same layer name/size as Electron.
rows.divergence: 4.1: Word Art text too large for the browser's canvas limits renders blank or fails silently (an empty toDataURL, wordart-add-to-canvas). v5: the render is capped at the image limits (16384 px per side, 50 MP) and the layer's scale makes up the difference, so the layer lands at the requested size with no error and no message (M4b, T1).

rows.name: packs/drips contents (156 PNGs)

rows.name: Packs directory resolution: dev vs packaged
rows.behavior: resolvePackDir(name): first path.join(__dirname,'packs',name) if exists (dev, repo root next to editor.js; also true if app is unpacked); else path.join(process.resourcesPath,'packs',name) if exists (packaged NSIS/MSIX via electron-builder extraResources {from:'packs', to:'packs', filter:['**/*.png']}); else null. Not found -> alert('Built-in pack "<name>" not found. Reinstall the app to restore it.').
rows.quirks: main.js enables nodeIntegration:true / contextIsolation:false (root of the PR #27 injection issue), which the native port drops. __dirname check means a packaged app whose asar contains a packs dir would pick that; extraResources avoids this.
rows.portTarget: Resolve via AppContext.BaseDirectory + 'Assets\\packs\\<name>' (works for self-contained MSIX since package install folder is the base dir). No dev/prod fork needed; keep a Missing-pack MessageBox with same text for parity ('Built-in pack "drips" not found. Reinstall the app to restore it.').
rows.parityCheck: Run from dev output dir and from installed MSIX; both list 156/25. Temporarily delete folder: MessageBox text matches.

rows.name: Load built-in pack into asset browser
rows.behavior: Buttons 'Drips' (#btnPackDrips, tooltip 'Load the bundled blood / liquid drip pack.') and 'Word art' (#btnPackWordArt, tooltip 'Load the bundled word art pack.') under label 'Built-in packs' call loadBuiltInPack('drips'|'word_art'). Reads directory with readdirSync, filters /\.(png|jpg|jpeg|gif|webp)$/i, reads each file fully into a Blob and a File (name=filename, type forced 'image/png' regardless of extension), with a fake non-configurable webkitRelativePath 'packs/<pack>/<name>'. If none: alert('Built-in pack "<pack>" is empty.'). Otherwise allAssetFiles=files, assetFolderMap={'(all)':files,[packName]:files}, shows #assetBrowser (display:block), clears subfolder buttons (no folder filter buttons for packs), sets count text, then showAssetFolder('(all)'). No dedup by filename in this path. Loading a pack replaces whatever was in the asset browser.
rows.quirks: The count text assigned here ('N images in built-in <pack> pack') is immediately overwritten by showAssetFolder('(all)') which sets '<N> images in all folders', so the intended message never shows. Port decision: show the intended built-in text (fix) or the effective one (parity). Hard-coded MIME image/png even for jpg is harmless.
rows.portTarget: AssetBrowserViewModel.LoadPack(name): enumerate files, create AssetItem{Name, Path, ParentFolder=packName}. Load thumbnails lazily/async (Task.Run decode to downscaled SKBitmap) to avoid the Electron sync-read hitch. Reuse the same pipeline as folder loading.
rows.parityCheck: Click Drips: the view model holds 156 tiles in ordinal-ignore-case order, three per row, and the realized tiles are the first ones in that order (LedgerScenarioTests, bridge A1); Word art: 25; the count reads '156 images in built-in drips pack' and stays (the fix). Narrowed in M4a: thumbnails decode as rows scroll into view (asset-grid-thumbnails).
rows.divergence: 4.1: the intended 'N images in built-in <pack> pack' count is immediately overwritten by 'N images in all folders'. v5: the built-in pack count text is shown.

rows.name: Open folder (webkitdirectory) and image filtering
rows.behavior: 'Load folder' label + 'Open folder' button (#btnLoadFolder, tooltip 'Pick a folder of PNGs to browse.') clears the hidden input value then clicks #folderInput (webkitdirectory directory multiple). Chromium enumerates ALL files recursively. Filter by filename regex /\.(png|jpg|jpeg|gif|webp)$/i. No matches -> alert('No images found in that folder. Pick a folder with PNG, JPG, GIF, or WEBP files.') and the existing browser state is left unchanged. Cancel does nothing.
rows.quirks: Filter excludes bmp/svg that other image loaders (isImageFile) accept. Browser shows a Chromium permission prompt ('Upload N files?') in Electron; native has no such prompt. Large folders (thousands) are all read into a File list and every thumbnail is created eagerly.
rows.portTarget: Use Microsoft.Win32.OpenFolderDialog (.NET 8+) then Directory.EnumerateFiles(SearchOption.AllDirectories) with the same extension filter (case-insensitive: png, jpg, jpeg, gif, webp). Same MessageBox text on empty. Preserve relative paths (root folder name + subpath) to feed the grouping logic.
rows.parityCheck: Reworded in M4a: a folder with .png, .bmp, .txt and .svg files lists the six import formats (.png, .jpg, .jpeg, .webp, .bmp, .gif; interfaces R14) and skips the rest; an empty folder shows 'No images found in that folder. Pick a folder with PNG, JPG, GIF, or WEBP files.' verbatim (LedgerScenarioTests, AssetScanTests, bridge A2 and F4).
rows.divergence: 4.1: the folder picker lists .png, .jpg, .jpeg, .gif and .webp only (editor.js:2381). v5: it lists the import formats, .bmp included, in a deterministic order (io-folder-picker); the no-images alert keeps 4.1's text (M4a, interfaces R14).

rows.name: Deduplicate by filename (deepest path wins)
rows.behavior: Files keyed by f.name in a Map; depth = webkitRelativePath.split('/').length; a file replaces the existing entry only if its depth is strictly greater. Ties keep the first seen. Result array = uniqueFiles (insertion order of first appearance of each name, value possibly replaced). Count of dropped duplicates = files.length - uniqueFiles.length.
rows.quirks: Dedup is by file NAME ONLY, so two different images with the same name in different subfolders collapse into one (silent data loss from the user's view). Intentional ('most processed version'); keep. Case-sensitive: X.png and x.png both kept (Windows treats them as same name).
rows.portTarget: Dictionary<string,(AssetFile file,int depth)> with ordinal (case-sensitive, match JS Map) key; depth = number of path segments incl. root folder name.
rows.parityCheck: Fixture folder: a/x.png, a/sub/x.png, b/x.png, a/sub/deep/x.png -> only a/sub/deep/x.png remains, count text reflects it.

rows.name: Grouping by immediate parent folder and subfolder buttons
rows.behavior: parts = webkitRelativePath.split('/'); if parts.length<=2 -> group '(root)'; else group = parts[parts.length-2] (immediate parent only, not full path). assetFolderMap['(all)']=uniqueFiles. Folder button list sorted: '(all)' first, '(root)' second, rest by localeCompare. Buttons created ONLY if Object.keys(map).length > 2 (i.e. at least two real groups). Button style: btn btn-sm btn-secondary, font-size 9px, padding 2px 6px, label 'All (n)' / 'Root (n)' / '<folder> (n)', title = raw folder key. Click -> showAssetFolder(folder). Active button highlighted bg #2d4a2d, color #7fff7f (matched via btn.title === folder). Buttons container is flex-wrap gap 3px.
rows.quirks: Two different deep folders with the same leaf name merge into one group. Files at depth 2 (direct children of the picked folder) go to '(root)'; if the user picks a folder with only subfolders there is no (root) group. The active-highlight is only applied after showAssetFolder, so initial active = '(all)'. With exactly one subfolder no buttons at all (cannot filter, but all == that group anyway).
rows.portTarget: WPF ItemsControl of ToggleButtons in a WrapPanel bound to FolderGroups (Name, Count). Sort with string.Compare(a,b,CultureInfo.CurrentCulture) after pinning (all),(root). Selected style via Style trigger #2d4a2d / #7fff7f.
rows.parityCheck: Fixture tree with root files + 3 subfolders + nested same-named leaf folders; verify group names, order, counts, and that no buttons show when only one subfolder exists.

rows.name: Asset count label text
rows.behavior: #assetCount (font 10px #555) shows text set in showAssetFolder: '<N> images in all folders' for '(all)' else '<N> images in <folder>' (folder key e.g. '(root)'). Folder loader assigns '<N> unique images (<D> duplicates removed)' just before, but showAssetFolder('(all)') overwrites it in the same tick.
rows.quirks: The duplicate-removal message is dead code in practice. Port decision: surface it (fix) or keep. Recommend show 'N images in all folders (D duplicates removed)'.
rows.portTarget: TextBlock bound to CountText; computed in SelectFolder only unless fixing.
rows.parityCheck: Reworded in M4a to the fixed behavior: after a folder with duplicates loads, the label reads '<U> unique images (<D> duplicates removed)' (editor.js:2448) and stays; a subfolder button sets '<N> images in <folder>' and All sets '<N> images in all folders' (editor.js:2544) (LedgerScenarioTests, bridge A2).
rows.divergence: 4.1: the duplicates-removed count message is dead code, overwritten before display. v5: the duplicate-count label is shown.

rows.name: Asset grid thumbnails rendering
rows.behavior: #assetBrowser is a scroll container (max-height 180px initially, overflow-y auto, hidden until a pack/folder is loaded, margin-top 6px). Inside: 3-column CSS grid (repeat(3,1fr)), gap 4px. Each thumb: square (aspect-ratio 1), 1px solid #333 border, radius 4, overflow hidden, bg #111, cursor pointer, centered image object-fit contain (max 100%), tooltip = file.name. Name overlay: absolute bottom bar rgba(0,0,0,0.7), color #ccc, font-size 7px, padding 1px 2px, single line with ellipsis. Overlay text = filename without image extension; EXCEPT if the name starts with a UUID-looking prefix /^[0-9a-f]{8}-[0-9a-f]{4}/i and the file has a parent folder (path parts >= 3) the parent folder name is shown instead. Thumbnails use blob object URLs created from the File; on re-show old blob URLs are revoked then grid cleared.
rows.quirks: No virtualization/lazy decode in Electron: 156 full-size images decode eagerly. Browser scroll area persists max-height only (see resizable). Grid order = array order (not sorted by name except what the OS returned).
rows.portTarget: ListBox with UniformGrid(Columns=3) or VirtualizingWrapPanel; ItemTemplate Border 1px #333 radius 4 bg #111 with Image Stretch=Uniform and bottom TextBlock overlay (7pt ~ 9.3px => use FontSize 7 DIP-equivalent 7px, CharacterEllipsis). Decode thumbnails at reduced size (DecodePixelWidth) off-thread; dispose bitmaps on folder change. Keep ListBox virtualization on to handle thousands.
rows.parityCheck: Screenshot diff of grid at 3 columns for Drips pack; verify UUID-named file shows parent folder name; tooltip equals file name. Signed off at MAN-7 (Este, 2026-10-25, by eye in a live side-by-side with 4.1): the asset grid at three columns on the look page; the virtualized grid, captions and order are proven (M4a A1).
rows.divergence: 4.1: every full-size image is decoded eagerly and pack order is whatever the OS returns. v5: thumbnails decode lazily at thumb size and packs are deterministically sorted. The grid is virtualized by rows of three, and only realized rows decode, at 160 px on one background worker (M4a, interfaces R5).

rows.name: Click thumbnail: add as layer (fit 85% in front region)
rows.behavior: Left click reads the file as data URL, decodes, then addLayer(img, displayName) where displayName = filename without last extension. addLayer: saveUndo(); scale = min(front.w/img.w, front.h/img.h)*0.85 with front = SHIRT_REGIONS.torso_front (current mode); positioned centered in that region; id=nextId++; default adjustments; push to top; select; setTool('select'); updateUI(); render().
rows.quirks: Layer name uses extension-stripped file name (UUID names not replaced as on the tag). addLayer default name is 'Image <nextId>' (uses already-incremented id) but not reachable here.
rows.portTarget: Command AddLayerFromFile(path, dropPos=null) -> shared LayerFactory used by pack click, Add image, drop, word art. Must create exactly identical numeric layer values.
rows.parityCheck: Click drip_blue_front_v1 (128x150) in Shirt mode: scale=min(128/128,128/150)*0.85=0.7253..., x,y centered at region; layer name 'drip_blue_front_v1'.

rows.name: Right-click thumbnail: add at full template size
rows.behavior: contextmenu is prevented (no menu). Image loaded then saveUndo(); layer name = displayName + ' (full)'; x=0, y=0; scale = max(TW/img.w, TH/img.h) with TW=585, TH=559 (cover, not contain); rotation 0, flips false, adjustments defaults; push, select, setTool('select'), updateUI, render. No tooltip/hint documents this gesture.
rows.quirks: Image is anchored top-left, not centered, so non-template-aspect images overflow right/bottom (cover). It bypasses addLayer, so duplicates its logic; keep results identical. Undefined hint: undiscoverable feature users may rely on.
rows.portTarget: MouseRightButtonUp handler on the item with e.Handled = true (suppress any context menu). Same layer math. Consider a discoverable tooltip (additive).
rows.parityCheck: Right-click a 390x200 drip: scale = max(585/390,559/200)=2.795; x=y=0; name ends ' (full)'; undo removes it.

rows.name: Drag a thumbnail onto the canvas
rows.behavior: Each thumb is draggable. dragstart sets dataTransfer text/plain 'asset-drag' and application/x-asset-name=displayName, and stores module globals _assetDragFile/_assetDragName. canvas.ondrop computes drop point ((clientX-rect.left)/zoom, (clientY-rect.top)/zoom); if _assetDragFile is set it clears both globals, reads the file as data URL, and addLayer(img, name, dropX, dropY), centering the image (scaled as in click-add) on the cursor. Canvas dragover is prevented to allow drop. Document-level dragover/drop are prevented to stop Electron navigating to dropped files.
rows.quirks: BUG: _assetDragFile is never cleared on dragend/cancel. If a user starts an asset drag and releases it somewhere other than the canvas (or presses Esc), the stale file remains and the NEXT external file drop onto the canvas will add the stale asset instead of the dropped file. Native should clear on drag end (deliberate fix). Drop onto the left 'Drop art here' zone with an asset drag adds nothing.
rows.portTarget: System.Windows.DragDrop.DoDragDrop from the thumbnail with a custom DataFormat 'application/x-asset' carrying the AssetItem; canvas element AllowDrop with Drop/DragOver handlers; convert screen point to template coordinates by dividing by zoom (and pan if present). Use DragEnd to clear any stale state rather than globals.
rows.parityCheck: UI automation: drag thumb to (300,200) in canvas at zoom 1 and 2; new layer center equals drop point in template pixels; undo restores.
rows.divergence: 4.1: a cancelled asset drag leaves a stale file that replaces the next external file drop. v5: drag state is cleared on drag end or cancel. The drag is in-app with mouse capture, not an OLE drag: it starts past the system drag distance and ends with nothing added on Esc, a lost capture or a release off the canvas, and it shows the Hand cursor over the canvas and No elsewhere, with no drag image (M4a, interfaces R6, T2-R1).

rows.name: Resizable asset browser (drag handle)
rows.behavior: An 8px-high full-width strip #assetResizeHandle (cursor ns-resize, tooltip 'Drag to resize', 40x3px pill centered in --border-2 color that turns brand gradient on hover/active) sits under the count label. mousedown: preventDefault, startY=clientY, startH=browser.offsetHeight || 180 (offsetHeight is 0 when hidden), body cursor ns-resize and user-select none. mousemove on document: newH = clamp(startH + (clientY-startY), 80, 0.7*window.innerHeight), applies browser.style.maxHeight = newH px. mouseup on document ends and restores cursor/selection. Not persisted between sessions or projects.
rows.quirks: Resizes max-height only: if the grid content is shorter than newH nothing visibly grows. mouseup outside the Electron window is lost (resize can get stuck until the next mouseup); WPF CaptureMouse fixes this. Handle is visible even while the browser is hidden.
rows.portTarget: A GridSplitter or custom Thumb in the left panel: on DragDelta change MaxHeight of the ScrollViewer with the same clamp (min 80 DIP, max 70% of the window client height), CaptureMouse for drags that leave the window, Cursor=SizeNS, hover brush uses brand gradient (#17d4fa->#f22f89).
rows.parityCheck: AssetLibraryPanelTests.The_handle_resizes_the_browser_from_its_rendered_height_within_the_clamps and In_the_window_the_resize_clamps_at_70_percent_of_the_client (DPI rows at 96, 120 and 144), The_handle_shows_the_ns_resize_cursor_and_restores_it_after_release; through the bridge (M4a A1) a 50 and a 100 DIP handle drag grow the browser by the same amount, it clamps at 80 DIPs and at 70% of the client height, and no cursor stays overridden. Narrowed in M4b: the cursor is the WPF SizeNS cursor the handle sets; the OS cursor image is not observable. MAN-8 (Este, 2026-10-25): the full suite passes at a real 125% display and again at 100% (782687f).

rows.name: Save project (.r15proj) JSON format
rows.behavior: Button 'Save work' (#btnSaveProject, tooltip 'Save your workspace. Reopen and keep editing.') builds object and writes JSON.stringify(project,null,2) (2-space indent) with MIME application/json via anchor download. Top-level fields in order: version '4.0' (string, hard-coded), app 'RBX15 Classic Shirt and Pants Maker', savedAt (ISO-8601 UTC now), mode ('Shirt'|'Pants' = currentMode), bgColor (hex string), bgOpacity (0-1 number), bgImageSrc (data URL string or null), regionColors (object regionName -> fill descriptor object from lib/fills.js, or legacy color string), showMask (bool), showGrid (bool), layers[] in bottom-to-top order, each {id, name, visible, opacity, x, y, scale, rotation (degrees), flipH, flipV, brightness, contrast, saturate, hueRotate, rShift, gShift, bShift, imgSrc (data URL or null)}. Images are embedded as base64 data URLs so files can be many MB.
rows.quirks: Version string stays '4.0' even though the app is 4.1.0 and is never read on load. Not saved: undo history, zoom, active tool, selected layer, currentFill (active fill style config), export title, drawing state, bg swatch, asset browser. Store compliance: privacy doc states .r15proj is plain inspectable JSON.
rows.portTarget: System.Text.Json writer with property order and camelCase names exactly as above, indented 2 spaces, UTF-8 no BOM. LayerImage -> PNG-encode to 'data:image/png;base64,...' (preserve original MIME if source was jpg only if the source data URL is retained; recommend retaining original data URL string to keep round-trip byte-identical). Fill descriptors serialize via the same schema as lib/fills.js (type, c1, c2, angle, scale ...) - reuse the existing JSON contract.
rows.parityCheck: ProjectIOTests (M2b): Write keeps saveProject's field set and order for the three 4.1-saved fixtures in tests/goldens/projects and round-trips them to equal documents. LedgerScenarioTests: a save through the File group writes version 5.0 with no title and reopens to the same export. 4.1 reads a v5 file: tools/parity-ref/app-render.js loads a v5-saved project through 4.1's real Open path with no alert, and its export equals v5's export of the same file under the golden rule (M4a Task 5 P41, brg compare). Narrowed in M4a: the JSON is compared field by field with 4.1's own saves, not diffed against a same-scenario Electron save.
rows.divergence: 4.1: writes version '4.0'. v5: writes the same fields with version '5.0'.

rows.name: Save filename and dialog behavior
rows.behavior: Filename = exportTitle input value (placeholder 'Template name...'), fallback 'untitled', with every char not in [a-zA-Z0-9_-] replaced by '_' (spaces, dots, unicode all become '_'), plus '.r15proj'. Saved through the browser download mechanism: Electron shows its default Save As dialog (no custom handler in main.js) pre-filled with this name; no overwrite/last-folder memory in-app. Blob URL revoked immediately after click().
rows.quirks: Non-ASCII title chars (e.g. accented letters) are all flattened to '_'; a title of '..' becomes '__'. No error handling if write fails or the dialog is cancelled.
rows.portTarget: Microsoft.Win32.SaveFileDialog: Filter 'RBX15 project (*.r15proj)|*.r15proj', FileName = sanitized title, DefaultExt .r15proj, OverwritePrompt true. Keep identical sanitization regex.
rows.parityCheck: Title 'My Shirt v2!' -> suggested 'My_Shirt_v2_.r15proj'; empty -> 'untitled.r15proj'.

rows.name: Open project: file picker and restore order
rows.behavior: 'Open' (#btnLoadProject, tooltip 'Open a saved workspace.') clicks hidden #projectFileInput (accept '.json,.r15proj'); on change, loads first file only, then clears the input value (so same file can be reopened). loadProject: JSON.parse; then in order: if project.mode truthy -> switchMode(mode) (rebuilds mask/region grid, wipes regionColors); bgColor = project.bgColor || '#192e44'; bgOpacity = value if != null else 1; sync #bgColor and #bgOpacity (opacity*100) inputs; bgImageSrc -> async Image then bgImage + render(), else bgImage=null; regionColors = project.regionColors || {} and repaint every .region-btn swatch via paintRegionButton (descriptor or legacy string); showMask/showGrid restored only if present (checkboxes synced); layers cleared, selection cleared; empty layers -> updateUI()+render(). Errors: any thrown error (bad JSON, wrong shape) -> alert('Failed to load project. ' + err.message).
rows.quirks: No undo entry is pushed and history is NOT cleared on load, so Ctrl+Z after Open restores the pre-edit state of the previous project (mixes projects). Loading ignores 'version', 'app', 'savedAt'. mode is not validated: an unknown mode string is stored in currentMode and goes to the Shirt branch. currentFill and showMask default are not reset when the field is absent (showMask keeps previous value). Decide: clear history on load (fix) or keep. Current-fill style controls are not restored.
rows.portTarget: Microsoft.Win32.OpenFileDialog (Filter 'RBX15 project|*.r15proj;*.json', single select). Deserialize with System.Text.Json into a tolerant DTO (all properties nullable, JsonElement for regionColors fill which may be string or object). Catch JsonException/any -> MessageBox 'Failed to load project. <message>' (message text will differ; document).
rows.parityCheck: ProjectIOTests (M2b) open the 4.1 fixtures (a v4 file and the legacy color-string pants file), '{}' and every structural refusal field by field; LedgerScenarioTests and the bridge (F1) show a non-JSON and a truncated file alerting 'Failed to load project. ...' with the document, history and title unchanged and no save prompt first; the read runs off the UI thread (ProjectFileServiceTests) and a file past the caps is refused by them (ImagesCapsTests). Narrowed in M4a: 'huge file' is the decode caps, not a timed load.
rows.divergence: 4.1: load applies fields piecemeal, accepts bad shapes and unknown modes, and leaves the previous project's undo history in place. v5: all-or-nothing validated load with history cleared. The Open dialog lists RBX15 project (*.r15proj) first and JSON project (*.json) second, keeping 4.1's .json reach (editor.html:108); the file is read and decoded off the UI thread with the window blocked, and a file that fails to read alerts before any save prompt (M4a, interfaces R4).

rows.name: Open project: layer restoration algorithm and ordering
rows.behavior: For each layer record with an imgSrc, a new Image is decoded asynchronously and on load a layer is pushed with: id=d.id, name=d.name||'Layer', visible=(d.visible!==false), opacity = d.opacity if != null else 1, x=d.x||0, y=d.y||0, scale=d.scale||1, rotation=d.rotation||0, flipH/flipV=!!, brightness/contrast/saturate default 100 (null-check), hueRotate default 0 (null-check), rShift/gShift/bShift=||0. Records without imgSrc are counted as loaded and skipped. When the loaded counter reaches layerData.length on an onload: layers are sorted by their index in the saved array (findIndex by id), nextId=max(layer ids)+1, selectedLayerId = topmost layer id, updateUI(), render(). onerror (corrupt/unsupported image): counter++ and the layer is dropped; if this is the final event, updateUI()+render() only.
rows.quirks: BUGS: (1) if the last-finishing event is an onerror (or the final records have no imgSrc and no loads), sorting, nextId update and selection are skipped; layers are left in decode-completion order and nextId stale -> id collisions with later added layers. (2) If all records lack imgSrc and none load, UI is never refreshed. (3) Sorting uses id lookup: duplicate ids order unspecified. (4) `scale: 0` and `x: NaN` coerce via ||. Native should sort deterministically and always set nextId/selection; document deliberate fix. Layer ids in the file are preserved verbatim.
rows.portTarget: Decode synchronously/in parallel (Task.WhenAll) then build ordered list by array index; selection = last; nextId = max+1 (use int). Preserve all defaulting rules incl. `scale: 0 -> 1` and `opacity: 0 stays 0`.
rows.parityCheck: ProjectIOTests (M2b): missing fields, opacity 0, scale 0, visible false, an undecodable image in the middle and in the last position, duplicate ids and nextId follow loadProject's rules; LedgerScenarioTests: stored values out of range open raw. Narrowed in M4a: the 50-large-image fixture is covered by the decode caps (ImagesCapsTests) and the off-thread read, not run.
rows.divergence: 4.1: layer order, nextId and selection depend on async decode completion and are skipped when the last event is an error. v5: deterministic ordering with nextId and selection always set, and a visible warning naming dropped layers. Stored rotation, scale, opacity and adjustment values open raw, in range or not, as 4.1 opens them; only the field a gesture or the panel edits is clamped (M4a, interfaces R12).

rows.name: Project file version compatibility policy
rows.behavior: Writer always emits version '4.0'. Reader performs no version check; it is purely defensive field-by-field defaulting, so older/partial files (missing bgColor, bgOpacity, showMask/showGrid, regionColors, per-layer adjustments, and legacy regionColors values that are plain color strings instead of fill descriptors) all load. Legacy region colors are handled by window.RBX15Fills.fillToCSS in the swatch and by the fills engine at render. Files with .json extension accepted too. Per the spike notes existing v4 files must open in the native build.
rows.quirks: Because Electron ignores the version, native writing a new schema breaks users who roll back. Keep schema identical. Unknown extra fields are ignored (not preserved).
rows.portTarget: Keep version '4.0' string for forward compat with Electron 4.1.0 (or bump to '4.1' and keep tolerant reader); implement FillDescriptor JsonConverter accepting string (legacy color -> solid) or object. Add a 'minimum supported' policy test pack.
rows.parityCheck: Round-trip matrix: (Electron save -> native open) and (native save -> Electron open) for solid, gradient, mixed fills, camo, stripes at slider max; load docs/ sample files, shirts/ or variations/ project files if any exist.
rows.divergence: 4.1: writer emits version '4.0' and the reader ignores version. v5: reads all 4.1 files and writes version '5.0'.

rows.name: Add image (load image as layer)
rows.behavior: 'Add image' button (#btnLoadImage, tooltip 'Add an image file as a layer.') clicks hidden #imageLoadInput (accept 'image/*', multiple). For each selected file passing isImageFile (MIME starts with image/ OR extension in png, jpg, jpeg, gif, webp, bmp, svg; non-images are skipped silently): name = filename minus last extension; FileReader -> data URL -> Image -> addLayer(img, name) (default placement centered in torso_front at 85% fit, saveUndo each). Input value cleared after the loop. Multi-select produces multiple layers (each its own undo step), order determined by async read completion, not selection order.
rows.quirks: SVG/BMP are accepted here but not by the asset-library filter. Order of multi-file adds is racy in Electron. Each add pushes one undo snapshot. Same function path as drop zone (handleFiles at editor.js:998) - align semantics in the slice owning drop.
rows.portTarget: OpenFileDialog Multiselect=true, Filter images (png, jpg, jpeg, gif, webp, bmp, svg). SVG needs Svg.Skia (SkiaSharp.Extended.Svg / Svg.Skia) rasterized at intrinsic size; GIF = first frame (browser Image shows first frame in drawImage). Process files in selection order (deterministic) - fix of racing order.
rows.parityCheck: Add a PNG, JPG, GIF (first frame), BMP and WEBP: each becomes a layer named by its file name minus the last extension; an SVG and a .txt become no layer and each shows a status message (ImageImporterTests, ImportServiceTests). Reworded in M3a: v5 refuses SVG, so there is no SVG intrinsic size to compare.
rows.divergence: 4.1: multi-file import order is racy, each file is its own undo step, and SVG is accepted. v5: files import in pick order as one undo step and SVG is dropped with a message.

rows.name: Initial render and startup order
rows.behavior: Last statement of editor.js is render() (draws template canvas with default state: Shirt mode, bg #192e44 opacity 1, mask visible, grid off, no layers). Word art preview renders after fonts.ready (or 1s fallback). Asset browser starts hidden with empty count. Window: 1200x800, title 'RBX15 Classic Shirt and Pants Maker', menu bar hidden (main.js). Google Fonts are requested via <link> in editor.html head at startup.
rows.quirks: Electron window state (size/position) is not persisted; keep or add (additive). Missing: single-instance lock, app.on activate only for macOS.
rows.portTarget: MainWindow 1200x800 (default; set MinWidth/MinHeight to taste), Title identical, no menu. Constructor order: load fonts -> init VM -> first SKElement paint. Startup perf budget: first frame <= 0.96 s per spike numbers.
rows.parityCheck: Cold start: window title, size, default visuals equal the 4.1.0 screenshot set in docs/store; first frame time recorded. Signed off at MAN-7 (Este, 2026-10-25, by eye in a live side-by-side with 4.1): the default-visuals clause. Proven by the M4b smoke cold start: zero sockets over 6 launches, the title 'RBX15 Classic Shirt and Pants Maker', window 1200x800 (client 1184x761), first frame 1.11-1.18 s recorded (over the 0.96 s port-target spike budget). The divergence's remembered window size and position is M5's (shell-no-persistence).
rows.divergence: 4.1: requests Google Fonts at startup and does not remember window size or position. v5: zero network requests and the window remembers size and position.

rows.name: Electron-specific mechanisms in this slice that vanish
rows.behavior: This slice relies on nodeIntegration require('fs'/'path') in the renderer, process.resourcesPath, File/Blob fakes with defineProperty on webkitRelativePath, FileReader/data URLs for every image path, blob object URLs for thumbnails, browser download for save, hidden file inputs for open, alert() for all errors (blocking modal). main.js sets nodeIntegration:true, contextIsolation:false.
rows.quirks: Alert wording is user-visible: keep strings exactly: 'Built-in pack "X" not found. Reinstall the app to restore it.', 'Built-in pack "X" is empty.', 'No images found in that folder. Pick a folder with PNG, JPG, GIF, or WEBP files.', 'Failed to load project. <err>'.
rows.portTarget: Replace with .NET file APIs, async streams, WPF dialogs (Microsoft.Win32 file/folder dialogs), MessageBox for alerts. No IPC needed. Image decode via SKCodec/SKBitmap.Decode; keep layers in memory as SKBitmap (not data URLs) and only encode to data URL on save.
rows.parityCheck: No renderer-level injection surface: verify no WebView is used.
rows.divergence: 4.1: relies on nodeIntegration, fs/path in the renderer, blob URLs and browser downloads. v5: native .NET file APIs and dialogs, with no nodeIntegration.

rows.name: Window frame, title, menu, default size
rows.behavior: Electron BrowserWindow 1200x800, no minWidth/minHeight, title 'RBX15 Classic Shirt and Pants Maker' (main.js:5-9; <title> editor.html:6 is the same string). Menu bar hidden via setMenuBarVisibility(false) (main.js:21) so there is no visible menu, but Electron's default hidden menu still gives Ctrl+R reload, Ctrl+Shift+I devtools, Ctrl+=/- browser zoom (editor.js:1803-1805 comments rely on this). Single window, quits when all closed (main.js:34-38). No unsaved-changes prompt on close, no persistence of any state (no localStorage/sessionStorage anywhere in editor.js), so closing silently discards work. Window is freely resizable; the whole page is a fixed-viewport flex column with overflow hidden (styles.css:99-108).
rows.quirks: Ctrl+R in Electron reloads the page and wipes all work with no confirmation (editor.js:1803 comment shows the author knows). Port should simply not have this. No min window size: at narrow widths the ribbon scrolls horizontally and the canvas area can collapse.
rows.portTarget: WPF Window Width=1200 Height=800 (client area differs from Electron content area, so match content area ~1200x(800-title bar)), Title string as-is, no MenuBar. Do not carry over browser reload/devtools/zoom accelerators. Decide deliberately: add an unsaved-changes prompt on close (recommended deviation) or keep silent discard.
rows.parityCheck: Launch: title bar text matches, no menu, window opens 1200x800, resizes without crash down to ~640x480, closing with edits shows no prompt (or the new prompt if chosen). The caption reads as one band with the header (brand-navy-deep), its text is light, the caption buttons and snap layouts work, and on Windows without the DWM color attributes the window still opens with the default caption. CaptionThemeTests pin the attribute values.
rows.divergence: 4.1: Electron's default Windows caption, light or dark by the system setting. v5: the native caption is themed through DWM (immersive dark mode, brand-navy-deep caption, ink-100 caption text, brand-navy-soft border) with the system frame, caption buttons and snap layouts kept, per Este's call (2026-10-14); MainWindow and the themed dialog take it (the borderless color picker has no caption).

rows.name: Page skeleton and flex layout
rows.behavior: body is a column flex, 100vh, overflow hidden (styles.css:99-108). Children top to bottom: header (flex-shrink 0), .ribbon (flex-shrink 0, tab strip + one active pane), .app (flex:1, row flex, overflow hidden), footer (flex-shrink 0). .app contains left .panel (fixed 280px, flex-shrink 0, overflow-y auto, padding 14px) and .canvas-area (flex:1). The legacy .rpanel right panel (240px) is defined in CSS but no element uses it (styles.css:462-469); the DOM has only left panel + canvas. A hidden #btnExport2 button sits inside .app purely for JS compat (editor.html:339-340, editor.js:1542).
rows.quirks: Ribbon height is NOT constant: each pane has different content height (Home panes have 2-row vertical groups, Details is single row), so switching ribbon tabs changes the ribbon height and resizes/shifts the canvas area vertically (canvas is vertically centered so it jumps). Decide: keep (parity) or fix to a fixed ribbon height (recommended, tiny deviation).
rows.portTarget: Grid with rows Auto (header), Auto (ribbon), * (app), Auto (footer); app row = columns 280 (panel, ScrollViewer vertical auto) and * (canvas area). Drop the dead .rpanel and btnExport2.
rows.parityCheck: Overlay native screenshot against docs/screenshots/4.1/*.png at 1920x1080 window content; region boundaries (header bottom, ribbon bottom, panel right edge x=280, footer top) match within 1 px. RibbonMeasureTests (M4b item 12): at 1184x761 with a layer selected, the ribbon is 167 DIP (138 DIP panes) on every tab, and Details and Text fit without a horizontal scroll; ShellLookTests pins the ribbon at 167 and the canvas area at 519. Narrowed in M4b: Home and Layout scroll horizontally at this width, as both did in 4.1 (ribbon-overflow-hscroll; Este, 2026-10-18 and 2026-10-25; RibbonMeasureTests.The_ribbon_has_one_height_and_Home_and_Layout_scroll_at_1200_as_in_4_1). Signed off at MAN-7 (Este, 2026-10-25, by eye in a live side-by-side with 4.1): the region boundaries; the 1 px overlay was not measured. The 167 and 138 DIP pins are 100% measurements: at a real 125% the ribbon is 165.6 and the panes 137.6, still one height on every tab (MAN-8, 2026-10-25).
rows.divergence: 4.1: ribbon height changes per tab, shifting the canvas vertically on tab switch. v5: fixed ribbon height. The fixed height is the tallest pane's, the Text tab's 138 DIP, so Home is 17 DIP taller than its content; Home (about 1455 DIP) and Layout (about 1460, with Fill Style and the region grid back on it) scroll sideways at 1200 DIP, as both did in 4.1 (M4b, R1; Este, 2026-10-18; F1 reversed 2026-10-25).

rows.name: Narrow-window breakpoint
rows.behavior: Only one media query: @media (max-width:900px) sets .panel width to 200px and .rpanel to 200px (styles.css:694-697). No height queries, no min-width on canvas area. Below 900px viewport width the left panel shrinks 280 -> 200 and its content (3-col asset grid, controls) reflows.
rows.portTarget: Window SizeChanged handler (or VisualStateManager style trigger) setting panel column Width 200 when content width <= 900 DIPs, else 280.
rows.parityCheck: Resize window content width to 900 and 901: panel is 200 then 280 wide; asset grid stays 3 columns and thumbnails shrink. RibbonMeasureTests.The_900_901_breakpoint_keeps_the_panel_width_and_three_asset_columns and ShellTests.The_left_panel_narrows_at_900 (M4b item 12).

rows.name: Header bar content and styling
rows.behavior: Header: padding 10px 24px, row, gap 16, 135deg gradient navy->navy-deep(50%)->navy, 1px bottom border rgba(23,212,250,.45), shadow 0 2px 8px rgba(0,0,0,.35). h1 text 'RBX15 Classic Shirt & Pants Maker' (HTML &), Space Grotesk 20px weight 600, letter-spacing -0.02em, text filled with 135deg cyan->magenta gradient (background-clip:text, transparent fill). Adjacent span 'ItsjustEste | v4.1' rendered JetBrains Mono 11px, color #8e9bad, uppercase (displays 'ITSJUSTESTE | V4.1'), letter-spacing .12em. Version is hard-coded text in HTML (not read from package.json).
rows.quirks: Gradient text is clipped to the h1 box only (not the whole header). Letter-spacing in WPF needs a workaround; budget for it for all mono uppercase labels (tabs, group labels, h3, .info, footer).
rows.portTarget: Border with LinearGradientBrush background; TextBlock for title using a gradient foreground (LinearGradientBrush Foreground with StartPoint/EndPoint 0,0->1,1 in bounding box) and FontFamily Space Grotesk; subtitle TextBlock with CharacterSpacing equivalent (WPF has no letter-spacing: use Typography or per-glyph Run spacing / a custom TextBlock with TextOptions; or use FormattedText + DrawingContext). Bind version text to assembly/MSIX version formatted 'v{Major}.{Minor}'.

rows.name: Footer line
rows.behavior: Footer text 'Developed at 626 Labs LLC' displayed uppercase via CSS (text-transform) as 'DEVELOPED AT 626 LABS LLC', JetBrains Mono 10px, color #5e6b7f, letter-spacing .15em, centered, padding 7px 24px, 1px top border rgba(255,255,255,.08), vertical gradient ink-950 -> ink-900, flex-shrink 0.

Letter-spacing has no WPF property and is tracked with the header's look sign-off (shell-header).

rows.name: Color token set (:root)
rows.behavior: Brand navy #192e44/#0f1f31/#223a54; cyan #17d4fa, bright #5ce6ff, dim #0fa8c9; magenta #f22f89, bright #ff5aa3, dim #c21f6c. Ink scale: 0 #fff, 50 #f5f7fb, 100 #e6ebf3, 200 #c4cdda, 300 #8e9bad, 400 #5e6b7f, 500 #3d4a5e, 600 #2a3649, 700 #1e2a3d, 800 #152135, 900 #0a1524, 950 #050c18. Foreground: fg-1 #fff, fg-2 #c4cdda (body default text), fg-3 #8e9bad, fg-muted #5e6b7f, accents cyan/magenta. Backgrounds: bg-0 navy-deep (body), bg-1 navy, bg-2 navy-soft, bg-3 ink-600. Dark theme only: no light theme, no prefers-color-scheme handling, no theme switch exists.

The ribbon and panel regions compared side by side with 4.1 at 1200x800 and 100% scale in the M3b look sign-off (states 01-07), signed off by Este on 2026-10-16 (.superpowers/m3b-look/SIGNOFF.txt). rows.name: Radii, shadows, motion, type tokens
rows.behavior: Radii xs4 sm6 md10 lg14 pill999. Shadows: shadow-2 0 4px 16px rgba(0,0,0,.45) (canvas wrap), glow-duo = cyan 0 0 24px .25 + magenta 0 0 48px .18 (selected layer, primary button hover). Motion: ease cubic-bezier(.2,.7,.2,1), fast 120ms, med 220ms; transitions on color/border/background/transform/box-shadow of tabs, buttons, swatches, layer items, drop zone, region buttons, preset buttons, wordart style buttons, resize handle. rows.name: UI fonts loaded at runtime from Google Fonts
rows.behavior: styles.css line 6 @imports Space Grotesk 400/500/600/700, JetBrains Mono 400/500/600, Inter 400/500/600/700 from fonts.googleapis.com (display=swap). Nothing is bundled. Offline, the stack falls back to system-ui (Segoe UI on Windows) and ui-monospace (Cascadia/Consolas), so offline users see different typography; online first paint uses fallback then swaps. Also leaks an IP to Google on every launch (privacy doc relevance).
rows.quirks: Intended-vs-actual: tab labels etc. specify weight 600 mono; screenshots show those weights, so ship 600.
rows.portTarget: Bundle Inter (400/500/600/700), Space Grotesk (400-700; only 600 used visibly), JetBrains Mono (400/500/600) as WPF Resources (FontFamily='pack://application:,,,/Fonts/#Inter'), include OFL license files. No network access at runtime. Pin to the Google static instances matching weights (Inter variable file needs static cuts or use variable-font aware loading; WPF does not support variable axes well, so ship static TTFs).
rows.parityCheck: No network: the app has no network code (the M3b final verification grep) and the UI faces resolve to the vendored files (ThemeTokenTests.Ui_fonts_resolve_to_the_vendored_files). Glyph metrics: the 'Download template' button is within 2 px of 4.1's width in the M3b look run's metrics table; signed off by Este on 2026-10-16 (.superpowers/m3b-look/SIGNOFF.txt). Narrowed in M3b: the button box stands in for the text box.
rows.divergence: 4.1: UI fonts load at runtime from Google Fonts, leaking an IP and falling back offline. v5: Space Grotesk, Inter and JetBrains Mono are bundled with zero network requests.

rows.name: 15 Word Art fonts loaded from Google Fonts
rows.behavior: editor.html:11 loads: Anton 400, Bebas Neue 400, Dancing Script 700, Great Vibes 400, Pacifico 400, Creepster 400, Poppins 700+900, Lato 900, Bangers 400, Permanent Marker 400, Bungee Shade 400, Rubik Mono One 400, Press Start 2P 400, Righteous 400, Orbitron 700+900 (display=swap), with preconnect to fonts.googleapis.com/fonts.gstatic.com. The <select id=waFont> offers exactly these 15 families (labels in separate item). Offline users silently get 'sans-serif' fallback because the canvas font string ends with ', sans-serif' (editor.js:2131) with no error. Preview waits on document.fonts.ready (editor.js:2294) but fonts are lazily fetched on first use, so the first preview/first Add-to-canvas of a not-yet-fetched font can render in the fallback font and is not re-rendered when the font arrives.
rows.quirks: Weight request is always 900 (editor.js:2131). Fonts with only a 400 face (Anton, Bebas Neue, Great Vibes, Pacifico, Creepster, Bangers, Permanent Marker, Bungee Shade, Rubik Mono One, Press Start 2P, Righteous) are synthesized bold by Chromium (Skia fake-bold embolden); Dancing Script (700 only) resolves to its 700 face; Poppins/Lato/Orbitron use true 900. To reproduce, use SKFont.Embolden=true for faces whose weight < 600 and the 700/900 faces otherwise. Decide whether to keep faux-bold (parity) or render at native weight.
rows.portTarget: Bundle all 15 TTFs (static cuts matching weights above) and load as SKTypeface via SKTypeface.FromStream or SKFontManager.CreateTypeface from embedded resources; map family name -> typeface at startup. No fallback needed. License check: all OFL except Permanent Marker (Apache 2.0); ship license texts.
rows.parityCheck: Glyph output is golden-checked for Anton, Poppins, Dancing Script and Orbitron; the other 11 fonts are covered by FontsTests (load, family match, synthetic-bold flags), not by glyph output. Fonts are vendored, so offline by construction. Narrowed in M2b: no glyph goldens for 11 of 15 fonts.
rows.divergence: 4.1: the 15 Word Art fonts load at runtime from Google Fonts and fall back to sans-serif offline. v5: all 15 are bundled.

rows.name: Scrollbar styling (effective result)
rows.behavior: styles.css sets both standard (scrollbar-color navy-soft on ink-950, scrollbar-width:thin on *) and WebKit pseudo-element rules (10px, thumb vertical gradient navy-soft->navy with 2px ink-950 border and 6px radius, hover cyan-dim, track/corner ink-950). Electron 41 (Chromium >=121) ignores the ::-webkit-scrollbar rules when scrollbar-color/width are set, so the effective look is a THIN native-style scrollbar with thumb #223a54 on track #050c18 and no hover recolor or gradient (visible in docs/screenshots/4.1/02-layers.png). Scrollbars appear on: left panel (overflow-y auto), asset browser (max-height 180, overflow-y auto), ribbon pane (overflow-x auto) and the layer area via panel scroll.
rows.quirks: The webkit gradient/hover rules are dead code under Electron 41. Do not implement them.
rows.portTarget: ScrollViewer ControlTemplate/Style with thin (about 8 px) track #050c18, thumb #223a54 (rounded), no hover color. Apply to Panel ScrollViewer, asset browser ScrollViewer, ribbon pane horizontal ScrollViewer. Decide: match effective (thin flat) look, not the dead webkit gradient.
rows.parityCheck: The left panel's scrollbar (states 03 and 05) and the canvas scrollbars (state 05) compared side by side with 4.1 in the M3b look sign-off, which also confirmed M3a's provisional width 8 and thumb inset 1; signed off by Este on 2026-10-16 (.superpowers/m3b-look/SIGNOFF.txt). Narrowed in M3b: 1200x800 captures stand in for 02-layers.png.

rows.name: Keyboard focus ring
rows.behavior: Visible focus uses :focus-visible only: button, select, input, textarea, .ribbon-tab, .preset-btn, .fill-type-btn, .swatch get outline 2px solid #17d4fa with offset 2px (styles.css:357-367). Mouse clicks do not show the ring. The .swatch selector can never match because swatches are non-focusable divs; region tiles (.region-btn divs), layer items (divs), drop zone (div), adjustments toggle (div), zoom buttons (are buttons, ring applies) are likewise not keyboard reachable. No tabindex, ARIA roles, aria-labels, aria-pressed on toggles, or live regions exist anywhere in editor.html/editor.js. No :focus border style on ribbon inputs (only .controls inputs change border-color to cyan on :focus, styles.css:348-352).
rows.quirks: Current app is keyboard-inaccessible for swatches, region tiles, layers, drop zone, adjustments toggle. Port should fix, but it is a deliberate deviation to record.
rows.portTarget: WPF FocusVisualStyle: custom Style with 2px cyan Rectangle, Margin -2 (offset 2); WPF shows focus visuals for keyboard only by default. Apply to Button, ComboBox, TextBox, CheckBox, Slider, ribbon tabs. Decision: fix parity gaps by making swatches, region tiles, layer items, drop zone and adj toggle focusable (Button/ListBoxItem) with AutomationProperties.Name; add AutomationProperties to all controls (UIA) since MSIX Store certification favors it.
rows.parityCheck: Tab through the whole Home tab: each stop shows 2px cyan ring offset 2 px; mouse click does not. Run Accessibility Insights UIA scan: no unnamed interactive controls.
rows.divergence: 4.1: swatches, region tiles, layers and the drop zone are not keyboard reachable. v5: keyboard-reachable tiles, layers and swatches with automation names and a cyan focus ring.

rows.name: Ribbon tab strip and switching
rows.behavior: Four tab buttons in order Home (active by default), Layout, Details, Text (data-tab). Click removes .active from all tabs/panes and activates the matching pane; no animation, no persistence (always starts on Home), no keyboard arrow navigation (plain buttons, reachable by Tab, activated by Enter/Space). Tab style: mono 11px weight 600 uppercase letter-spacing .1em, padding 6x16, color #8e9bad; hover #c4cdda; active color cyan with background navy-deep and a 2px brand-gradient underline positioned at bottom:-1px; tab strip padding 0 8px, vertical gradient ink-950->ink-900, 1px bottom border. Pane: hidden by default, active = display:flex, align-items stretch, overflow-x auto, padding 8px 12px.
rows.quirks: Tab switching changes ribbon height (see shell-layout-skeleton).
rows.portTarget: Custom ribbon (do not use a stock TabControl look): RadioButton-style tab headers (Style with ToggleButton) bound to a SelectedTab VM property, ContentControl switching four group panels inside a horizontal ScrollViewer.
rows.parityCheck: Click each tab: only that pane visible; active tab has cyan text, navy-deep fill, gradient underline; initial tab is Home; switching never changes document state.

rows.name: Ribbon group chrome
rows.behavior: Each .ribbon-group is a column flex with padding 0 10px, 1px right divider rgba(255,255,255,.08) (none on last child), flex-shrink 0 (never compresses, so overflow scrolls horizontally). .ribbon-group-items is a wrapping row (gap 4, align center, flex:1); .vert variant is a column with align-items stretch. .ribbon-group-label sits under the items: mono 10px 600 uppercase, letter-spacing .12em, color #5e6b7f, centered, padding-top 5, nowrap. Pane gap 0, items stretch to the same height so dividers span full height.
rows.quirks: Group labels are displayed uppercase by CSS (e.g. 'BG SETTINGS', 'COLORS & SIZE').
rows.portTarget: A RibbonGroup UserControl: Grid rows (Content *, Label Auto), right border 1px, Padding 0,0 10,0; WrapPanel (Horizontal) or StackPanel for items. Set Margin so label sits 5 px below items.
rows.parityCheck: Group dividers and labels line up with 4.1 screenshot; labels: Mode, Tools, Brush, Placement, Edit, File, Settings (Home); Presets, Background, BG Settings, Fill Style, Template Regions (Layout); Settings, Neckline, Edges, Seams, Accents (Details); Text, Colors & Size, Style, Preview (Text). RibbonMeasureTests.Each_tab_carries_its_groups_labels (M4b item 12) asserts v5's labels per tab; Fill Style and the region grid (labelled CLICK REGIONS TO FILL, ribbon-fill-regions-joined) end the Layout tab, as in 4.1 (Este, 2026-10-25, reversing F1). Signed off at MAN-7 (Este, 2026-10-25, by eye in a live side-by-side with 4.1): the divider and label alignment.
rows.divergence: 4.1: the second ribbon tab is labelled Layout. v5: it reads Background (automation name 'Background tab'), since it holds the background, fill and region groups; the code keeps the name Layout (RibbonTab.Layout, LayoutViewModel), so the tab plumbing is unchanged (Este, MAN-7, 2026-10-25).

rows.name: Ribbon horizontal overflow
rows.behavior: When a pane's groups exceed window width the active pane scrolls horizontally (overflow-x:auto) with the thin themed scrollbar; groups never wrap or shrink. Text tab is widest (~900px of content); Home about 1050 px at the 4.1 layout. Home overflows a 1200 px window too (pane 1432 px in a 1184 px client, measured M3b).
rows.portTarget: ScrollViewer HorizontalScrollBarVisibility=Auto VerticalScrollBarVisibility=Disabled around each pane's StackPanel(Orientation=Horizontal). Mouse wheel horizontal scroll is NOT provided by the original (wheel over ribbon does nothing); keep or add (low-risk nicety).
rows.parityCheck: The launch state at a 700 DIP client width (state 07): the ribbon scrolls horizontally and its groups keep their size, compared side by side with 4.1 at the same width, signed off by Este on 2026-10-16 (.superpowers/m3b-look/SIGNOFF.txt). Narrowed in M3b: a 700 DIP client stands in for a 700 px window.

rows.name: Shirt/Pants mode toggle button
rows.behavior: Single button #btnModeToggle in the 'Mode' group labeled 'SHIRT' (or 'PANTS'), inline style: 13px/700, padding 6x18, min-width 80, radius 6, letter-spacing .5px, text #050c18, no border, background 135deg gradient cyan->magenta for SHIRT and magenta->cyan for PANTS (set in JS). Click: saveUndo() then switchMode(opposite). switchMode: swaps active region table, label, gradient, WIPES regionColors, rebuilds the 585x559 mask and Layout-tab region grid, re-renders. A hidden <select id=assetType> (Shirt/Pants) is kept in sync (editor.js:1697) but is hidden and otherwise unused. Layers are NOT cleared on switch (layers persist; only region fills are wiped).
rows.quirks: See bug-pants-mode-region-keys: in Pants mode most layer-adding actions throw because they still read SHIRT_REGIONS.torso_front.
rows.portTarget: ToggleButton/Button bound to Mode enum; same label text/gradient; remove the dead hidden <select>. Mask and region tables are data (same coordinates for shirt and pants except key names: torso->waist, rarm->rleg, larm->lleg; geometry identical).
rows.parityCheck: Click toggles label SHIRT<->PANTS and gradient direction; Undo after switching returns to prior mode with region fills intact (docs/SMOKE_TEST.md:56); Layout tab region labels change Torso/Right Arm/Left Arm -> Waist/Right Leg/Left Leg.
rows.divergence: 4.1: in Pants mode most layer-adding actions throw because they read the shirt torso_front region. v5: Pants mode works everywhere via semantic slots per mode.

rows.name: Tool buttons: Select, Draw, Line, Rect, Ellipse, Eraser
rows.behavior: Six .btn-sm.btn-secondary buttons with tooltips: Select 'Select/Move (V)', Draw 'Freehand draw (B)', Line 'Line tool (L)', Rect 'Rectangle (U)', Ellipse 'Ellipse (O)' (id btnDrawCircle, internal tool 'circle'), Eraser 'Eraser (E)'. Select is active at startup. Clicking a tool makes it the only one with .btn-active (cyan border/tint/text via !important); clicking the ACTIVE tool again returns to Select (toggleTool). Select cannot be toggled off. Switching tool resets cursor (eraser gets a custom ring cursor, all others crosshair). Adding a layer, selecting a layer, or creating a detail/word-art layer forces tool back to Select.
rows.quirks: Tooltip says 'Ellipse' but created layers are named 'Circle drawing'. Select tool state is not visually 'off-able'.
rows.portTarget: ToggleButton group (single-select, tap-active-to-deselect returns to Select). CurrentTool enum in the VM; style 'btn-active' as checked state.
rows.parityCheck: Press V/B/L/U/O/E: highlight moves; press same key again returns to Select; selecting a layer in the panel returns to Select.

rows.name: Keys: ON/OFF shortcut toggle
rows.behavior: Button #btnToggleKeys in the Tools group (tooltip 'Toggle keyboard shortcuts'), initial text 'Keys: ON', inline bg #2d4a2d, color #7fff7f, font 10px, no border (no btn-secondary). Click flips keyboardShortcutsEnabled; label 'Keys: OFF' with bg #4a2d2d, color #ff7f7f. When OFF every key shortcut in the document handler is ignored, INCLUDING Ctrl+Z/Ctrl+Y undo/redo, Delete, arrow nudges. Not persisted; resets to ON every launch.
rows.quirks: Turning shortcuts off also disables undo shortcut (probably unintended; decide keep or exempt Ctrl+Z/Y).
rows.portTarget: ToggleButton with two visual states and same colors; gate all window-level KeyDown handling on the flag (including undo/redo).
rows.parityCheck: Reworded in M4b to the fixed behavior: with Keys OFF, V and Delete do nothing and Ctrl+Z still undoes (ShortcutRouterTests.Keys_off_blocks_v_but_not_ctrl_z; M4b smoke K1: arrows and Delete do nothing, Ctrl+Z undoes); toggled back ON they work.
rows.divergence: 4.1: Keys OFF disables every shortcut including Ctrl+Z and Ctrl+Y. v5: Keys OFF disables only bare-key shortcuts and Ctrl combos always work.

rows.name: Brush group: color, size, fill
rows.behavior: Color input #drawColor (default #17d4fa, 26x24, no border, radius 4, tooltip 'Draw color'), range #drawSize min 1 max 50 value 4 width 60px accent cyan (tooltip 'Brush size'), checkbox #drawFill (label ' Fill', 10px #888). All three are read live by drawing tools; drawFill affects rect and ellipse only (line and pen ignore). drawSize also sets eraser diameter and the eraser cursor ring. Mouse wheel over the canvas in a draw tool changes drawSize by 1 per tick (down = smaller), clamped 1..50, and syncs the slider.
rows.quirks: Native Chromium color dialog is a system/HTML popup the port must replace; hex values are lowercase '#rrggbb' only (no alpha), so a color picker without alpha is correct.
rows.portTarget: Custom color button (WPF has no built-in color picker; build a popup with HSV square + hex box + RGB, plus an eyedropper is NOT needed unless desired), Slider 1..50 SmallChange 1, CheckBox. Style Slider with accent cyan track/thumb.
rows.parityCheck: LedgerScenarioTests: Fill checked with Rect draws a filled rectangle in the brush color; wheel-down at 4 gives 3 (BrushViewModelTests); CanvasCursorsTests: size 50 gives a ring of radius 25 x zoom DIPs. Narrowed in M3b: view-model and cursor evidence, not UI automation (M6).

rows.name: Placement buttons: Fit Front, F+B, Stretch, Allover, Scatter
rows.behavior: Five buttons in two rows. All require a selected layer (silent no-op otherwise, no message). Fit Front 'Fit to front torso': saveUndo; scale = min(128/imgW,128/imgH)*0.9 centered in torso_front, rotation 0. F+B 'Front + Back': same as Fit Front then pushes a clone at torso_back, name + ' (back)'; original stays selected; clone appended on top (no selection change). Stretch 'Stretch across torso': image fitted into 260x128 box at (165,74) (covers right+front+left torso faces) without the 0.9 factor, rotation 0, plus a back clone at full-fit (no 0.9) named ' (back)'. Allover 'Tile allover': one clone per region (18) at 0.8 fit, rotation 0, name + ' tile'. Scatter 'Scatter randomly': for each region 3 clones if region width>100 else 1 (shirt: 4 wide regions*3 + 14*1 = 26 clones), scale (rand*0.3+0.15)*min(w,h)/max(imgW,imgH) min 0.02, x=r.x+rand*(0.7w), y=r.y+rand*(0.7h), rotation rand*60-30, name + ' scat'. Clones copy all adjustment props and share the same Image object.
rows.quirks: Scatter is unseeded. Stretch's back clone keeps the pre-Stretch flips/adjustments. In Pants mode F+B and Stretch throw (see bug-pants-mode-region-keys). Allover/Scatter iterate all current-mode regions so they work in Pants.
rows.portTarget: VM commands operating on the selected Layer record; use the same constants (0.9, 0.8, 260x128 at 165,74, 0.85 etc.). Scatter uses System.Random; allow a test seed injection.
rows.parityCheck: Reworded in M4b to the evidence: PlacementTests check each command's x, y, scale and rotation against 4.1's formulas for 200x100, 300x200, 512x512, 33x77, 40x30, 40x90 and 300x100 layers in Shirt and Pants, and Scatter's counts (26 in Shirt mode) and ranges with a seeded rng in 4.1's draw order; PlacementGroupTests run every command as one undo step through the view model and the composed shell, with the group collapsed until a layer is selected (M4b smoke P1).
rows.divergence: 4.1: F+B and Stretch throw in Pants mode and the Placement group shows with no layer selected. v5: Pants works via semantic slots and the Placement group is hidden until a layer is selected.

rows.name: Edit group: Undo, Redo, Clear
rows.behavior: Undo (tooltip 'Undo (Ctrl+Z)') and Redo (tooltip 'Redo (Ctrl+Y / Ctrl+Shift+Z)') are .btn-secondary; both disabled (opacity .4, default cursor) when their stack is empty, evaluated after each saveUndo/undo/redo (updateHistoryButtons). Both start disabled. Clear has no tooltip: saveUndo, deletes ALL layers and deselects; it does not clear region fills, background or the mode. No confirmation. History depth 30 (createHistory(30)); a fresh edit empties redo. Undo/redo restore whole state (see cross-cutting).
rows.quirks: Many edits do NOT push undo (see cross-cutting list). Clear leaves region fills, so 'Clear' does not blank a filled template.
rows.portTarget: RelayCommands with CanExecute from history stacks; limit 30; snapshots as immutable records (not JSON strings of base64 PNGs; share image buffers by reference to cut memory) while preserving semantics.
rows.parityCheck: The history sequence of tests/history.test.js runs in C# (HistoryTests, M2a). Through the Edit group: Undo and Redo start disabled, after 31 edits only 30 undos are available, and a new edit empties redo (EditGroupTests, LedgerScenarioTests). Narrowed in M3a: the disabled look (opacity .4) is checked on cross-undo-disabled-style.
