rows.behavior: PNG: (#exportTitle value || 'roblox_shirt') with every char outside [a-zA-Z0-9_-] replaced by '_' (each char individually, so 'My Shirt!' -> 'My_Shirt_', non-ASCII letters become '_'), then '_roblox.png' appended. Project: (title || 'untitled') sanitized the same way + '.r15proj'. Pants mode uses the same '_roblox.png' suffix. Input placeholder 'Template name...', width 140px.
rows.quirks: Emoji yields '__'; whitespace-only title is truthy so yields '___' not the default. Keep for parity, but a trim() before the default test would be a harmless fix.
rows.portTarget: Static helper Sanitize(string) using Regex.Replace(title, "[^a-zA-Z0-9_-]", "_") on UTF-16 code units (JS replaces per code unit: an emoji, being a surrogate pair, yields TWO underscores; .NET Regex on string behaves the same per char, but verify). Unit-test table of inputs.
rows.parityCheck: Table test: '', 'a b', 'ÅÄÖ', '😀', 'a/b\\c', 'CON' -> expected strings identical to JS. Document that 'CON','NUL' etc. pass through and SaveFileDialog may reject.

rows.name: Blank-export guard confirm()
rows.behavior: If there are no visible layers with images, no region fills and no background image, exportPNG shows confirm('The template is empty — download a blank PNG anyway?'); Cancel aborts. A background COLOR alone does not count as art (so a bare navy background still triggers the prompt).
rows.quirks: Electron confirm() dialog has no title text (shows app title); WPF MessageBox should use product title.
rows.portTarget: MessageBox.Show(owner, text, title, OKCancel, Question). Same exact text. Condition: layers.Any(l=>l.Visible && l.Image!=null) || regionColors.Count>0 || bgImage!=null.
rows.parityCheck: Fresh document, Download: the confirm appears; Cancel: no save dialog; OK: the save dialog. A background color alone, and hidden-only layers, still prompt (FileGroupTests, LedgerScenarioTests). Narrowed in M3a: the background color is set on the document; the Layout tab's swatches land with M4.

rows.name: All user-facing alert() prompts (exact strings)
rows.behavior: Five alert() sites: eraser with no layer ('Select a layer to erase from, then try again.'), built-in pack not found ('Built-in pack "<name>" not found. Reinstall the app to restore it.'), pack empty ('Built-in pack "<name>" is empty.'), folder with no images ('No images found in that folder. Pick a folder with PNG, JPG, GIF, or WEBP files.'), project load failure ('Failed to load project. <err.message>'). Plus one confirm (blank export). No toasts, no status bar messaging beyond Keys/asset counts.
rows.quirks: loadProject mutates state (switchMode, bgColor, regionColors) BEFORE layers parse, so a JSON that parses but fails halfway leaves a half-loaded document (and layers are cleared only after). Port should parse fully first, then apply atomically; document as a deliberate fix.
rows.portTarget: Central IDialogService.ShowMessage(text) -> MessageBox with product title and OK button; keep strings verbatim (they are also the smoke-test assertions). The JS err.message in 'Failed to load project' will differ (JSON parse messages); define native messages.
rows.parityCheck: Trigger each of the 6 conditions; compare text. For load failure feed a non-JSON file and a truncated JSON; both must show 'Failed to load project.' prefix and leave the current document untouched or defined.
rows.divergence: 4.1: loadProject mutates mode, background and fills before layers parse, leaving a half-loaded document on failure. v5: parse and validate fully first, then apply atomically, leaving the current document untouched on failure.

rows.name: Asset library folder picker semantics
rows.behavior: 'Load folder' uses <input type=file webkitdirectory> and enumerates recursively in the chromium file list. Filter /\.(png|jpg|jpeg|gif|webp)$/i by name. Dedup by filename keeping the DEEPEST path (greater webkitRelativePath depth wins; ties keep the first). Group by immediate parent folder name; files directly in the picked root are '(root)'; a '(all)' group always added. Empty result alerts the no-images message. The input value is cleared before click so choosing the same folder twice re-fires change.
rows.quirks: Dedup keeps deepest 'most processed' copy by design. Order within a group is the browser's enumeration order (OS-dependent); port should sort deterministically, call out as a minor difference. A name collision across different subfolders loses one image silently.
rows.portTarget: Microsoft.Win32.OpenFolderDialog (.NET 8+) then Directory.EnumerateFiles(recursive). Reproduce depth-based dedup and parent-folder grouping exactly; remember webkitRelativePath includes the picked folder name as segment 0. Thumbnails load lazily; decode with SKCodec/WIC for gif/webp (webp needs SkiaSharp codecs; gif first frame).
rows.parityCheck: Fixture folder tree with duplicates at depths 1,2,3 and mixed extensions in upper/lower case: assert chosen file per name, group names, counts shown in 'N images in <folder>' and '(all)'.
rows.divergence: 4.1: folder enumeration order is browser/OS-dependent. v5: deterministic sorted order, with the deepest-path dedup, parent-folder grouping and counts kept.

rows.name: Accepted image inputs (drop, Add image, Background, folder)
rows.behavior: File inputs use accept=image/* (add image, background, hidden fileInput) and the folder path whitelists png/jpg/jpeg/gif/webp. Project picker accepts .json and .r15proj. Browser decoders also open BMP, ICO, SVG, AVIF via image/*, since Chromium can decode them.
rows.quirks: accept=image/* silently allows SVG/AVIF in Electron; the port may drop them. Animated GIF/WEBP: Chromium draws first frame only to canvas; keep first-frame behavior.
rows.portTarget: Decide the supported set: SkiaSharp decodes png/jpg/gif/webp/bmp/ico natively; svg and avif need extra libs. Match the list in README (PNG/JPG/GIF/WEBP) and make the picker filter explicit.
rows.parityCheck: Reworded in M4b to the evidence: Add image, the drop zone and Background share one decoder, ImageImporter.Load (ImportService and BackgroundViewModel). ImageImporterTests: PNG, JPG, WebP, BMP and GIF decode to their pixel size, an animated GIF takes its first frame, SVG is refused with 'SVG images can't be added. Use PNG, JPEG, WebP, BMP or GIF.' and other extensions are named as unsupported; BackgroundGroupTests run the same matrix and the SVG message through the Background route; DialogInventoryTests and the M4a bridge (F4) show a failed Add image naming the file in the status strip with no dialog.
rows.divergence: 4.1: accept=image/* silently lets SVG/AVIF through the picker. v5: explicit PNG/JPG/GIF/WEBP/BMP filter, SVG import dropped with a message, first frame only for animated files. The folder picker lists the import formats, .bmp included, while its no-images alert keeps 4.1's text naming PNG, JPG, GIF and WEBP, and a .bmp keeps its extension in the thumbnail caption, whose regex is 4.1's (M4a, interfaces R14, T2-R6).

rows.name: Built-in Drips and Word art pack loading
rows.behavior: Buttons #btnPackDrips / #btnPackWordArt call loadBuiltInPack(name). Resolve dir: <__dirname>/packs/<name> if it exists else <process.resourcesPath>/packs/<name>; missing -> alert. Reads every .png/.jpg/.jpeg/.gif/.webp in directory order, builds File objects (type forced image/png) with a fake webkitRelativePath 'packs/<name>/<file>', sets groups {'(all)', <name>}, clears sub-folder buttons, shows the browser panel, caption 'N images in built-in <name> pack', then showAssetFolder('(all)').
rows.quirks: Caption uses the raw folder key so Word art reads 'word_art pack'. TEST_PLAN wording ('built-in drips pack', '25 word-art PNGs') matches. Enumeration order in Node on NTFS is alphabetical, so sort ordinal-ignore-case to match.
rows.portTarget: Ship packs as content files in the MSIX (Content, CopyToOutputDirectory) under <AppContext.BaseDirectory>/packs/{drips,word_art}. Enumerate with Directory.EnumerateFiles sorted by name. Keep the same two buttons and caption format.
rows.parityCheck: Click Drips -> caption '156 images in built-in drips pack'; click Word art -> '25 images in built-in word_art pack' (note the folder token is the folder name word_art, not 'word art'). Thumbnail count in grid equals caption.

rows.name: Pack inventory that must ship byte-identical
rows.behavior: packs/drips: 156 PNGs = 12 colors (blood, blue, cyan, gold, green, magenta, neon_green, orange, pink, purple, red, white) x 13 shapes (front v1/v2/flipped, sleeve v1/v2/flipped, wide v1/v2/flipped, pants_leg v1/v2, pants_wide v1/v2). packs/word_art: 25 PNGs (word_<slang>_<fontkey>.png). Total 1.6 MB. The 'drip_*_pants_*' subset is 48 files. Pack names are shown only through file names (layer name = filename without extension).
rows.quirks: TEST_PLAN/manifest/CHANGELOG all hardcode 156/25; any pack change requires updating those docs. drips are named for front/sleeve/wide but nothing in code filters by shirt vs pants mode (verify in editor slice).
rows.portTarget: Copy folders unchanged into the app package; add a manifest test that counts 156 and 25 and hashes each file. Licensing note in packs/README.md: only bundle assets Este owns.
rows.parityCheck: SHA-256 manifest of every pack file equals the repo's; count assertions 156/25 at startup in a test.

rows.name: 15 Word Art fonts load from Google Fonts at runtime (offline users get fallbacks)
rows.behavior: editor.html links one fonts.googleapis.com css2 URL (display=swap) for Anton, Bebas Neue, Dancing Script 700, Great Vibes, Pacifico, Creepster, Poppins 700;900, Lato 900, Bangers, Permanent Marker, Bungee Shade, Rubik Mono One, Press Start 2P, Righteous, Orbitron 700;900, plus preconnects. The word art preview refreshes once on document.fonts.ready (fallback setTimeout 1000ms if document.fonts is missing). Offline or blocked: silently falls back to a system font, no error. Pre-rendered word_art pack PNGs were produced from these fonts. This is the ONLY network traffic and the only reason for the privacy/network claims.
rows.quirks: Skia text vs Chromium text shaping/hinting will not be pixel-exact; the parity check for word art must be tolerance or perceptual, unlike fills. The family 'Poppins 700;900' etc. means weight naming must map to the right TTF files. Updating PRIVACY/SECURITY/TEST_PLAN/reviewer letter is part of the port.
rows.portTarget: Bundle all 15 families as .ttf (OFL-licensed; keep licenses) as Resource/Content fonts and reference via FontFamily('pack://application:,,,/Fonts/#Anton') or load SKTypeface.FromFile for rendering to SkiaSharp. Include the exact weights (Dancing Script 700, Poppins 700+900, Lato 900, Orbitron 700+900). Zero network access afterwards.
rows.parityCheck: Render the string 'RIZZ' in each of the 15 fonts x 6 styles with the native renderer and diff against a reference rendered by Electron with fonts installed locally; allow font-rasterizer tolerance. Network monitor: zero outbound connections. Narrowed in M4b, accepted by Este on 2026-10-25: the 15 fonts are frozen in Solid only (GoldenWordArtFontTests, W1), and the five other styles have goldens in Anton, Poppins and Dancing Script only, so 15 fonts x 6 styles is not shown. Zero outbound connections is proven by the M4b smoke cold start (no socket owned by the process over 6 launches), and the faces are vendored (WordArtHardeningTests.Every_font_renders_RIZZ_in_its_vendored_face_with_no_fallback).
rows.divergence: 4.1: 15 Word Art fonts load from Google Fonts at runtime and fall back offline. v5: fonts bundled with the app and zero network requests.

rows.name: electron-builder config: appId, files allowlist, NSIS
rows.behavior: appId com.626labs.rbx15maker; productName 'RBX15 Classic Shirt and Pants Maker'; version 4.1.0; build.files allowlist = main.js, editor.html, editor.js, styles.css, lib/**, package.json (no packs, no docs, no tests, no shirt_editor.html, no python). win.target nsis; nsis: oneClick false, allowToChangeInstallationDirectory true, createDesktopShortcut true, createStartMenuShortcut true. Defaults implied: per-user install under %LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\<productName>, assisted wizard, uninstaller in Apps & features, artifact 'RBX15 Classic Shirt and Pants Maker Setup 4.1.0.exe'. Scripts: start, build (electron-builder --win --publish never), lint, test.
rows.quirks: The shipped GitHub artifact name contains spaces and the version. release workflow hardcodes that exact name. No electron-builder icon, so default Electron icon (see shell-window-no-icon).
rows.portTarget: MSIX is the primary channel. Decide whether the GitHub-Releases channel keeps a non-Store installer: either keep an NSIS/Inno/WiX setup for the self-contained publish output (needs per-user, optional dir, shortcuts, uninstaller parity) or drop it and distribute only the .msix/.msixbundle (sideloading needs a cert; SmartScreen story in SIGNING.md). Track as an explicit product decision.
rows.parityCheck: If an installer is kept: clean VM install -> shortcuts exist (desktop + Start), dir picker defaults to %LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\<name>, appears in Apps & features, uninstall removes shortcuts and dir. If dropped: README/index.html/RELEASE_NOTES no longer promise a Setup.exe.
rows.divergence: 4.1: electron-builder config with NSIS target. v5: deleted at cutover, NSIS retired in favor of Store MSIX plus portable zip.

rows.name: extraResources copies packs/**/*.png to resources/packs
rows.behavior: from packs to packs, filter **/*.png. So README.md is excluded; non-PNG files in packs (jpg etc.) would not ship even though the loader accepts jpg/gif/webp. Resolved at runtime via process.resourcesPath.
rows.quirks: Filter excludes non-PNG silently; harmless today.
rows.portTarget: csproj <Content Include="packs\**\*.png" CopyToOutputDirectory=PreserveNewest> or MSIX layout files; include only PNG.
rows.parityCheck: Inspect the built package file list: 181 pack PNGs, no README.
rows.divergence: 4.1: electron-builder extraResources copies packs to resources/packs. v5: deleted with electron-builder, packs ship as app content in the MSIX and zip.

rows.name: CI uses npm install because package-lock has stale 'conundrum-r15-designer' identity
rows.behavior: Both CI workflows run `npm install` (not npm ci) with comments saying the lockfile still has the v1 identity. node_modules present locally; electron ^41.1.0, electron-builder ^26.8.1, @napi-rs/canvas ^1.0.2, eslint ^10.7.0, globals ^17.7.0 are all devDependencies (no runtime deps).
rows.quirks: Reproducibility gap exists today; not a user-visible behavior.
rows.portTarget: The .NET build is NuGet with packages.lock.json / Directory.Packages.props and `dotnet restore --locked-mode`. Do not carry the unlocked-install habit over. Electron/npm devDeps go away from the shipped product but remain for the legacy app until the cutover; decide repo layout (same repo subfolder vs new).
rows.parityCheck: CI log shows restore with locked mode and identical package versions on two runs.
rows.divergence: 4.1: stale npm package-lock with CI using npm install. v5: package.json and npm tooling deleted at cutover.

rows.name: MSIX Identity must be preserved exactly (same Store identity)
rows.behavior: Identity Name='626LabsLLC.RBX15ClassicShirtandPantsMaker' (exact case), Publisher='CN=177BCE59-0966-4975-9962-10E36652141F' (626 Labs LLC account CN shared with Sanduhr), Version injected as MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH.0 from package.json, ProcessorArchitecture x64. PublisherDisplayName '626Labs LLC' (no space; the spaced form fails Partner Center validation). Package Family Name 626LabsLLC.RBX15ClassicShirtandPantsMaker_wz1chhb2h2v4a. Store ID 9MV9G4XFJ8S0.
rows.quirks: The Store-ingested package is re-signed; PFN suffix wz1chhb2h2v4a derives from Publisher so any CN change breaks the upgrade path. Must also ship version > 4.1.0.0; current native spike is not versioned. Runtime flip: Electron->WPF in the same PFN is allowed because architecture is x64 for both.

Version for the native release must be strictly greater than the last Store-submitted 4.1.0.0 (Store requires monotonically increasing; the 4th component is reserved by the Store for the Store, keep .0). Do NOT reserve a new app name.

rows.name: Application element: Id, Executable, EntryPoint, tiles
rows.behavior: Application Id='RBXMaker', Executable='RBX15 Classic Shirt and Pants Maker.exe' (electron-builder's productName.exe), EntryPoint Windows.FullTrustApplication. VisualElements DisplayName 'RBX15 Classic Shirt and Pants Maker', Description 'Roblox Classic R15 shirt and pants template editor', BackgroundColor #0f1f31, Square150x150Logo, Square44x44Logo; DefaultTile Wide310x150Logo, Square310x310Logo, Square71x71Logo, ShortName 'RBX15'; SplashScreen Images\SplashScreen.png with #0f1f31 background. Resources: en-US only.
rows.quirks: 4.0.0 was REJECTED by Partner Center for a tile filename mismatch (SmallTile.png/LargeTile.png vs Square71x71Logo.png/Square310x310Logo.png), fixed in 4.0.1; the make-msix flow uses /nv which skips semantic validation, so image-name errors are only caught at upload. Add a validation step that checks every manifest-referenced file exists.

Add scale variants (scale-125/150/200/400) for crisp tiles since Images only has base sizes. M6a: Application Id RBXMaker kept; Executable is RBX15.App.exe (AssemblyName unchanged, the PE name is the only visible effect); visual elements unchanged; tile scale variants not added.
rows.parityCheck: Install the native package: Start tile label 'RBX15', tile and splash match images; pinned tile from the Electron install keeps working after upgrade.

rows.name: Capabilities: only runFullTrust; justification text; network capability gap
rows.behavior: Only <rescap:Capability Name='runFullTrust'/>. Justification (for Partner Center) says Electron multi-process + user-initiated folder picker need unsandboxed access. No internetClient capability although the app makes the Google Fonts requests (README roadmap flags this mismatch). No file-type associations, no protocol handlers, no startup task, no background tasks, no broadFileSystemAccess.
rows.quirks: The old justification point (1) 'Electron spawns renderer child process' no longer exists and point (2) 'folder picker every load' is weak: with a user picker the sandbox also allows access via the file picker broker. runFullTrust remains for the .NET runtime.

rows.name: make-msix.ps1 pipeline: stage, inject version, pack, optional self-sign

Output name RBX15-Maker-v4.1.0.0.msix.

rows.portTarget: Rebuilt as scripts/build-msix.ps1 (PowerShell 7 and Windows PowerShell 5.1) around `dotnet publish` of src/RBX15.App (no npm): version defaults to the csproj <Version> plus .0 and must equal it; output RBX15-Maker-v<ver>.msix plus RBX15-Maker-v<ver>-portable-win-x64.zip; -SelfSign, -SkipPublish, -OutDir; Windows SDK discovery kept; /nv dropped and every manifest-referenced file checked; SIGNING.md Path 4 corrected.
rows.parityCheck: M6a: `pwsh -File scripts/build-msix.ps1 -Version 5.0.0.0` (and the same under powershell.exe) ends with the MSIX and the zip; `makeappx unpack` shows AppxManifest.xml with Version 5.0.0.0 and every referenced image; the manifest identity and capability asserts, the pack with validation and the bridge-exclusion scan of the packaged RBX15.App.dll all run inside the script; -SelfSign signs with a cert whose subject equals the Publisher. Narrowed in M6a: installing the self-signed package is exercised by parity-store-update-path, which cannot run without trusting a cert as admin.

rows.name: fills.test.js: 14 tests that define the fill contract
rows.behavior: normalizeFill folds string/null into {type:'solid',c1}; legacy string paints solid (#f00 -> [255,0,0] at 20,20); solid descriptor; linear c1->c2 at angle 0 (left red-ish, right blue-ish); stripes on global lattice (scale 8: c2 at x0-8, c1 at 8-16); dots continuous across adjacent regions (lattice centers 8,24,40,56,72, scale 16; x=56 blue, x=48 red); checker alternates (5,5 differs from 15,5 at scale 10); dots c2 at (8,8), c1 at (0,0); camo deterministic across two renders; fill clipped to region rect (outside alpha 0); linear gradient with shared extent is continuous across seam and without extent jumps (>150 blue delta); fillKey groups equal fills and treats '#aabbcc' == {solid,'#aabbcc'}; fillToCSS returns plain color for solid, 'linear-gradient(45deg' for linear, radial-gradient for dots.

rows.name: roblox_uploader.py: Chrome cookie extraction + Roblox upload (credential-lifting code)
rows.behavior: Reads %LOCALAPPDATA%\Google\Chrome\User Data\Local State, DPAPI-decrypts the AES key (ctypes CryptUnprotectData), opens the Chrome Cookies SQLite DB read-only with nolock/immutable, selects .ROBLOSECURITY for .roblox.com, AES-GCM decrypts it (cryptography or pycryptodome), prints the cookie tail (last 20 chars), fetches x-csrf-token from auth.roblox.com/v2/logout, then POSTs multipart to apis.roblox.com/assets/user-auth/v1/assets for each upload_manifest.json item (assetType Shirt, hardcoded creator userId '1647274201', description 'Exclusive design by Conundrum by Este | 626Labs'), retries once on 403, sleeps 2s between uploads, writes upload_results.json. Not in build.files, not invoked by main.js or editor.js.
rows.quirks: Credential-stealing pattern in a public repo; flagged by the 2026-08-03 privacy sweep. Adjacent: a store-submitted package must never include it. Also a certification risk if the repo is scanned.
rows.portTarget: NOT part of the product; DO NOT PORT. The reviewer letter tells Microsoft the app 'does not connect to Roblox, does not sign in to any Roblox account'; this file contradicts the spirit if it ever ships. Founder decision already open (README). Recommendation: remove from the public repo (history rewrite not needed unless secrets are embedded; userId is the only hardcoded identity), and ensure the native repo/package never contains it.
rows.parityCheck: Native package file list contains no .py and no reference to ROBLOSECURITY, Chrome paths, or CryptUnprotectData (static scan in CI).
rows.divergence: 4.1: roblox_uploader.py with Chrome cookie extraction lives in the public repo. v5: moves to a private repo and is never packaged.

rows.name: .r15proj JSON contract (read-compat required, shell-level facts)
rows.behavior: Saved JSON (indent 2): version '4.0' (NOT bumped for 4.1 even though regionColors may now hold fill descriptor objects), app name, savedAt ISO string, mode, bgColor, bgOpacity, bgImageSrc (data URL or null), regionColors (map of region id -> color string OR descriptor object), showMask, showGrid, layers[] {id,name,visible,opacity,x,y,scale,rotation,flipH,flipV,brightness,contrast,saturate,hueRotate,rShift,gShift,bShift,imgSrc data URL}. Open picker accepts .json and .r15proj. Load defaults: bgColor '#192e44', bgOpacity 1, layer opacity 1, brightness/contrast/saturate 100, hueRotate 0, shifts 0, scale 1, visible unless false; layers sorted back by file order; nextId = max id + 1; selection = last layer; missing/unloadable images skipped (onerror increments the counter). RELEASE_NOTES: older project files (including flat region colors) open unchanged.
rows.quirks: Edge cases to decide: if every layer image fails, nextId stays; Math.max(...[]) of an empty set is -Infinity (only reachable when all layers loaded but array empty, guarded earlier); layer ids in a file that collide are not de-duplicated; undo history and selection are not saved; project does not store export title; load does not push an undo entry (verify in editor slice).
rows.portTarget: System.Text.Json DTOs tolerant of missing fields with the same defaults; decode data URLs (data:image/png;base64,...) via SKBitmap.Decode. Write the same schema; consider bumping version to '4.1' while keeping read of '4.0'. Saves must remain readable by the Electron 4.1 app (flat or descriptor) if users go back.
rows.parityCheck: Round-trip matrix: (a) fixture .r15proj saved by Electron 4.1 loads natively with same composite pixels; (b) native-saved file loads in Electron 4.1; (c) v3-era file with no adjustment fields loads with defaults; (d) file with a layer whose imgSrc is null or corrupted does not crash.
rows.divergence: 4.1: writes version '4.0' and loads unvalidated, trusting imgSrc and numeric fields. v5: reads all 4.1 files, writes version '5.0', all-or-nothing validated load, data: URLs only, visible warning naming dropped layers.

rows.name: Hidden Electron default menu still fires its accelerators (Ctrl+R reload, Ctrl+Shift+I DevTools, page zoom, F11)
rows.behavior: main.js:22 only hides the menu bar (setMenuBarVisibility(false)); it never calls Menu.setApplicationMenu(null), so Electron's default application menu stays installed and its accelerators stay live in the packaged build. The editor knowingly relies on this: editor.js:1803-1806 returns early on any Ctrl/Meta combo with the comment 'Ctrl/Cmd combos belong to the app shell (Ctrl+R reload, Ctrl+= zoom)'. User-visible effects: Ctrl+R / Ctrl+Shift+R reload the renderer and silently discard the whole unsaved document. Ctrl+Shift+I opens DevTools in the shipped build (docs/SMOKE_TEST.md:9-10 tells testers to do exactly that). Ctrl+= / Ctrl+- / Ctrl+0 zoom the whole UI, not the canvas zoom control. F11 toggles fullscreen. The exact accelerator set is Electron 41's default menu and was not enumerated in this repo, so confirm it on a running build. CHANGELOG 4.1.0 claims Ctrl+R was fixed ('no longer resets rotation'), but in practice Ctrl+R now reloads the app.
rows.quirks: Data-loss quirk: Ctrl+R reloads with no confirm. The SMOKE_TEST instruction to open DevTools with Ctrl+Shift+I has to be rewritten for the native build (a log pane or nothing).
rows.portTarget: WPF has no implicit app menu. Decide each one explicitly in a KeyBinding table: drop Ctrl+R reload (a deliberate fix, since it loses data), drop or debug-gate DevTools, optionally map F11 to a WindowState/WindowStyle fullscreen toggle, and do not add whole-UI zoom unless chosen (use LayoutTransform if it is).
rows.parityCheck: Press Ctrl+R, Ctrl+Shift+I, Ctrl+=, Ctrl+-, Ctrl+0 and F11 in the Electron build and in the native build with a document open. Record each outcome and confirm the native build matches the decision table, in particular that no key silently discards work.
rows.divergence: 4.1: hidden default Electron menu leaves Ctrl+R reload (no confirm), DevTools and page-zoom accelerators live. v5: no such accelerators exist in WPF, Ctrl+R unbound.

rows.name: No unsaved-work prompt on close or reload
rows.behavior: There is no beforeunload / onbeforeunload handler anywhere (grep of editor.js finds none) and no 'close' handler in main.js. Closing the window (X, Alt+F4), a renderer reload, or quitting discards every layer, fill and undo step with no warning. Nothing is persisted between runs (see shell-no-persistence).
rows.quirks: A candidate deliberate fix. If added, the prompt must not appear on a pristine launch or straight after a save.
rows.portTarget: Window.Closing handler. Either keep parity (no prompt) or deliberately add a dirty flag that is set whenever history.push runs and cleared on Save work, plus a Save/Discard/Cancel MessageBox.
rows.parityCheck: Make an edit and close the window. Electron closes immediately. The native build should match, or show the documented prompt if the fix is taken.
rows.divergence: 4.1: closing or reloading silently discards all work. v5: save-changes prompt on close plus 60s autosave and crash recovery, not shown on a pristine or just-saved document. The prompt (Save, Don't save, Cancel, in the Windows wording) and the window title's * marker ship in M4a, ahead of M5's autosave and recovery (Este, 2026-10-16); the prompt also guards Open, and undoing back to the saved state reads clean.

rows.name: Electron writes a hidden per-user profile folder despite the 'no hidden data' claim
rows.behavior: PRIVACY.md says the app has no persistent settings and that after uninstall 'There is no hidden data to wipe'. By default Electron creates a userData directory under %APPDATA% named after productName (package.json:3) holding HTTP Cache (where the Google Fonts responses land, as PRIVACY.md itself admits), Code Cache, GPUCache, Local State and Preferences. The NSIS config (package.json nsis block) does not set deleteAppDataOnUninstall, so the folder survives uninstall. This is Electron's default behavior, not app code; confirm it on a real install.
codeRefs: docs/PRIVACY.md (What data the app touches; How you remove your data)
rows.quirks: The existing claim is false for the Electron build. The port fixes it for free, but only if it does not introduce a settings file without updating PRIVACY.md.
rows.portTarget: The native WPF app should write nothing outside user-chosen files. With bundled fonts there is no HTTP cache. Under MSIX, any ApplicationData use is removed on uninstall. Update PRIVACY.md to state this, which makes the claim true.
rows.parityCheck: After running the native build, %APPDATA% and %LOCALAPPDATA% contain no app folder (or only the MSIX package's LocalState, which is removed on uninstall). Record the Electron leftover folder as the 'before' state.
rows.divergence: 4.1: Electron creates a hidden %APPDATA% userData folder with cache while PRIVACY says no hidden data. v5: only window state, recents and autosave are stored locally and PRIVACY discloses them.

rows.name: .r15proj load does no sanitization; image fields accept any URL
rows.behavior: SECURITY.md (Out of scope paragraph) claims 'we sanitize on load'. In fact loadProject runs JSON.parse and assigns project.bgImageSrc (editor.js:2606-2609) and each layer's d.imgSrc (editor.js:2673) straight to Image.src. A crafted project can therefore point those fields at http(s):// URLs (network fetches, a tracking beacon, which contradicts the 'one network request' privacy claim) or at file:// paths (local file reads displayed on the canvas, which then re-save as data). project.mode is passed to switchMode unvalidated (editor.js:2599): any value other than 'Pants' renders Shirt regions while currentMode keeps the raw string, so the toggle then flips oddly. regionColors is taken verbatim (editor.js:2615).
codeRefs: SECURITY.md (Out of scope: 'we sanitize on load')
rows.quirks: The claim is false today. The port should make it true (a deliberate fix). Real saved projects only ever contain data: URLs because every image enters through FileReader, toDataURL or the pack Blob path (editor.js:539, 943, 979, 1007, 1282, 1864, 2290, 2507, 2536, 2703), so tightening the rule breaks no legitimate file.
rows.portTarget: Use System.Text.Json DTOs. Accept only 'data:image/(png|jpeg|gif|webp);base64,' for imgSrc/bgImageSrc, decode with Convert.FromBase64String into SKBitmap.Decode, and skip (count as failed) anything else. Accept mode in {'Shirt','Pants'} only and default to Shirt. Run regionColors through fills normalize and drop unknown types.
rows.parityCheck: ProjectIOTests (M2b): http and file image URLs and undecodable payloads are dropped and named, a background that is not a data: URL refuses the file, an unknown mode refuses it, and junk regionColors are skipped; LedgerScenarioTests: an http imgSrc layer is named in the status strip after Open; GoldenAppTests project-* scenes render the 4.1 fixtures against 4.1's goldens. Narrowed in M4a: no file or network read is possible because only data: URLs are decoded, from memory, and the app references no network API (Step 13's grep); a project file over 512 MiB is refused before it is read (ProjectFileServiceTests.A_file_over_the_size_limit_alerts_and_changes_nothing); no Process Monitor trace is taken.
rows.divergence: 4.1: .r15proj load assigns any URL (http, file) from imgSrc/bgImageSrc/mode/regionColors without sanitizing. v5: all-or-nothing validated load accepts data: image URLs only, validates mode, with a visible warning naming dropped layers.

rows.name: Opening a project whose layers all lack imgSrc leaves stale UI
rows.behavior: In loadProject, a layer without imgSrc does 'loaded++; return;' (editor.js:2632) without checking completion. The only completion paths are inside img.onload and img.onerror (editor.js:2655-2668). If every entry lacks imgSrc, updateUI() and render() never run, so layers=[] internally while the layer list still shows the previous document. Also, after load nextId = Math.max(...ids)+1 (editor.js:2662), and no undo snapshot is pushed nor is history cleared, so Undo after Open restores whatever was snapshotted before the open.
rows.quirks: The stale-UI case is a bug and should be fixed. Undo crossing a project open is surprising and should probably be fixed by clearing history on load.
rows.portTarget: A synchronous decode loop in C# (SKBitmap.Decode per layer), then one Refresh. Decide on undo-after-open: clear history (recommended) or push a snapshot.
rows.parityCheck: ProjectIOTests.A_layer_without_an_image_is_dropped_and_named; LedgerScenarioTests: a project whose two layers lack imgSrc opens to an empty layer list, the canvas view model takes the opened document, the status strip names both layers, and Undo straight after Open does nothing (history cleared).
rows.divergence: 4.1: a project whose layers all lack imgSrc never finalizes and leaves stale UI, and open leaves undo history intact. v5: synchronous decode with a single finalize and history cleared on open.

rows.name: Template name is not stored in .r15proj
rows.behavior: saveProject serializes mode, bgColor, bgOpacity, bgImageSrc, regionColors, showMask, showGrid and layers (editor.js:2552-2582) but not the Settings-group template name (#exportTitle). The project filename comes from it (default 'untitled.r15proj', editor.js:2586-2587), but after reopening, the field keeps whatever was last typed in this session, so exports default to roblox_shirt_roblox.png (editor.js:1536-1537). TEST_PLAN section 11 has the tester type a name before Save, which hides this.
rows.quirks: A candidate small fix. If added, document it in the format contract.
rows.portTarget: Keep the save schema unchanged for parity, or add an optional 'title' field that older Electron builds would simply ignore (forward-compatible). Either way, reading must tolerate its absence.
rows.parityCheck: Save with name 'abc', restart, open the project, and check the template-name box: blank (parity) or 'abc' (if the fix is taken).

rows.name: Landing page claims 'full text wraps' and 'add at any size'; the code does neither
rows.behavior: docs/index.html (Word art feature card) says 'Add to canvas at any size. Full text wraps, multi-line support.' In fact there is no automatic wrapping: renderWordArt splits only on explicit newlines (editor.js:2135), so a long single line produces a very wide canvas. Add to canvas always scales the result to 85% of torso_front's fit (editor.js:2271-2276) whatever the Size value, which therefore only changes rendering resolution and stroke-to-glyph proportion, not placed size. Multi-line input (Enter in the waText textarea, editor.html:229) does work.
rows.quirks: The docs claim is false. Keep the behavior and correct the copy.
rows.portTarget: Port the actual behavior (explicit newlines only, fit 85% of the front region) using SKFont.MeasureText per line. Fix the landing copy rather than adding wrapping, unless the feature is chosen deliberately.
rows.parityCheck: Enter a 60-character single line and a 3-line text, then Add to canvas: the placed layer bounds match Electron within 1px and there is no wrapping. Repeat at Size 24 and Size 120: same placed bounds.
rows.divergence: 4.1: landing page claims Word Art wraps text and adds at any size, but only explicit newlines break lines. v5: behavior ported unchanged and the landing copy corrected to match.

rows.name: 'Fullscreen canvas' claim has no fullscreen feature behind it
rows.behavior: The store short description, long description and product features, plus the README hero, promise 'a fullscreen canvas built for the exact 585x559 template grid'. There is no fullscreen toggle in editor.js or editor.html (grep 'fullscreen' finds no hits). The only route is F11 from Electron's hidden default menu (see shell-default-menu-accelerators), and nothing documents it.
rows.quirks: The marketing claim is only true by accident in Electron.
rows.portTarget: Either add F11 (and optionally a View button) toggling WindowStyle=None + WindowState=Maximized, or reword the listing to say a large canvas that fills the window.
rows.parityCheck: Press F11 in the native build: the documented outcome happens. The listing copy and the build agree.
rows.divergence: 4.1: Store and README promise a fullscreen canvas with no fullscreen feature behind it. v5: listing and README reworded (and the Store 'native' claim corrected) to describe what the app does.

rows.name: Test docs say clicking a region opens a color picker; it paints the current Fill Style
rows.behavior: windows/TEST_PLAN.md section 13 ('Click any template region button -> color picker -> region fills') and docs/SMOKE_TEST.md A4 ('click a region button with nothing selected, pick a color') describe a picker. In the code a region click with no selection paints regionColors[r] = {...currentFill} straight away (editor.js:1668-1674), and with a layer selected it fits that layer into the region instead (editor.js:1658-1667). No picker opens. Colors come from the Fill Style group.
rows.quirks: Stale documentation. Testers following TEST_PLAN would report a false failure.
rows.portTarget: Port the code behavior and rewrite both test docs for the native build.
rows.parityCheck: With nothing selected, click Torso Front: it fills with the current Fill Style and no dialog appears. With a layer selected: the layer fits the region (85%, rotation reset) and the fill is unchanged.
rows.divergence: 4.1: TEST_PLAN and SMOKE_TEST say a region click opens a color picker, but it paints the current Fill Style. v5: test docs rewritten for the native build to describe the real behavior.

rows.name: Network claims contradict each other and the code
rows.behavior: SECURITY.md opens with 'this app makes zero network requests' and lists Google Fonts as an exception a few lines later. PRIVACY.md and SECURITY.md say the Google Fonts request happens 'once per install' and 'stops on subsequent runs', and that it 'only loads the font files used by the word-art generator'. In reality: (a) styles.css:6 @imports the UI fonts (Space Grotesk, JetBrains Mono, Inter) from Google Fonts as well as the 15 Word Art families in editor.html:9-11. (b) The stylesheet link is requested on every launch and served from cache only as Google's cache headers allow, so the request is not limited to the first launch. (c) A crafted .r15proj can trigger arbitrary fetches (see project-load-untrusted-src). TEST_PLAN section 14 expects exactly two hosts.
rows.quirks: The docs understate the font surface (UI fonts are missing from the disclosure). The port makes 'zero requests' true for the first time.
rows.portTarget: Bundle all 18 font families (15 Word Art + 3 UI) as embedded resources with FontFamily pack URIs and SKTypeface.FromStream. The native build then makes zero requests. Rewrite PRIVACY, SECURITY, reviewer letter and TEST_PLAN section 14 to 'no network access', and keep the MSIX manifest with no internetClient.
rows.parityCheck: Run the native build with the network disabled and under Fiddler: zero outbound connections, Word Art preview glyphs pixel-match Electron rendered with fonts loaded online, and UI fonts render as Space Grotesk, Inter and JetBrains Mono.
rows.divergence: 4.1: SECURITY and PRIVACY contradict each other and the code on network and Google Fonts requests. v5: fonts bundled, zero network requests, and PRIVACY/SECURITY network claims corrected.

rows.name: Store 'Undo everything' overstates coverage
rows.behavior: The listing long description and features say 'Undo everything, redo too'. Several user edits create no undo step: arrow nudge, [ ] rotate, R reset, + - scale (editor.js:1807-1823, no saveUndo), wheel scale (editor.js:1305-1313), and the property and adjustment sliders, visibility toggle and drag-reorder (no saveUndo call sites; the full list of 23 call sites starts at editor.js:501). Meanwhile layout presets double-push (saveUndo at editor.js:1734, then the clicked placement button pushes again). See undo-coverage-gaps for the full matrix.
rows.quirks: Marketing overclaim. The preset double-push means one Undo after a preset lands on an intermediate state.
rows.portTarget: Port the coverage exactly (parity) or deliberately extend it with coalesced undo for drags, nudges and sliders. Whichever is chosen, the listing copy must not claim more than the build does.
rows.parityCheck: Scripted sequence (nudge x3, wheel, slider, Fit Front, preset Meme) then count the Undo presses needed to return to the start. The native count matches Electron's, or the documented new count.
rows.divergence: 4.1: Store claims 'Undo everything' while nudge, rotate, scale, wheel and slider edits push no undo step. v5: every document mutation is exactly one undo step, so the claim becomes true and the docs are updated.

rows.name: CHANGELOG 3.0 'per-mode region data' is false: a mode switch wipes fills
rows.behavior: CHANGELOG [3.0] lists 'Shirt / Pants mode toggle with per-mode region data'. switchMode sets regionColors = {} on every switch (editor.js:1710-1711). Fills are not kept per mode. They come back only through Undo (snapshot at editor.js:1723) or a project load.
rows.quirks: Historic claim mismatch. Decide whether per-mode memory is wanted.
rows.portTarget: Keep the wipe for parity (undo makes it recoverable), or deliberately store per-mode fill dictionaries. Either way, the project save still holds only the active mode's fills.
rows.parityCheck: Paint 3 Shirt regions, switch to Pants then back to Shirt: the regions are empty. Undo twice: the fills return.

rows.name: Header version string is hand-typed and drifts from docs
rows.behavior: The header subtitle is static markup 'ItsjustEste | v4.1' (editor.html:17), not read from package.json version 4.1.0. The docs disagree: TEST_PLAN section 2 expects 'ItsjustEste | v4.0', the docs/index.html eyebrow says 'v4.0', and the README says v4.1.0.
rows.quirks: Doc drift. Fix the TEST_PLAN expectation when porting.
rows.portTarget: Bind the header text to the assembly version (major.minor), or to Package.Current.Id.Version under MSIX, so it cannot drift.
rows.parityCheck: ShellTests.The_app_version_is_5_0_0 and the byline facts ('v5.0', shown 'V5.0'), LedgerScenarioTests.The_product_name_and_version_come_from_one_place; the M4b smoke's look capture shows V5.0 from assembly 5.0.0. Narrowed in M4b: no packaged build was launched; the MSIX Identity Version equals the csproj <Version> plus '.0' by construction, because scripts/build-msix.ps1 derives it from the csproj, refuses a mismatch and asserts the packaged manifest's Identity Version (M6a).
rows.divergence: 4.1: header version is hand-typed markup that drifts from docs and package version. v5: header text bound to the assembly/package version.

rows.name: Second distribution channel: unsigned NSIS installer on GitHub Releases
rows.behavior: The README Install section, the docs/index.html 'Download for Windows' button (links to /releases) and .626labs/manifest.json distribution[0] (github-releases, nsis, signed:false) all promise a Setup.exe that is a per-user install (default %LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\..., TEST_PLAN section 1), lets the user change the directory (package.json nsis.oneClick=false, allowToChangeInstallationDirectory), creates Desktop and Start Menu shortcuts, and registers an uninstaller in Apps & features (TEST_PLAN section 15). Users on this channel are not upgraded by the Store MSIX, and both installs can sit side by side.
rows.quirks: Two installs with the same display name confuse users. The README promise 'winget install rbx-maker' is roadmap only.
rows.portTarget: Decide the non-Store channel: a sideload MSIX/App Installer, a self-contained zip, or a WiX/Inno installer for the self-contained publish output. Document the migration for existing NSIS users (uninstall the old one; .r15proj files carry over).
rows.parityCheck: On a clean VM, the chosen non-Store artifact installs, creates the same shortcuts, appears in Apps & features and uninstalls cleanly. On a VM with the 4.1.0 NSIS build present, the documented migration steps leave one working app.
rows.divergence: 4.1: unsigned NSIS installer on GitHub Releases is a second channel. v5: NSIS retired in favor of the Store MSIX plus an unsigned portable zip on GitHub.

rows.name: Build-from-source and dev-mode instructions are Node/Electron-specific
rows.behavior: README (Build from source, Development mode), RELEASE_NOTES (Install) and the docs/index.html install section instruct 'npm install && npm run build' (produces dist/ with the installer), 'npm start', and 'Requires Node.js 18+ and Electron 41'. docs/SMOKE_TEST.md's automated floor is 'npm run lint && npm test', and the release-note and smoke-test test counts (31 versus 17+) do not match.
rows.quirks: Test-count inconsistency is already tracked (tests-count-claims). This item covers the instructions themselves.
rows.portTarget: Replace with 'dotnet build' / 'dotnet test' / 'dotnet publish -r win-x64 --self-contained' plus the MSIX packaging step, state the .NET 10 SDK requirement, and port the lib tests to xUnit with one stated count.
rows.parityCheck: A clean clone with only the .NET 10 SDK runs the documented commands successfully, and the documented test count equals the actual count.
rows.divergence: 4.1: README, RELEASE_NOTES and landing page give npm/Electron build and dev instructions. v5: rewritten for dotnet build, test and publish plus MSIX packaging.

rows.name: Ctrl+letter combos still toggle tools (V B L U O); Ctrl+E does not
rows.behavior: The tool switch matches e.key.toLowerCase() before any modifier check, so Ctrl+V, Ctrl+B, Ctrl+L, Ctrl+U, Ctrl+O (and the Shift forms) toggle Select, Pen, Line, Rect and Ellipse and call preventDefault. Only 'e' checks !e.ctrlKey, so Ctrl+E falls through and does nothing. Ctrl+D with no selection calls preventDefault and does nothing. Undo and redo check only ctrlKey, never metaKey. Ctrl+O toggles Ellipse; it does not open a project.
rows.quirks: Ctrl+O is the Windows convention for Open, but here it switches to Ellipse. The port should probably fix this; it's a deliberate decision either way.
rows.portTarget: Window PreviewKeyDown with Keyboard.Modifiers. Decide whether Ctrl+O should become Open project and Ctrl+S Save work (standard Windows), or keep the current mapping.
rows.parityCheck: ShortcutRouterTests.Ctrl_and_alt_letters_leave_the_tool_alone (Ctrl+V/B/L/U/O/E, with and without Shift, and Alt, leave the tool alone), Ctrl_d_duplicates_the_selection and Ctrl_d_with_nothing_selected_is_handled_and_does_nothing; ShellTests.The_window_binds_exactly_the_seven_chords_and_not_ctrl_v (Ctrl+O opens, Ctrl+S saves, Ctrl+Shift+S saves as). Narrowed in M4b: Ctrl+V's paste moves to M5's paste row; M4b proves Ctrl+V does nothing (K3; M4b smoke K2).
rows.divergence: 4.1: Ctrl+V/B/L/U/O toggle tools and swallow standard shortcuts. v5: Ctrl+letter no longer toggles tools; Ctrl+O opens, Ctrl+S saves, Ctrl+Shift+S saves as, Ctrl+V pastes. Ctrl+V paste arrives with M5's paste row; in M4b Ctrl+V does nothing and toggles no tool (M4b, K3).

rows.name: [ rotate wrap formula breaks below -180
rows.behavior: '[' sets rotation = ((rot - step + 180) % 360) - 180. JS % keeps the sign, so from -180 one press gives -185, then -190, and it keeps decreasing without bound. ']' wraps correctly from +175 to -180. The rotation slider (min -180) then clamps its displayed thumb while the layer renders at the true angle.
rows.quirks: Bug. Recommend fixing with a true modulo and logging that as a decision.
rows.portTarget: C# % has the same sign behavior. Port the formula verbatim to keep parity, or use a proper modulo to normalize into (-180,180].
rows.parityCheck: Reworded in M4b to the fixed behavior: from -180, '[' three times reads 175, 170, 165, and 80 presses stay in [-180, 180) (ShortcutRouterTests.Repeated_left_brackets_never_drift_below_minus_180, LayerKeyOpsTests.RotateStep_wraps_with_a_true_modulo); 4.1 reads -195.
rows.divergence: 4.1: '[' rotation wrap uses JS % and drifts below -180 without bound. v5: rotation wrap fixed with a true modulo, normalized to -180..180.

rows.name: Shortcuts die after clicking any slider, checkbox or color input
rows.behavior: The keydown guard returns whenever activeElement is an INPUT, SELECT or TEXTAREA, and that includes range sliders, checkboxes (Mask, Grid, Fill, Stitch) and color pickers. After a user drags the Scale slider, the arrow keys move the focused slider natively instead of nudging the layer, and V/B/etc. do nothing until the user clicks a non-focusable area such as the canvas. Mousedown on the canvas blurs the input, which restores the shortcuts.
rows.quirks: Users may have learned to click the canvas to 'wake up' shortcuts. Fixing this changes behavior, so it needs a decision.
rows.portTarget: WPF Slider/CheckBox take keyboard focus and handle arrows. Decide whether to gate on TextBox/ComboBox only (likely better) or mimic this. Use Focusable=false on canvas host plus explicit focus clearing.
rows.parityCheck: Drag the Scale slider, press ArrowLeft, and check whether the layer x or the scale changed.
rows.divergence: 4.1: shortcuts die whenever focus is on any input including sliders, checkboxes and color inputs. v5: shortcuts are suppressed only in text fields. Only text fields (every TextBoxBase), an open color picker, the layer list (Up, Down, Alt+Up and Alt+Down; Delete and Backspace on a focused row delete the layer, as in 4.1), a focused region tile (Delete, Shift+F10, Menu) and the 3D viewport (arrows, Home) keep a key that is also a shortcut; a focused slider's arrows nudge the selected layer instead of stepping the slider, and a closed ComboBox does not trap the tool letters (M4b, K1, D8, D13, D14).

rows.name: Enter/Space re-fire the last clicked button
rows.behavior: BUTTON elements aren't excluded from the shortcut guard, and Chromium activates the focused button on Enter and Space. After a click on Allover or Scatter, pressing Enter or Space repeats the action, adding layers and an undo step each time. Focus rings show only for :focus-visible.
rows.quirks: Accidental repeat of destructive actions (Clear) is possible.
rows.portTarget: WPF Buttons also activate on Space/Enter when focused. Set Focusable=false on ribbon buttons or accept the parity.
rows.parityCheck: Reworded in M4b: ShortcutRouterTests.Space_on_a_focused_scatter_button_repeats_the_click raises Space through the window's preview handlers on a focused Scatter button, on Home and on Layout, after a click: the click repeats and adds Scatter's layers as one more undo step (WPF's own ButtonBase handling); each further press takes the same path.

rows.name: Brightness/Contrast/Saturation of 0 display as 100 after reselect
rows.behavior: The panel uses `sel.brightness || 100` (and the same for contrast and saturate) for both the label and the slider value. A layer set to 0% shows 100% with the slider at 100 after any updateUI, while the render still uses 0. The next drag of that slider jumps the value. hueRotate and the RGB shifts use `|| 0`, which is harmless.
rows.quirks: Bug, fix in port.
rows.portTarget: Bind sliders directly to the layer view-model. Fixing this is recommended.
rows.parityCheck: LayerPropertiesViewModelTests and LedgerScenarioTests: brightness 0, then another selection and back: the slider reads 0 and the label '0%'. Narrowed in M3b: view-model evidence, not a screenshot.
rows.divergence: 4.1: brightness/contrast/saturation of 0 display as 100 after reselect. v5: 0 adjustments display as 0.

rows.name: Rotation label shows raw float after handle drag
rows.behavior: The rotVal label shows `${sel.rotation}°` without rounding, so after a rotate-handle drag it reads something like '37.28194618°'. The canvas overlay label uses toFixed(1). The slider oninput path shows integers.
rows.quirks: Cosmetic bug.
rows.portTarget: StringFormat on the binding. Pick toFixed(1) or the integer form deliberately.
rows.parityCheck: LayerPropertiesViewModelTests and LedgerScenarioTests: after a handle drag to 77.4 the label reads '77°', 30.4 reads '30°' and -0.4 reads '0°'. Narrowed in M3b: view-model evidence, not a screenshot.
rows.divergence: 4.1: rotation label shows a raw float after a handle drag. v5: rotation label is rounded.

rows.name: Every updateUI rebuilds the property panel and collapses Image adjustments
rows.behavior: updateUI replaces layerControls.innerHTML wholesale. #adjPanel is created with display:none, so any call to updateUI collapses the open adjustments panel: wheel-scale, rotate/resize drag (which calls it every mousemove), [ ] R + - keys, rename, Reset adjustments, region fit, layer select, undo. It also drops focus from any control in the panel. The layer list is rebuilt the same way, which recreates the thumbnails from l.img.src.
rows.quirks: Users likely find the collapse annoying, so fixing it is safe.
rows.portTarget: WPF data binding keeps the Expander state. Decide whether to persist IsExpanded (a likely fix) and note it as a behavior change.
rows.parityCheck: LayerPropertiesViewModelTests and LedgerScenarioTests: with Image adjustments open, a rename, a slider edit, Reset, a selection change and a canvas drag leave it open. Narrowed in M3b: the ']' key lands with M4's keyboard, so the same refresh is driven by the edits that reach it today.
rows.divergence: 4.1: every updateUI rebuilds the panel and collapses Image adjustments. v5: the adjustments panel stays open.

rows.name: Scale bounds differ by input path
rows.behavior: Each input path clamps scale differently. Slider: 1-500% (0.01-5). +/- keys: x1.1/x0.9 clamped to 0.01..5. Wheel: x1.05/x0.95, minimum 0.01, no maximum. Corner resize drag: minimum 0.01, no maximum. Preset fullbleed and asset right-click compute an unclamped cover scale. Above 5, the slider thumb pins at 500 while the label shows the real percentage.
rows.quirks: Inconsistent. Unify or keep.
rows.portTarget: Slider Maximum=500 with a coerce-free binding, or unify the clamps. Document the choice.
rows.parityCheck: LedgerScenarioTests and SelectionGeometryTests: wheel scaling past 500% stops at 500% and the slider reads 500 with the label '500%'; the slider, the wheel and the handles share SelectionGeometry.ClampScale (1-500%).
rows.divergence: 4.1: slider, keys, wheel, handles and presets each clamp scale differently. v5: one scale clamp of 1%-500% for slider, keys, wheel and handles, with presets computing exact fits.

rows.name: Hidden selected layer keeps box and live handles
rows.behavior: Selection overlay and handle hit-tests check only layer.img, not visible. A hidden layer that's selected (via the list or because it was selected before being hidden) still draws its dashed box, corner handles and rotation knob, and can be rotated and resized from the canvas. Its body can't be picked because the topmost scan skips !visible. The eraser also erases a hidden selected layer.
rows.quirks: Probably unintended. Decide keep vs fix.
rows.portTarget: Overlay visual in SkiaSharp. Mirror the guard or hide handles for hidden layers (decision).
rows.parityCheck: RendererOverlayTests and LedgerScenarioTests: a hidden selected layer renders exactly as with no selection (no box, handles, knob or label), and a press on its knob or corner falls through to the pick, which skips hidden layers. Narrowed in M3b: the knob drag is checked as a press that does not rotate, not as a screenshot.
rows.divergence: 4.1: a hidden selected layer still shows its box and live handles. v5: hidden layers show no handles.

rows.name: Hit-test uses the rotated bounding rect, not pixel alpha
rows.behavior: pointInRotatedRect tests the full scaled image rect, so clicking a transparent area of a top PNG (a word art or drip with lots of alpha) selects that layer over the visible art below. Flip is ignored, which is harmless because the rect is symmetric.
rows.quirks: Common user complaint class. Keep for parity unless decided otherwise.
rows.portTarget: Same inverse-rotation math in C#. Don't 'improve' to alpha hit-testing without a decision.
rows.parityCheck: Stack a small opaque layer under a large mostly-transparent one, click the visible small one, and check which layer gets selected.

rows.name: Right and middle mouse buttons act like left on canvas
rows.behavior: The canvas mousedown/move/up handlers never check e.button. Right-drag moves layers or draws strokes, and middle-click does the same. There's no contextmenu handler on the canvas, and Electron shows no default context menu, so nothing pops up.
rows.quirks: Likely unintended but harmless.
rows.portTarget: WPF MouseDown fires for all buttons. Mirror it by handling MouseDown/Up generically, or restrict to the left button (decision).
rows.parityCheck: With Draw, right and middle drags on the canvas add no layer and no undo step, and a right drag on the selected layer with Select moves nothing (bridge H4; TemplateCanvasHostTests). Narrowed in M4a: the gesture is real WPF routed input injected in-process by the test-only input bridge (brg smoke; interfaces R7, R8) and read back through its inspect command and UI Automation; the bridge cannot show the OS cursor image or drive a physical device (H4).
rows.divergence: 4.1: right and middle buttons move layers and draw like left. v5: canvas input responds to the left button only.

rows.name: Wheel uses sign only; wheel mid-shape changes live stroke width
rows.behavior: The wheel handler reads only the sign of deltaY: each event is x0.95 or x1.05 scale, or ±1 brush size. High-resolution trackpads emit many events, so scaling is very fast there. The wheel always calls preventDefault, even in Select mode with no selection. During a Line, Rect or Ellipse drag, the preview reads drawSize on every mousemove, so wheeling mid-drag changes the committed shape's width. The Pen and Eraser lineWidth is fixed at mousedown.
rows.portTarget: MouseWheel Delta sign only (Delta is a multiple of 120). Precision touchpads send smaller deltas, so normalize by sign to match.
rows.parityCheck: A mouse notch (delta 120) is one scale step, and five events of delta 8 are five steps, by sign not distance (bridge H3); three wheel notches during a Rect drag raise the brush by 3 and the Rect commits at the same size as one drawn at that width (bridge H4; CanvasInteractionTests, TemplateCanvasHostTests, LedgerScenarioTests). Narrowed in M4a: the gesture is real WPF routed input injected in-process by the test-only input bridge (brg smoke; interfaces R7, R8) and read back through its inspect command and UI Automation; the bridge cannot show the OS cursor image or drive a physical device; the small deltas are injected wheel reports of a precision touchpad's size, not a physical touchpad (H3, H4).
rows.divergence: 4.1: wheel scaling uses delta sign with asymmetric x1.05/x0.95 steps, no max clamp, and changes width mid-stroke. v5: wheel scaling centered with symmetric steps (x1.05 up, /1.05 down) under the single 1%-500% clamp. The wheel still counts one step per event by its sign, and a step mid-shape still redraws a Line, Rect or Ellipse at the new brush width (kept); Pen and Eraser keep the width of the press, as in 4.1.

rows.name: Actions that push an undo step but change nothing
rows.behavior: These push a snapshot with no visible change. Every drawing-tool mousedown, even a click that draws nothing. Eraser strokes with no selection, which also show an alert. Detail generators whose autocrop returns null. The bgColor and bgOpacity pointerdown even if the picker is cancelled. Layer list drops onto an adjacent position that keeps the order. Fill-type clicks on the already-active type when regions share the key. Presets meme, allover, mirror and scattered push two snapshots, because the preset handler calls saveUndo and then .click()s a button that calls saveUndo again. Each push also clears the redo stack.
rows.quirks: The double undo step on presets means one Ctrl+Z appears to do nothing.
rows.portTarget: Undo service in C#. Decide whether to suppress no-op pushes (recommended) and log the decision.
rows.parityCheck: Count history.sizes() after each listed action in Electron vs the port (expose a debug counter).
rows.divergence: 4.1: no-op actions and presets push empty or double undo steps. v5: every document mutation is exactly one undo step, with no empty or double steps.

rows.name: Rapid undo/redo during async restore corrupts history
rows.behavior: restoreState clears layers synchronously and reloads images asynchronously via Image.onload. A second Ctrl+Z before the loads finish calls snapshotState() on the partially-restored (often empty-layer) state and parks it on the redo stack, so a later redo restores an empty or partial state. The background image also loads async, so a render can briefly show the color background.
rows.quirks: Bug. The port should fix it.
rows.portTarget: Keep decoded SKImage objects in snapshots (or decode synchronously) so restore is atomic. That fixes this by construction.
rows.parityCheck: Script: add 5 large image layers, hold Ctrl+Z (key repeat), then Ctrl+Y fully. The port must end with all layers.
rows.divergence: 4.1: async image restore lets a rapid second undo corrupt the redo stack. v5: layers share immutable bitmaps and restore is synchronous, so it is atomic.

rows.name: Undo/redo drops selection and doesn't touch Fill Style UI
rows.behavior: restoreState always sets selectedLayerId = null, so every undo deselects. currentFill and the active fill-type button aren't in the snapshot, so after undo the Fill Style controls keep their current values even if the restored regions used other fills. The tool isn't restored. Z-order is preserved by sorting on the snapshot index, and nextId only grows.
rows.portTarget: Same semantics in the C# undo model, or improve by restoring the selection (decision).
rows.parityCheck: Select a layer, paint a region, Undo: the layer is still selected (EditorSessionTests, LedgerScenarioTests). Narrowed in M3a: the arrow nudge lands with M4's keyboard, and the Fill Style controls after an undo are checked on fillstyle-type-buttons.
rows.divergence: 4.1: every undo/redo deselects the layer. v5: selection survives undo.

rows.name: Redo stack unbounded; redo can push undo past 30
rows.behavior: push() caps undoStack at 30 by shift. redo() pushes onto undoStack without re-applying the cap, so undo depth can briefly exceed 30. redoStack has no cap at all, but it's bounded in practice by undo depth.
rows.portTarget: Port lib/history.js 1:1 including the tests in tests/history.test.js. Optionally cap on redo.
rows.parityCheck: Port history.test.js cases. Add one case: 30 pushes, 5 undos, 5 redos, 1 push, and assert the sizes.
rows.divergence: 4.1: redo is uncapped and can push undo past 30. v5: redo capped while undo depth stays 30.

rows.name: Front region button loses its purple base highlight once cleared
rows.behavior: The torso_front/waist_front button is built with inline background #2a1040 to mark it. paintRegionButton(btn, null) sets style.background = '', which removes that highlight. This happens after a right-click clear, and after undo, redo or project load for any front region without a fill, because restoreState and loadProject repaint every button. The highlight comes back only when the grid is rebuilt (mode switch).
rows.quirks: Bug, fix.
rows.portTarget: Region button style via DataTemplate with an IsFront trigger. Fix by construction.
rows.parityCheck: Paint Front, right-click it, and screenshot the region grid. Narrowed (M3b close-out, 2026-10-16): the tint return was observed after clearing Front with the Delete key, which runs the same clear command as right-click (pixels 67,51,92 -> 90,224,251 -> 67,51,92); the real mouse right-click clearing Front was observed in the 2026-10-16 computer-use smoke.
rows.divergence: 4.1: front region button loses its purple base highlight once cleared. v5: highlight is a persistent template trigger.

rows.name: Fill Style controls are one-way (never read back from regions)
rows.behavior: Clicking a painted region with no layer selected overwrites it with currentFill. There's no eyedropper or 'load this region's fill' behavior, and the controls never update from a region, a project load or an undo. The active fill-type button highlight is DOM-only state.
rows.portTarget: ViewModel with CurrentFill one-way into regions.
rows.parityCheck: Load a project with a camo region. The Fill Style controls should still show the defaults (solid, #17d4fa).

rows.name: Default layer names are off by one from the id
rows.behavior: addLayer increments nextId then names an unnamed layer 'Image ' + nextId, which is id+1. addDrawingLayer's fallback is 'Drawing ' + (nextId + 1) before makeLayer increments. In practice every caller passes a name (file basename, 'Pen drawing', 'Line drawing', etc.), so the fallbacks almost never show.
rows.portTarget: Keep the fallback strings or simplify.
rows.parityCheck: LayerOpsTests (M3a): LayerOps.DefaultName(id) is 'Image <id>'; ToolsTests and LedgerScenarioTests: drawing layers are named by Tools.DrawingName, so 4.1's 'Drawing <nextId+1>' fallback never applies.
rows.divergence: 4.1: default layer names are off by one from the layer id. v5: default layer names match the id.

rows.name: Multi-file add: z-order follows decode completion, one undo per file
rows.behavior: Dropping or picking N images reads each with its own FileReader and Image. Layers are added in onload completion order, not selection order, so small files land on top first. Each addLayer pushes its own undo snapshot, so N files take N undos. A canvas drop places every file centered on the same drop point. The last-decoded file ends up selected.
rows.quirks: The order is nondeterministic today. The port should pick a deterministic rule.
rows.portTarget: Decode in parallel but add deterministically in selection order. Consider one undo step for the batch (decision).
rows.parityCheck: Drop 3 files (1 huge, 2 tiny) and record the final layer order and undo count.
rows.divergence: 4.1: multi-file add orders layers by decode completion with one undo per file. v5: layers added in pick order as one undo step.

rows.name: Drop-zone and Background pickers ignore re-picking the same file
rows.behavior: #fileInput (drop-zone click) and #bgFileInput never reset .value, so choosing the same file again fires no change and nothing happens. #projectFileInput, #imageLoadInput and #folderInput do reset (value = ''), so they accept the same file repeatedly. bgFileInput pushes an undo step before the read, even if decoding fails.
rows.quirks: Bug that disappears in the port.
rows.portTarget: Microsoft.Win32.OpenFileDialog always returns, so the bug disappears naturally. Note it as a fix.
rows.parityCheck: DialogInventoryTests.Picking_the_same_file_again_acts_again (drop-zone click, Add image, Open, Open folder) and bridge F4. Narrowed in M4a: the Background picker is the M4b Layout tab's.
rows.divergence: 4.1: drop-zone and background pickers ignore re-picking the same file. v5: native open dialogs always return, so the bug is gone.

rows.name: Picking a background color or swatch silently discards the background image
rows.behavior: Both the swatch click and bgColor input set bgImage = null, so a background image is dropped the moment the color is touched, with no prompt. Opacity applies to whichever is active.
rows.portTarget: Same rule in BackgroundViewModel.
rows.parityCheck: Set a background image, click a swatch, and check that the image is gone and undo restores it.

rows.name: Stale asset-drag file hijacks the next OS file drop
rows.behavior: Thumbnail dragstart stores _assetDragFile and _assetDragName globally. They're cleared only when the drop lands on the canvas. If the user drags a thumbnail and releases elsewhere (layer list, drop zone, outside the window), the reference persists. The next OS file drag onto the canvas then adds the stale asset instead of the dropped file. Dropping a thumbnail on the drop zone adds nothing, because dataTransfer.files is empty.
rows.quirks: Bug, fix.
rows.portTarget: WPF DragDrop.DoDragDrop with a typed DataObject payload. Fixes this by construction.
rows.parityCheck: In-app drags carry no OS data: a thumbnail drag released over the layers list or cancelled with Esc adds nothing (bridge A1, AssetLibraryPanelTests), and by hand (MAN-1) a PNG dragged from Explorer onto the canvas right after a cancelled thumbnail drag adds the Explorer file. Narrowed in M4a: the in-app half through the bridge, the OS drop by hand.
rows.divergence: 4.1: a stale asset-drag file hijacks the next OS file drop. v5: stale asset-drag bug fixed via a typed drag payload.

rows.name: Thumbnail caption substitutes parent folder name for UUID filenames
rows.behavior: The caption is the filename without its extension. If it starts with a UUID pattern /^[0-9a-f]{8}-[0-9a-f]{4}/i and the file sits at depth >= 3, the caption shows the immediate parent folder name instead. The caption is 7px, ellipsized, on rgba(0,0,0,.7). The tooltip is the full file.name. The layer added from it always uses the filename (UUID), not the caption.
rows.quirks: Mismatch between caption and layer name.
rows.portTarget: Caption converter in the asset grid DataTemplate.
rows.parityCheck: A folder with root/x/Cool/1a2b3c4d-1111-...png shows the caption 'Cool' and the layer name is the UUID.

rows.name: Count label's dedupe/pack message is immediately overwritten
rows.behavior: The folder load sets 'N unique images (M duplicates removed)' and the pack load sets 'N images in built-in X pack', but both then call showAssetFolder('(all)'), which overwrites the label with 'N images in all folders'. The dedupe and pack messages are never visible.
rows.quirks: Dead message. Fix or drop.
rows.portTarget: Decide which text to show. Parity is the 'in all folders' / 'in <folder>' form.
rows.parityCheck: Through the bridge (A2): after a folder with duplicates loads, the label read through UI Automation is '4 unique images (3 duplicates removed)', with a PrintWindow capture (a2-folder.png); LedgerScenarioTests pin the same. Narrowed in M4a: read and captured, not compared by eye.
rows.divergence: 4.1: dedupe/pack count message is immediately overwritten by 'in all folders'. v5: the duplicate-count label is shown.

rows.name: Built-in pack load is synchronous and labels every file image/png
rows.behavior: loadBuiltInPack uses fs.readdirSync and readFileSync for every file (156 drips) on the UI thread, which freezes the UI briefly. Every file gets Blob type 'image/png' regardless of extension. Pack loads always set assetFolderMap to {(all), packName} and clear the subfolder buttons. Folders with <= 2 keys show no subfolder buttons.
rows.quirks: Thumbnail order equals readdir order. NTFS returns it sorted, so make the port's sort explicit (ordinal vs culture).
rows.portTarget: Enumerate the packs folder under the MSIX install dir (Package.Current.InstalledLocation or AppContext.BaseDirectory). Load async with SKBitmap.Decode.
rows.parityCheck: Load Drips and compare the thumbnail count (156) and order (readdir order is OS-dependent, alphabetical on NTFS).
rows.divergence: 4.1: pack load is synchronous on the UI thread in readdir order. v5: deterministic sorted packs loaded without blocking the UI. The 156 names are listed synchronously; every read and decode runs off the UI thread (M4a, interfaces R5).

rows.name: Thumbnail blob URLs created eagerly and revoked on folder switch
rows.behavior: showAssetFolder revokes the previous grid's blob: URLs, then creates one object URL per file with no lazy loading or virtualization, so every thumbnail decodes at full resolution. Layers created from assets use data: URLs via FileReader instead, so they survive revocation.
rows.portTarget: VirtualizingWrapPanel with downscaled thumbnail decode (SKBitmap.Decode with SKImageInfo sampling) for memory.
rows.parityCheck: Load a 500-image folder and compare memory and scroll responsiveness. Functional parity: all thumbnails display.
rows.divergence: 4.1: every thumbnail is decoded eagerly at full resolution. v5: thumbnails decoded lazily at thumb size.

rows.name: Project load: failed or missing images skip finalize (order, nextId, selection, render)
rows.behavior: Finalize (sort by file order, nextId = max id + 1, select the top layer, updateUI, render) runs only when the last completion is an onload. If the last completion is an onerror, it just calls updateUI and render: layers stay in decode-completion order, nextId isn't advanced (id collisions with new layers are possible), and nothing is selected. If every layer lacks imgSrc, no completion ever fires, so the old layer list UI and canvas stay stale until the next interaction. Bad layer images are dropped silently. JSON parse errors alert 'Failed to load project. <message>'.
rows.quirks: Bugs, fix. Existing user files may contain broken images.
rows.portTarget: A synchronous C# loader decodes all images, then builds the layer list atomically. Surface skipped layers to the user.
rows.parityCheck: Craft an .r15proj whose last layer has a corrupt data URL. In the port, the layer order must still match the file and new layer ids must be unique.
rows.divergence: 4.1: a failed last image skips finalize (order, nextId, selection, render). v5: all-or-nothing validated load with a visible warning naming dropped layers.

rows.name: Open project neither snapshots nor clears undo history
rows.behavior: loadProject mutates the whole state without saveUndo and without resetting history. After an Open, Ctrl+Z restores the snapshot taken before the last pre-load edit, which discards the loaded project and lands on an older session state. Redo then returns the loaded state. Mode switching inside the load calls switchMode directly, with no undo entry.
rows.quirks: Surprising behavior. Fix recommended.
rows.portTarget: Decide: clear history on open (common) or push a snapshot first. Log the decision.
rows.parityCheck: Reworded in M4a to the fixed behavior: after an edit and an Open, the history is empty, Undo is disabled and Ctrl+Z changes nothing (LedgerScenarioTests, bridge F1); 4.1's Ctrl+Z back into the pre-load session is what this row fixes.
rows.divergence: 4.1: opening a project leaves undo history so Ctrl+Z restores a pre-load session. v5: history cleared on open.

rows.name: Project load field coercions and fallbacks
rows.behavior: Layer fields are coerced on load. x||0 and y||0, and scale||1, so a stored scale of 0 becomes 1. rotation||0. name||'Layer'. visible !== false. opacity defaults to 1 only when null or undefined. brightness, contrast and saturate default to 100 and hueRotate to 0 when null. rShift, gShift and bShift ||0. flips coerced with !!. Ids are kept as stored, with no dedupe. mode is passed to switchMode unvalidated: any non-'Pants' string loads Shirt regions while currentMode holds the bad string, so the toggle then flips oddly. bgColor||'#192e44'. bgOpacity null→1. showMask and showGrid apply only if present. Extra JSON fields are ignored. version, app and savedAt are never checked.
rows.quirks: Lowercase 'pants' would load Shirt regions. Keep or normalize.
rows.portTarget: System.Text.Json DTO with the same defaulting. Validate mode in {Shirt,Pants}.
rows.parityCheck: Golden-file test: a corpus of v4 .r15proj files (including missing fields, scale 0, mode 'pants' lowercase) loads to identical layer state in both builds.
rows.divergence: 4.1: an unknown mode string is applied without validation (editor.js loadProject): switchMode loads the Shirt regions while currentMode holds the bad string. v5: an unknown mode refuses the whole file; nothing is applied. Duplicate layer ids (which 4.1 kept) are renumbered: the first holder keeps the id, later holders take fresh ids above every id in the file.

rows.name: Zoomed canvas is clipped with no scrollbars or pan
rows.behavior: .canvas-area is a flex-centered container with overflow:hidden. At zoom levels where the canvas exceeds the area (125%-300%), the canvas overflows equally on all sides and the edges are clipped and unreachable. There are no scrollbars, no pan gesture, and no Ctrl+wheel zoom; the canvas wheel always scales the layer or brush. The zoom label shows zoom*100 + '%' (25%..300% in 25% steps).
rows.quirks: Likely a long-standing UX gap. Fix recommended.
rows.portTarget: ScrollViewer around the SKElement would be an improvement. Parity would be a clipped centered Viewbox. Decision required.
rows.parityCheck: At 300% on a 1200x800 window, check whether region torso_up and the pants legs are reachable. M3a smoke S8 (2026-10-14, UI Automation ScrollPattern): at 300% on a 1200x800 window the scrollbars reached torso_up and the bottom limb faces; screenshots S08-300-scroll-*.png.
rows.divergence: 4.1: zoomed canvas is clipped with no way to pan. v5: scrollbars to pan when zoomed, zoom stays 25-300%.

rows.name: No unsaved-changes guard on close, reload or quit
rows.behavior: There's no beforeunload handler and no dirty tracking. Closing the window, and the default-menu accelerators that still work while the menu bar is hidden (Ctrl+R / F5 reload, Ctrl+W close, Ctrl+Shift+R force reload), discard all work instantly with no prompt. Ctrl+R is explicitly left to the shell by the keydown comment. Ctrl+= / Ctrl+- / Ctrl+0 change Chromium page zoom for the whole UI, and canvas mapping stays correct via getBoundingClientRect.
rows.quirks: Data-loss gap. The port can close it.
rows.portTarget: Window.Closing with a dirty flag and a 'Save work?' prompt (a new feature, decision). No reload accelerator in WPF. Page zoom has no equivalent; optional LayoutTransform UI scale.
rows.parityCheck: Through the bridge (F2): closing with edits shows the themed Save / Don't save / Cancel prompt; Cancel keeps the window and the edits, Save saves to the current file and closes, Save on an untitled document runs Save As and a cancelled Save As cancels the close, Don't save closes without writing, and a window with no edits closes at once; the same prompt guards Open (F1). LedgerScenarioTests and ShellTests pin the guard. Reworded in M4a to the new behavior (Este, 2026-10-16).

rows.name: 3D avatar preview (new in v5.1)
rows.behavior: 4.1 has no 3D view: the template is only ever seen flat, and its right-hand .rpanel (styles.css:462-469) is styled but never used.
rows.portTarget: A column right of the canvas (260 wide, 200 at the 900 DIP breakpoint, styled like the left panel) hosts a WPF Viewport3D of the six R15 boxes dressed in the live template, turning on its own and by mouse drag or Left / Right arrows (AvatarPreviewViewModel, AvatarPreviewPanel, Engine Avatar). A "3D preview" checkbox after Mask and Grid in the Settings group, on by default, collapses the column and stops the rendering; it is session state only: not in the document, no undo step, never dirty, not saved.
rows.parityCheck: Engine AvatarTests: the box geometry, the texture mapping and the body-color render per mode. App AvatarPreviewTests: the view-model follows the document, rebuilds once per idle moment, renders nothing while hidden, the 2 s spin-resume rule with a fake clock and the clamp on pitch.
