ShellPreviewTests: the column holds the AvatarPreviewPanel right of the canvas at 260 and at 200 at the breakpoint; unchecking "3D preview" collapses the column and hides the view-model, rechecking restores both; toggling it adds no undo step, leaves the Document unchanged and never dirties the session.

rows.name: R15 body in the 3D preview (new in v5.1)
rows.behavior: 4.1 has no 3D view, so no body to switch. The 3D preview (avatar-preview-3d) shows only Roblox's classic blocky body; Roblox R15 avatars cut the same template into more parts (DevForum, "Classic Clothing UV Mapping Guidelines [R15]").
rows.portTarget: A small "Classic | R15" switch in the preview panel's header picks the body (AvatarPreviewViewModel.Body, classic on every launch; session state only: not in the document, no undo step, never dirty, not saved). R15 is approximate and the note under the viewport says so: 15 parts (head, UpperTorso over LowerTorso, and per limb an upper, lower and hand or foot part) sized as their template slices at 64 px a stud, the classic silhouette in pieces, since no official stud sizes are published. The template is cut where the DevForum guideline cuts it: on every 128 px tall torso face the UpperTorso takes the top 96 rows and the LowerTorso the bottom 32; on every 128 px tall limb side the upper limb takes the top 64, the lower limb the next 48 and the hand or foot the last 16, each slice inset 0.5 px. Outer caps wear the Up and Down regions; the caps where two parts meet are undressed body-color geometry. A fixed pose (arms 6 degrees outward at the shoulder, forearm and hand 14 degrees forward at the elbow, legs 3 degrees outward at the hip) is applied as rigid rotations in Engine Avatar, so the view draws every face from its corners. The head stays the styled cylinder. Rthro and mesh bodies are still out of scope.
rows.parityCheck: Engine AvatarR15Tests: Build(mode) equals Build(mode, Classic) face for face and Classic is unchanged; R15 has exactly 15 boxes; every side face's UV is its region's V slice (torso 0-96 and 96-128, limbs 0-64, 64-112, 112-128, all inset 0.5); outer caps map to Up and Down, inner caps are undressed; dressing per mode; every box stays rigid after posing (all edges and diagonals), the posed left and right limbs are mirror images, every posed face still faces outward, and the unposed chains share their joint faces with no gap. App AvatarPreviewTests: switching Body rebuilds Boxes (15 against 6), adds no undo step and leaves the Document unchanged; the switch buttons "Classic body" and "R15 body" set the body and the note text follows; a rendered R15 shirt panel with rarm_front split at row 64 shows red on the projected upper arm and green on the lower arm and hand, and torso_front split at row 96 shows red on the UpperTorso and green on the LowerTorso.

rows.name: Image decode/read failures are console-only (silent to user)
rows.behavior: handleFiles logs 'Skipped non-image', 'Loaded: name WxH', 'Image load failed' and 'FileReader failed' to the console only. Undecodable images dropped on the canvas or drop zone vanish without feedback. The asset thumbnail click, Add image, Word Art and background image paths have no onerror at all.
rows.portTarget: Debug.WriteLine or ILogger plus optional user toast (decision).
rows.parityCheck: Through the bridge (F4): a text file renamed .png and picked through Add image adds no layer, opens no dialog and names the file in the status strip ('Couldn't add not-an-image.png: ...'). Narrowed in M4a to the import, asset, project and preview routes (DialogInventoryTests: undecodable files through Add image, the drop zone, the canvas drop and an asset click; handleFiles' three console lines; a project layer that cannot load; preview failures once per set; bridge F4); the Background image route (editor.js:940-944) is the M4b Layout tab's.
rows.divergence: 4.1: image decode and read failures are console-only and silent to the user. v5: status strip reports previously console-only failures.

rows.name: Decoder matrix: SVG, BMP, GIF, WebP accepted by extension or MIME
rows.behavior: isImageFile accepts any image/* MIME, or the extensions png, jpg, jpeg, gif, webp, bmp, svg. SVG decodes via Chromium (an SVG without width/height yields 0 or 300x150 intrinsic size, so scale math can blow up). GIF is first frame only. Folder and pack filters exclude bmp and svg (png|jpg|jpeg|gif|webp only). SkiaSharp has no SVG decoder and handles BMP, GIF, WebP, PNG, JPEG, plus ICO and HEIF depending on the platform.
rows.quirks: SVG support is a hidden dependency on Chromium.
rows.portTarget: SKCodec for raster. SVG needs Svg.Skia or must be dropped from accepted types (decision).
rows.parityCheck: Reworded in M4b to the evidence: the three routes share ImageImporter.Load; ImageImporterTests.Each_accepted_format_decodes, An_animated_gif_takes_its_first_frame, A_bmp_decodes_its_pixels and Svg_is_refused_by_extension compare pixel size and first-frame pixels, and BackgroundGroupTests.Each_accepted_format_decodes_through_the_background_route and An_svg_gives_the_message_and_no_step run the matrix through the Background route.
rows.divergence: 4.1: SVG imports via Chromium alongside raster formats. v5: SVG import dropped with a message; raster formats still decode.

rows.name: Word Art layer name has a sparkle emoji prefix
rows.behavior: The layer name is '✨ ' + first 20 chars of text + ' [' + font + ']'. It shows in the layer list and the name field, and saves into .r15proj. Rendering the emoji needs a color emoji font.
rows.quirks: substring(0,20) counts UTF-16 units and can split a surrogate pair. C# Substring behaves the same.
rows.portTarget: WPF TextBlock renders Segoe UI Emoji monochrome unless TextOptions or the Emoji.Wpf lib is used. Decide on mono vs color.
rows.parityCheck: Add Word Art 'HELLO WORLD THIS IS LONG TEXT' and compare the name string exactly (truncation at 20 UTF-16 units).

rows.name: Hidden vestigial elements: assetType select and btnExport2
rows.behavior: <select id=assetType hidden> (Shirt/Pants) is still written by switchMode but read by nothing. <button id=btnExport2 hidden> is wired to exportPNG 'for JS compat'. #canvasWrap has an id that is unused in JS. None are user-visible.
rows.portTarget: Drop. List them so nobody hunts for their behavior.
rows.parityCheck: N/A (confirm there's no visible UI in Electron).
rows.divergence: 4.1: hidden unused assetType select and btnExport2 button exist in markup. v5: not carried over.

rows.name: Layer drag ghost styling via setTimeout(0) and native drag image
rows.behavior: On dragstart, the 'dragging-layer' class is applied in setTimeout(…,0), so the native drag image is captured before the dimming. The drop indicator is top/bottom half (drag-over-top/bottom). The layer list also accepts dragover from any source (preventDefault), and dropping OS files or thumbnails there is a no-op.
rows.portTarget: WPF DragDrop with an adorner. Ghost appearance will differ, so accept a visual delta.
rows.parityCheck: Mid-drag the bridge reads the source row's drag mark and the target row's drop line (above) through its inspect command, and a PrintWindow capture records them (.superpowers/m4a-smoke/out/h7-mid-drag.png); LayersPanelDragTests pin the look: the source row at opacity .4 and a 2 px #17d4fa line on the target's top or bottom edge (styles.css:310-312). Narrowed in M4a: the dim and the line are checked as state plus a capture, not by eye (H7).

rows.name: Drawings are clipped to the 585x559 template and auto-cropped with 10px pad
rows.behavior: The stroke canvas is TW x TH, so the parts of a stroke outside the template are lost. Commit runs a full-frame getImageData alpha scan for hasContent, then autocrop scans the whole canvas again (pad 10, clamped to bounds). The drawing layer gets scale 1 at the crop origin. Eraser stroke pixels are magenta #f22f89 on the mask canvas.
rows.portTarget: SKBitmap stroke surface. Scan with Span<uint> over the pixel buffer.
rows.parityCheck: Pixel-diff the drawing layer bitmap and crop origin for a scripted stroke crossing the canvas edge.

rows.name: Imported image size caps (file bytes, side length, pixel count)
rows.behavior: 4.1 reads every dropped or picked image whole with FileReader and decodes it with an Image element (editor.js:992-1011, :2692-2707). It sets no limit of its own on file size, image dimensions or pixel count.
rows.quirks: Cap rationale: 50,000,000 pixels admits 48 MP phone photos (8000x6000); at 4 bytes per pixel a plain decode holds the bitmap and its image copy (about 400 MB), an EXIF-rotated decode peaks near 600 MB, and the premultiplied draw copy comes later. 16384 per side bounds long strips that stay under the pixel cap. The 100 MiB file cap is checked from the file length before any byte is read.
rows.portTarget: Images.Decode reads SKCodec.Info and refuses before allocating: MaxEncodedBytes 100 MiB, MaxDimension 16384 per side, MaxPixels 50,000,000. It throws ImageTooLargeException, which ProjectIO's layer decode catches alongside InvalidDataException: an over-cap layer is dropped and named in ProjectLoad.DroppedLayers, so M4's Open inherits the caps.
rows.parityCheck: ImagesCapsTests: a payload over 100 MiB, a side over 16384 and a pixel count over 50,000,000 are each refused before decode, and images at the caps decode. ImageImporterTests and LedgerScenarioTests: an over-cap file in a batch is reported on the status strip by file name while the other files import as one undo step.
rows.divergence: 4.1: imports set no limit on file size, image dimensions or pixel count. v5: an image file over 100 MiB, with a side over 16384 px, or over 50,000,000 pixels is refused before decoding, with a status message naming the file; 48 MP phone photos fit.

rows.name: View canvas rendered at device pixels
rows.behavior: The view canvas backing store is TW*zoom x TH*zoom CSS pixels (editor.js:339-341) with no devicePixelRatio handling, so above 100% display scale Chromium stretches it onto the device pixels: at 150% and zoom 1 a 585-pixel bitmap covers 877 device pixels (cross-window-dpi-rendering).
rows.portTarget: Renderer.RenderView with ViewOptions.DeviceScale set to the monitor's DPI scale; TemplateCanvasHost shows the frame 1:1 in device pixels under per-monitor DPI v2 and re-renders on DPI change. The checker half-tile is round(8 x scale) device px and the grid line is one CSS px wide.
rows.parityCheck: RendererViewTests (M3a): the frame is Renderer.ViewSize at DeviceScale 1.25, 1.5 and 2, and at DeviceScale 1 it equals the view goldens. By hand in the M4a manual list (MAN-3) at 125% or 150% display scale: template edges are crisp at zoom 1, and the export stays 585x559.
rows.divergence: 4.1: above 100% display scale the view canvas is a CSS-pixel bitmap stretched by Chromium, so the template, checker and grid look soft. v5: the view is rendered at device pixels and stays crisp at every display scale; at 100% it equals 4.1's view, and the export is unchanged.

rows.name: UI labels at CSS weight 600 in the vendored variable fonts
rows.behavior: Chromium instances the Google variable fonts at weight 600 for the header title, the ribbon tabs, the ribbon group labels and the panel headings (styles.css:142, :175, :220, :261).
rows.quirks: WPF exposes only the named instances of a variable font file. Space Grotesk lists Light, Regular, Medium and Bold; JetBrains Mono lists Thin through ExtraBold without SemiBold. Inter has a real SemiBold.
rows.portTarget: The theme asks for SemiBold; WPF resolves it to the Bold (700) instance of Space Grotesk and JetBrains Mono and to Inter SemiBold. Vendoring static 600 cuts would mean new font files and manifest rows.
rows.parityCheck: ThemeTokenTests.Ui_fonts_resolve_to_the_vendored_files pins the face each family resolves to; the header title, ribbon tabs, group labels and panel headings were compared side by side in the M3b look sign-off, signed off by Este on 2026-10-16 (.superpowers/m3b-look/SIGNOFF.txt).
rows.divergence: 4.1: Chromium instances the Google variable fonts at weight 600 for the header title, ribbon tabs, group labels and panel headings (styles.css:142, :175, :220, :261). v5: WPF exposes only the named instances of the vendored variable files, and Space Grotesk and JetBrains Mono have no 600 instance there, so those labels draw at 700. Inter's 600 is exact.

rows.name: Zoom buttons disabled at 25% and 300%
rows.behavior: 4.1's zoom buttons stay enabled at 25% and 300%; a click there clamps to a no-op (editor.js:1490-1491; zoom-controls quirks: no disabled state at limits).
rows.portTarget: CanvasViewModel.ZoomInCommand and ZoomOutCommand cannot execute at MaxZoom and MinZoom; CanvasView's ZoomButton style draws a disabled button at .btn:disabled's opacity .4. An Execute past a limit still clamps.
rows.parityCheck: CanvasViewModelTests.Each_button_is_disabled_at_its_limit_and_comes_back: each command is disabled at its limit and enabled again one step in, and an Execute at the limit still clamps. CanvasViewTests.The_host_and_the_pill_follow_the_view_model: the zoom-out button is disabled at 25%. M3a smoke S8 (2026-10-14): both buttons measured at 0.40 opacity at their limits from screenshot pixels.
rows.divergence: 4.1: the zoom buttons stay enabled at 25% and 300%, and a click there clamps to a no-op (editor.js:1490-1491). v5: each button is disabled at its limit (opacity .4, styles.css:414-416), so no button is dead.

rows.name: EXIF orientation applied when an image is decoded
rows.behavior: Chromium draws img elements with the EXIF orientation applied (image-orientation: from-image), so 4.1 shows a portrait phone photo upright and addLayer fits it by its displayed size (img.width and img.height, editor.js:503). A 4.1 project stores the original data URL (editor.js:2580), so the photo is upright again on load.
rows.quirks: A plain SKCodec decode returns the stored pixels, which for most phone photos are sideways.
rows.portTarget: Images.Decode applies SKCodec.EncodedOrigin, so the decoded image has its displayed size; import and M4's project open share the path.
rows.parityCheck: ImagesOrientationTests.Exif_orientation_is_applied_like_chromium, 8 orientations. By hand in the M3a smoke checklist: a portrait phone photo imports upright. Narrowed: the M3a smoke S5 (2026-10-14) used a synthetic JPEG (pixels stored sideways, EXIF Orientation=6) in place of a real phone photo; it imported upright and was fit by its upright size.

rows.name: A burst of wheel scaling is one undo step
rows.behavior: 4.1's wheel scales the selected layer with no undo step at all (editor.js:1305-1313; undo-coverage-gaps), so a wheel change can be undone only together with the action before it.
rows.portTarget: CanvasInteraction opens one EditorSession gesture at the first wheel scale event of a burst; EndWheelBurst closes it, called by TemplateCanvasHost's 400 ms one-shot timer after the last wheel event, and by a press, a tool change, a selection change or any other session change (EditorSession.Changing, raised first by every change entry point). The gesture records one step iff the content changed.
rows.parityCheck: LedgerScenarioTests.A_wheel_burst_scales_about_the_center_clamps_at_500_percent_and_is_one_step; CanvasInteractionTests and TemplateCanvasHostTests pin the closes (the 400 ms timer, a press, a tool change, a selection change, and an edit during the burst as its own step). Through the bridge (H3): 200 fast notches are one undo step and one Undo reverts the whole burst, and a burst of small deltas is one step. Narrowed in M4a: the gesture is real WPF routed input injected in-process by the test-only input bridge (brg smoke; interfaces R7, R8) and read back through its inspect command and UI Automation; the bridge cannot show the OS cursor image or drive a physical device (H3).
rows.divergence: 4.1: wheel scaling records no undo step. v5: each burst of wheel steps is one undo step; a burst ends 400 ms after its last wheel event, or at a press, a tool change, a selection change or any other edit, which stays its own step.

rows.name: An eraser click without movement erases nothing
rows.behavior: 4.1's eraser only moves to the press point on mousedown (editor.js:1143-1144) and strokes at mouseup only for the pen (editor.js:1253-1255), so a click without movement leaves no alpha on the stroke canvas and erases nothing, with no undo step.
rows.quirks: The approved pen dot (draw-pen-single-click) is not carried to the eraser: a click is not a destructive punch-out.
rows.portTarget: Eraser.Apply returns the layer itself for fewer than 2 points and Eraser.ApplyTo returns the same document, so EditorSession records no step; the live preview shows nothing for one point.
rows.parityCheck: EraserTests.A_press_without_movement_erases_nothing; CanvasInteractionTests.Eraser_click_without_move_changes_nothing_and_records_no_step; LedgerScenarioTests.The_eraser_refuses_without_a_selection_and_erases_only_the_selected_layer_even_when_hidden. Through the bridge (H5): an eraser click leaves the layer's image and the undo count unchanged, and a stroke replaces only the selected layer's image, as one step. Narrowed in M4a: the gesture is real WPF routed input injected in-process by the test-only input bridge (brg smoke; interfaces R7, R8) and read back through its inspect command and UI Automation; the bridge cannot show the OS cursor image or drive a physical device (H5).

rows.name: The canvas is exposed to UI Automation
rows.behavior: 4.1's <canvas id=mainCanvas> has no accessible name, role or value (editor.html:327), so a screen reader skips it and cannot tell which layer is selected.
rows.portTarget: TemplateCanvasHostAutomationPeer (FrameworkElementAutomationPeer, IValueProvider): ControlType Image, ClassName TemplateCanvasHost, Name 'Template canvas', bounds from the element, not keyboard focusable, Value = the selected layer's name or '', read-only, with a ValueProperty change event on selection change.
rows.parityCheck: CanvasAutomationPeerTests pin the control type, name, bounds, read-only value and its change event. The M3b look run reads the value through UI Automation: state 03 reads "drip_red_wide_v1" (.superpowers/m3b-look/v5/RESULTS.md).
rows.divergence: 4.1: the canvas is invisible to screen readers. v5: the canvas exposes its name, its bounds and the selected layer's name as a read-only value.

rows.name: The rotate knob's glyph antialiasing differs at some offsets
rows.behavior: 4.1 strokes the rotate knob's 1.5 px white glyph arc and arrowhead with Chromium's Skia (editor.js:403-414), at the knob offset h/2 + 30 screen px above the layer's center.
rows.quirks: Measured 2026-10-15 (M3b Task 1 ruling T1-3), 100 device positions per offset against Chromium 146: offsets 0, 10, 20, 30, 63, 67.5, 70, 80, 100, 129 and 130 screen px are exact; offsets 5 and 35 to 60 differ on up to about 14 glyph px by up to 41 levels. No construction reproduces Chromium at every offset: float rounding inside two Skia builds, not geometry.
rows.portTarget: Renderer.DrawSelectionOverlay draws the knob with 4.1's call structure, arc angles as given (ruling T1-2); the view-select goldens use offsets that measure exact.
rows.parityCheck: GoldenViewSelectTests: the six vs-select-* scenes (knob offsets 67.5, 130, 67.5, 86.25 and 75) match 4.1's view under the unchanged golden rule with the knob exact. The residual at other offsets is the measured quirk above, compared by eye in the M3b look sign-off (state 03).
rows.divergence: 4.1: Chromium 146's Skia antialiases the knob's 1.5 px white glyph. v5: SkiaSharp 4.153.1 antialiases it differently at some knob offsets (5 and 35 to 60 screen px: up to 41 levels on about 14 px); the geometry is 4.1's call for call, and the view-select goldens hold it exact at the offsets they use.

rows.name: Test-only input bridge (absent from Release and Store builds)
rows.behavior: 4.1 has no in-process test input: its UI was checked by hand and through tools/parity-ref's Electron harness, which drives the page's own DOM events.
rows.quirks: Limits (interfaces R7, R8): the OS cursor image is not observable; an OLE drag from another process, Alt+Tab and a second monitor are out of reach; a chord a control handles only on bubbling KeyDown (TextBox's own Ctrl+Z) is not reachable; the bridge pointer cannot click a WPF ButtonBase, whose ButtonState reads GetKeyState, so buttons are pressed by UI Automation Invoke (T4-R4); it raises no TextInput, so text is entered through UI Automation ValuePattern; the hardware keyboard is not neutralized, only the mouse is (T4-R17); its CaptureMouse is a real Win32 SetCapture on the app's own window; the file-dialog command lets the pipe's client, the current user, choose any path that user can write through Save (accepted by design).
rows.portTarget: src/RBX15.App/Testing/** compiles into RBX15.App only with the MSBuild property EnableTestInputBridge=true (never passed to a solution build, a Release build or Store packaging) and runs only with --test-input-bridge: a named pipe restricted to the current user with a per-launch random name, JSON commands for pointer, wheel, key, wait-idle, file-dialog and inspect, each dispatched on the UI thread into the app's own visual tree; native file dialogs are answered from a queue and settings go to a temp folder, deleted on exit (interfaces R7-R10). A publish or an MSIX build with the flag fails (RefuseTestInputBridgeOnPublish), and M6's packaging pipeline asserts EnableTestInputBridge is unset in its environment and runs BridgeExclusionTests' scan on the packaged RBX15.App.dll (critic M5).
rows.parityCheck: BridgeExclusionTests: the App assembly under test and a Release build of RBX15.App contain no RBX15.App.Testing type and neither the launch flag nor the pipe line, and a build with EnableTestInputBridge=true contains them (the positive control). BridgeSecurityTests: the pipe ACL allows only the current user (protected, network denied) and Requested needs the exact flag. InputBridgeTests: a canvas drag as one step, a release outside the window, Ctrl+S through its KeyBinding with the text-field guard, Alt+Up in the layer list, a bare key, the physical-modifier refusal and wait-idle. The controller ran brg probe, brg smoke and brg files against a flagged build (M4a Task 5).

rows.name: Each canvas layer is exposed to UI Automation and can be moved through it
rows.behavior: 4.1's <canvas id=mainCanvas> exposes nothing (editor.html:330): a screen reader or keyboard user cannot reach a layer on it, and moving one takes a mouse drag (editor.js:1056-1320).
rows.quirks: Move and Resize take template pixels, not UI Automation's screen coordinates (contract: 'in template units'); Rotate is relative, as UI Automation defines it.
rows.portTarget: TemplateCanvasHostAutomationPeer implements ISelectionProvider and has one LayerAutomationPeer per visible layer, top first, cached by id; LayerAutomationPeer is a ListItem with AutomationId Layer_<id>, ISelectionItemProvider and ITransformProvider over ICanvasLayerAutomation (LayerOps.MoveTo, ScaleAboutCenter, SetRotation), one undo step per call and none for a no-op (interfaces 3.7).
rows.parityCheck: CanvasLayerAutomationTests pin the children, SelectionItem and TransformPattern through the peers. Through UI Automation on the running app (bridge U1): each visible layer is a canvas child, top first, with AutomationId Layer_<id>; SelectionItem.Select selects it; only the selected layer can move; Move(100,120), Rotate(30) and Resize(195,100) set X/Y 100,120, rotation 30 and scale 0.5, one undo step each, and a no-op Move records none; a hidden layer is not a child.
rows.divergence: 4.1: layers on the canvas are invisible to assistive technology and move only by mouse. v5: each visible layer is a UI Automation child of the canvas (top first) that can be selected, and the selected layer takes TransformPattern Move, Resize and Rotate in template pixels, one undo step each (Este, 2026-10-16).

rows.name: Window title names the project file and marks unsaved changes
rows.behavior: 4.1's title is always the product name (main.js:8, editor.html:6); it never names the open project or shows unsaved work.
rows.portTarget: MainViewModel.Title = MainViewModel.WindowTitle(CurrentFile, IsDirty): the product name when clean and untitled, else [*]<file name or Untitled> - RBX15 Classic Shirt and Pants Maker (the Windows convention; interfaces R3). IsDirty compares the document with the last saved or opened one (R2).
rows.parityCheck: WindowTitleTests pin MainViewModel.WindowTitle. Through UI Automation (bridge F1): the title is the product name at launch, '*Untitled - RBX15 Classic Shirt and Pants Maker' after an edit, 'smoke1.r15proj - RBX15 Classic Shirt and Pants Maker' after Ctrl+S, starred again after an edit, and clean after Ctrl+Z back to the saved state (LedgerScenarioTests pin the same through the view model).
rows.divergence: 4.1: the title is always the product name. v5: it is the product name at launch, then '[*]<file> - RBX15 Classic Shirt and Pants Maker', with * while the document differs from its last save or open and 'Untitled' before the first save (interfaces R3).

rows.name: Palette from the user's art (new in v5.1)
rows.behavior: 4.1 has no palette from the user's art: a color is picked from the browser's color dialog or typed as hex, so matching the colors of an imported image or asset means eyedropping it by eye or guessing.
rows.portTarget: Engine Palette.Extract / FromDocument: each visible layer's image is sampled to at most 64 px on its long side, opaque pixels (alpha 128 or more) are binned at 4 bits per channel, and the busiest bins' average colors are taken, skipping a color within 48 (RGB distance) of one already taken and a bin under 0.5% of the counted pixels, up to 12 (lowercase #rrggbb). App ArtPalette follows the session at Background priority and recomputes only when the sequence of visible layers' images changes. The themed color picker (brush color, Fill Style colors, region swatches) shows a "From your art" row of 20x20 swatches under the hex field when the palette is not empty; a click sets the color as typing the hex would and leaves the picker open. The Brush group has a Palette button right of Fill (as tall as the Fill box, so the group keeps its height) opening a popup of the same swatches below it, or "Add an image or asset to build a palette." when there are none; a swatch sets the brush color and closes it. Session state only: not in the document, no undo step, never dirty.
rows.parityCheck: Engine PaletteTests: a solid image gives its one color, a 75/25 image gives both with the 75% first, near colors merge, transparent pixels and specks are ignored, max caps the count, no images or all-transparent give empty, the same input gives the same list, FromDocument skips hidden layers. App ArtPaletteTests: ArtPalette recomputes once for many layer changes in one turn, not for a grid toggle, region fill or layer move, and follows hiding a layer; ColorPickerViewModel.UseSwatch sets Hex and previews as typing would; the popup shows its swatch row only for a non-empty palette and a click keeps the pick open; the app's picker is fed by the one ArtPalette; the Palette button exists named "Palette" and fits the Fill row; the brush palette command sets the color and is no undo step.

rows.name: Color stops on gradient and radial fills (new in v5.1)
rows.behavior: 4.1's gradient and radial fills have exactly two colors, Color 1 and Color 2, so a three-color blend (a sunset, a metallic band) means painting regions in separate fills by hand.
rows.portTarget: Engine Fill gains Stops, an ImmutableArray of up to 3 lowercase #rrggbb middle colors (a longer list throws ArgumentException; ProjectIO refuses one as a ProjectFormatException). The colors are evenly spaced: Color 1 at 0, stop k of n at k/(n+1), Color 2 at 1; only "linear" and "radial" draw them, other types ignore them. With no stops the drawing path, every pixel and Fill.Key are 4.1's, byte for byte (the 4.1 goldens are untouched); with stops Key appends them after a second bar, so regions sharing a fill still group by key. Fill equality is structural for Stops (custom Equals and GetHashCode, since a record compares a list member by reference). ProjectIO writes "stops": [...] after scale in a region fill only when it has any, reads it when present (an array of #rgb or #rrggbb strings, a bad entry is a ProjectFormatException naming regionColors.<region>.stops[i]), and a file without it loads as before; 4.1 ignores the unknown key. App Fill Style group: for Gradient and Radial, one swatch per stop between Color 1 and Color 2 and a "+" button ("Add a color stop") after Color 2; "+" adds a stop halfway (RGB average) between the last stop, or Color 1, and Color 2, and is disabled at 3 stops; a click opens the same themed picker as Color 1 and 2 with live preview and cancel-reverts; right-click, Delete, Shift+F10 or the Menu key removes it. The other styles hide the stops and the "+" and keep the stops for the return to Gradient or Radial. Stops live in the current fill, so they follow the existing rules: session state, applyFillEdit's retarget by key, one undo step per edit that changes a region, a pick as one gesture, undo never moving the controls. Region button previews and the canvas paint through Fills and show the stops. The group's height does not change.
rows.parityCheck: Engine FillStopsTests: a red, green, blue linear at angle 0 is red, green-dominant and blue at the left, middle and right; two stops sit at thirds; a radial with one stop has the stop color at mid-radius; no stops give the two-color ramp and the same pixels, other types ignore stops; Key is 4.1's without stops and appends them with them; equality, hash and Key are structural for Stops; more than 3 stops throw; painting an equal stop fill is a no-op and retargeting follows the stops. ProjectIOTests: stops are written after scale only when present and round-trip, an empty or null array reads as none and is not written, a file without stops loads with none and the 4.1 key, a bad stops entry or a fourth stop throws ProjectFormatException naming its path. All 4.1 fills and goldens pass unchanged. App FillStopsTests: "+" adds the halfway color and disables at 3; remove drops the chosen stop; a stale swatch does nothing; a stop pick previews live, commits as one step and a cancel reverts; stops hide for Solid, Stripes, Checker, Dots and Camo and return for Gradient and Radial; painting stores the fill with its stops; add and remove retarget painted regions one step each and undo leaves the controls; a region tile swatch shows the middle color; the "+" button and swatches are named, ordered, hidden and shown as above; the Fill Style group and the Home ribbon keep their height with three stops.
